artigo.texto: CATL's Storage Battery Sales Jump 60% as Profit Trails a 58.6% Revenue Surge Published on 10/23/2026 at 05:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL closed the third quarter of 2026 with revenue of 165.22 billion yuan, up 58.6% from a year earlier — a headline number that would ordinarily settle any argument about demand. It doesn't. Net profit rose just 14.5% to 21.25 billion yuan over the same stretch, and fell 5.8% from the second quarter, leaving investors to weigh a fast-expanding top line against earnings that are not keeping pace. The storage battery business is where the volume story looks strongest. Shipments in that segment climbed roughly 60% year on year in the third quarter, and storage accounted for about 25% of CATL's total battery sales. That mix supports management's confidence in the demand outlook, though it says little about how profitably the additional units are being sold. Margin compression behind the selloff Gross margin slipped to 20.69%, down 5.1 percentage points from the year-earlier quarter and 2.46 points below the prior three months. CATL attributed the pressure to its product mix, a newly introduced consumption tax and a smaller export tax rebate. Reuters identified the profit miss and weaker margins as the main drivers of the share price reaction, alongside fierce competition in the battery market and slowing growth in Chinese car sales. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? The consumption tax, brought in just over a month ago, has become the focal point of the earnings debate. CATL is negotiating with customers over how to split the added cost and has not confirmed that any pass-through has been secured. UOB Kay Hian expects the company to push part of the tax burden onto buyers through higher battery prices and sees room for a margin recovery in the final quarter — a view built on the assumption that manufacturer and customers each absorb half the levy. A further headwind arrives on January 1, 2027, when the export tax rebate ends. A 20–30% market forecast, with caveats Management said on Tuesday that it expects the global market for power and storage batteries to grow 20–30% in 2027, citing rising vehicle electrification and larger battery capacity per car. That is a forecast for the market, not a commitment on CATL's own revenue or profit. Industry data points the same way: BloombergNEF projects newly installed global energy storage capacity will rise 45% to 188 GW in 2026, driven by solar buildout, storage mandates and subsidy programs. Protectionism is simultaneously making it harder for Chinese suppliers to access some markets and shifting supply chains, so a larger global pie does not translate automatically into unrestricted sales opportunities for CATL. The gap between the two figures — revenue up 58.58%, profit up 14.54% — is the crux of the investment case. More business is not the same as better business, and a surging top line can mask profitability that fails to keep up. None of this amounts to a profit collapse against the prior year, and the annual comparison alone does not justify ignoring the sequential decline. Both readings carry weight precisely because they tell different stories. What investors should watch next The more useful yardstick from here is not another revenue record but whether earnings growth and margins realign with the pace of the business. That is not an extra company forecast — it is the logical consequence of the latest quarter. CATL has no convincingly documented demand problem; what it has is an open question on profitability. The expected market expansion offers opportunity, but until it produces more convincing margins it remains an incomplete argument for the stock. Growth deserves recognition. It does not substitute for a vote of confidence in earning power. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 23 October Fresh CATL information released. What's the impact for investors? artigo.texto: Developers of a secretive data center in Grant County made their first public appearance in Southern New Mexico as commissioners approved a one-year moratorium on such projects Thursday. The moratorium, modeled after Socorro County’s resolution and proposed by Commissioner Nancy Stephens, passed 4-1, with Commissioner Tom Shelley as the only no vote. It comes amid a broader legislative push for a statewide pause on data center development. “If you’re driving, and you hear that there might be a danger ahead, you tap the brakes. You don’t speed up. There’s no hurry. We can pause. A year’s not that long,” Stephens said at the meeting. The moratorium bars anyone from establishing, building, expanding or operating a data center or infrastructure built primarily to serve one (such as dedicated solar, gas or battery power, water supply systems, substations and transmission lines), in unincorporated Grant County for one year. During the pause, the county plans to study whether and how to regulate them, according to the ordinance. It will be in effect from Nov. 21, 2026, to Nov. 21, 2027, unless the county decides to repeal or extend it. “This was the responsible thing to do given the huge scale of the proposed Site Layer 1 project and the fact that our county is not prepared to address the range of potential impacts from a project this size,” Allyson Siwik, executive director of the Gila Resources Information Project, said in a statement. “We need to be sure that the county is in the driver’s seat when big corporations come to town with lots of money to build a data center that could have serious consequences for our community.” Developer speaks at meeting Grant County residents learned of the data center in a legal notice in the Silver City Daily Press on Aug. 27. Upon reading about Site Layer 1 LLC’s plans to build a data center on the rural southern edge of Grant County, near Hachita and Playas, the community rapidly took action, sending letters to state Environment Secretary James Kenney and announcing their intent to introduce a data center moratorium. “Maybe they thought that they could just slide it under the radar because that’s what they did: in a one-inch ad in the back page of the press,” Commissioner Eddie Flores said. “They applied for an air permit, and somebody noticed it, and that’s why we are here today — because somebody noticed it.” The Aug. 27 notice provided scant information. It said the facility could consume about 2.3 million cubic feet of natural gas every hour. Its annual carbon emissions would be equivalent to those of about 282,600 cars. Little else has been known about Site Layer 1 LLC, which is being directed by Granite Renewables. Its leaders are brothers Ian and Blake Marcus, and its only address is an empty floor of an office tower in midtown Manhattan. At Thursday’s meeting, Blake Marcus provided more — albeit still sparse — details. He said they are planning a 715 megawatt solar and 715 megawatt storage project. It is not clear whether the project will be completely solar-powered, nor the data centers’ exact size — an Oct. 8 presentation to county commissioners said size is “fully dependent” on the result of an application to Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association. That application, required before a project with a very large electrical demand can connect to the power grid, will be submitted Wednesday, with results expected in February, Marcus said. Marcus said Site Layer 1 had “completed environmental diligence and an air permitting application” submitted to the New Mexico Environment Department — but advocacy groups and the department itself say that developers have not conducted sufficient levels of community engagement. Drew Goretzka, spokesperson for the New Mexico Environment Department, wrote in an email the department has received the developers’ application. “However, the applicant did not include any documentation of community engagement or input as the Department required,” Goretzka wrote. “The New Mexico Environment Department is unclear to what Site Layer 1, LLC’s ‘environmental diligence’ reference refers.” Granite Renewables did not respond to The New Mexican’s questions on how the moratorium would impact its timeline. Goretzka declined to comment on the implications of the moratorium. Public comments Community members of all ages gave public comment: The majority advocated for the moratorium, citing the data center’s projected health and environmental impacts and developers’ lack of transparency. “Don’t look at this venture of allowing a data center to come into your lands. Examine it. Take it apart before you make a decision,” said Cornell Torivio, the Continental Divide Trail Coalition’s regional representative. “With the amount of water that we have in the state and the continuance of developments of uranium mines and data centers, we’re not going to leave anything for our children.” The data center is set to be built on Hurt Cattle Co. Ranch, a historic, family-owned operation almost 35 miles from the U.S.-Mexico border. Located on a mix of private, federal and state land, the ranch runs parallel to the Alamo Hueco Mountains. Lawrence Hurt of Hurt Cattle Co. Ranch said he was against the moratorium, acknowledging he stands to benefit. But, he added, the county does, too. “The neat thing about the [industrial revenue bonds] is that the money goes to the county. It doesn’t go to Santa Fe,” Hurt said. He also argued the data center would benefit the community. “I have a constitutional right to use my property as I see fit,” Hurt said. “A moratorium would restrict my property right to get the most and best possible value for the property. artigo.texto: Huawei has stepped into the battery swapping track, joining hands with CATL to promote the energy replenishment for autonomous driving. From this very moment, the battery swapping track may truly take off at an unprecedented speed: The leading smart tech player Huawei and the top battery manufacturer CATL are joining forces to develop battery swapping services! The two sides have carried out cooperation before, and Huawei is not the only user of CATL's battery swapping service, but this collaboration is far from ordinary: It comes with an unprecedented technical chain, innovative and distinctive product solutions, and almost no restrictions on implementation scope... The combination of these elements is a signal that will subvert traditional business models. What exactly are Huawei and CATL going to do this time? First, let's sort out the division of responsibilities of all parties involved. The entities signing this agreement include Huawei's Zhiyuan Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., CATL, and its battery swapping business-related entity EVOGO. Generally, Zhiyuan provides intelligent vehicle solutions, CATL provides battery technology and its chocolate battery swapping system, while EVOGO participates in the construction of battery swapping networks and related operation services. The goal put forward by the three parties is to promote Huawei Qiankun cooperative models to access CATL's chocolate battery swapping network, and realize the interconnection of the vehicle end, station end and cloud end. This means that the cooperation is not just adding several battery swapping station locations to the vehicle navigation system, nor is it just equipping a single car model with a swappable battery. The three parties aim to build a set of collaborative mechanism covering from vehicle demand to station service: when the vehicle needs energy replenishment, the system can plan a suitable battery swapping station; after arriving at the station, the vehicle can connect with the battery swapping equipment; after the battery swapping is completed, the vehicle can resume its normal trip. The 99-second battery swapping index announced by CATL corresponds to the battery replacement process alone. This cannot be directly equated with the total time from when the vehicle decides to replenish energy to when it drives away from the battery swapping station, let alone conclude that the entire set of unmanned battery swapping services has been realized solely based on this single index. What is really worth analyzing is how the intelligent driving system and the battery swapping station cooperate with each other. After all, there are still many technical details to be solved between the scenario that a vehicle can complete navigation and driving on open roads and the scenario that it can accurately drive into a specific workstation and park at the exact position required by the equipment. From self-searching for stations to automatic battery swapping, how to get through the technical chain? If we split the whole process apart, the first step actually happens on the vehicle side. First, the vehicle needs to judge whether energy replenishment is needed by combining its battery status, remaining driving range and travel plan. This capability can be provided by Huawei's on-board model, on the premise that the car manufacturer grants Huawei sufficiently high underlying permissions; of course, it can also be independently developed by the car manufacturer itself. If the user chooses battery swapping, the system will also comprehensively consider the location of stations, supported vehicle models and actual availability to determine which station to go to. Next, the vehicle needs to switch from road driving mode to station operation mode, which is the core value of Huawei in this cooperation. On open roads, the assisted driving system mainly deals with road structures, traffic participants, driving routes and dynamic obstacles and other issues. But after entering the battery swapping station, the environment and tasks will change: the entrance may be narrow, the internal passages and parking spaces in the station have clear restrictions, and the vehicle must finally park at the precise position where the battery swapping equipment can work normally. This puts forward higher requirements for the vehicle's positioning, environmental perception and low-speed control performance: Navigation that brings the vehicle near the station is only the first half of the whole process; the vehicle also needs to identify the entrance, understand the internal passage route of the station, and complete the parking alignment according to the requirements of the battery swapping workstation. Of course, the current ADS 5 version can easily handle scenarios such as passing through gates and toll stations, and it can also handle narrow and complex parking spaces with great ease. The only thing to do is to collect enough scenario data of CATL's battery swapping stations to ensure 100% reliability. After the vehicle is parked stably, the battery swapping equipment takes over the work, which is the home field of CATL. CATL's standard battery swapping station is compatible with vehicles with a wheelbase ranging from 2.55 meters to 3.1 meters. Each standard battery swapping station is equipped with 14 to 30 battery compartments, with a 99.99% battery swapping success rate and a 99-second swapping duration. In actual operation, the battery swapping process for users is as convenient as refueling, but the cost is greatly reduced. After the battery swapping is completed, the whole process is not over. The vehicle needs to confirm the battery status, safely drive away from the workstation, and reconnect to the navigation and driving tasks. Only when all the links before and after are connected, can users get a continuous experience from the road to the station, and then from the station back to the road. artigo.texto: 15GWh Energy Storage, 30 Billion kWh Transactions: Huanghe Digital Energy Raises Tens of Millions of Yuan in Pre-A Round Financing, the Most Costly Link in the Energy Storage Sector Has Finally Been Separately Priced Energy Insight learned that Huanghe Digital Energy recently completed a Pre-A round of financing of tens of millions of yuan, jointly led by the North China Electric Power University Education Foundation and a leading enterprise in the energy storage industry chain. The use of funds is very clear: the engineering implementation of the vertical power industry model, the large-scale replication of energy storage asset operation capabilities, and the expansion of the R&D team. In the same period, as the only new-type market participant in the power sector, Huanghe Digital Energy was invited to join the "Education Community" jointly established by North China Electric Power University and State Grid. This seems to reflect that in the era when AI is reshaping all industries, power, as the "life source" of AI, is also in urgent need of compound talents who understand the market, power and AI. The field that this company is deeply engaged in provides a fertile test ground for universities and the power grid side. The company's model is quite unique — as an investor that holds energy storage power stations by itself, it also entrusts the operation of multiple third-party power stations. Up to now, its total accumulated operation scale has exceeded 15GWh, and the total accumulated traded electricity volume has exceeded 30 billion kWh. Objectively speaking, this financing scale is not prominent in the current energy storage track, but the direction it bets on is worth examining: when the revenue of energy storage power stations increasingly depends on who makes the "charge and discharge" decisions for them, whether the operation capability itself can be separated from specific people and specific provinces and precipitated into a set of standardized capabilities that can be delivered in batches, is becoming a key variable that determines the industry pattern. 01 Operators of energy storage power stations are becoming a variable in the asset pricing chain The asset attribute of energy storage power stations has undergone an easily overlooked change in 2026. In February 2025, Document No.136 promoted the full access of grid-connected new energy power to the market; in January 2026, Document No.114 included independent energy storage into the capacity tariff mechanism. After the rules are unified, national power assets begin to face the same set of price signals, and the decision-making power of revenue shifts from "generating more power" to "selling power at better prices". On April 28, 2026, the "Caitong Asset Management - Canadian Solar Held Real Estate Asset-backed Special Plan (Carbon Neutrality)" was established, becoming the first inter-institutional REITs with energy storage power stations as the underlying assets in China, and was listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in June. In August, the 304 million yuan energy storage REITs project of Huanghe Tianwei was accepted by the Shanghai Stock Exchange. What REITs value is predictable cash flow, and whether the cash flow of energy storage power stations can be predicted depends on operation. This is not an inference, but a question that financial institutions must answer during due diligence. However, an energy storage power station is by no means a machine that automatically generates revenue. China Post Securities has made a set of calculations based on a 100MW/200MWh system: under the assumptions of EPC at 1.6 yuan/Wh, cells at 0.5 yuan/Wh, and 260 days of operation per year, the after-tax IRR of independent energy storage in Shanxi is 5.9%, and that in Shandong is -1.8%. The source of the gap is not the battery, but the revenue structure. The revenue in Shanxi includes primary frequency regulation, contributing about 63,000 yuan per day on average; the benchmark spot price spread assumption in Shandong is only 0.4 yuan/kWh, 0.1 yuan lower than that in Shanxi, and the capacity compensation is limited. With the same set of equipment, crossing a provincial boundary, the account book is completely different. This is why operation is pushed to the forefront. Asset holders can be industrial capital, financial institutions, and local state-owned enterprises, but making a power station complete every declaration, every charge and discharge without errors in the rules of its own province is becoming a matter that requires special capabilities. The particularity of energy storage power stations is that they play two roles at the same time: they are power sources when discharging, and loads when charging. The revenue needs to be superimposed from three directions: capacity tariff, spot arbitrage and auxiliary services, and the weight of each layer varies from province to province and continues to drift — wind power and photovoltaic only need to manage the source side, while energy storage needs to put role switching, market declaration and battery boundaries into the same decision-making, which is the new energy asset with the longest decision chain among the three types. Hengyi Group entrusted Xinghe Microgrid with the full life-cycle operation of its 113.5MW/226.72MWh energy storage power station cluster, and the contract covers real-time monitoring, fault response and power trading assistance. The bid price for the operation and maintenance service of the 200MW/400MWh shared energy storage power station of Jiyang Green Energy Storage is 48 million yuan (including tax). artigo.texto: Is NIO no longer alone? Huawei teams up with CATL to launch battery swapping services: diversified energy replenishment is the trend. A few days ago, Huawei Yinwang Intelligent signed a cooperation agreement with CATL and CATL Digital Energy to jointly build an open intelligent battery swapping system. Shortly afterwards, media outlets including LatePost Auto, CLSA, and Blue Whale Auto successively disclosed that the first batch of Yinwang's battery swapping models is tentatively set to five, which are planned to be launched in 2027. The first model will be under the Yijing brand co-developed by Dongfeng and Huawei, and Qijing, the brand jointly built by GAC and Huawei, has also arranged battery swapping models. Earlier this year, BYD launched its super flash charging technology and the second-generation Blade Battery, which is claimed to "fully charge in 5 minutes, reach full capacity in 9 minutes, and only take 3 more minutes at -30°C". In April, CATL launched its third-generation Shenxing Super Charging Battery at its Super Science Day, with a peak charging rate of 15C and an equivalent 10C, which can be fully charged in 6 minutes at normal temperature. Against the backdrop that the time gap between energy replenishment via charging and battery swapping is getting smaller and smaller, and fast charging stations are becoming increasingly popular, Huawei Yinwang has chosen to join the battery swapping model, probably because it has seen the deeper value of the battery swapping model. Battery swapping is far more than just an energy replenishment solution Speaking of battery swapping, NIO is the first car brand that most people will think of. On October 19, NIO officially announced that the number of its battery swapping stations has reached 4186. During the National Day holiday this year, NIO's charging and swapping facilities provided more than 2 million services in total. For users of battery swapping models, battery swapping is not only an energy replenishment solution, but also a more convenient, stable, and even "unnoticeable" energy replenishment experience. Yinwang Intelligent follows the same logic. Huawei's Qiankun Intelligent Driving and CATL's Choco-Swap network carry out in-depth collaborative scheduling, and connect the vehicle end, station end and cloud end systems, so that the vehicle can independently determine the energy replenishment demand according to the real-time battery status and users' travel habits, realizing a full closed-loop process of independently finding stations, driving into stations, automatically aligning, completing 99-second fully automatic battery swapping, and driving away on its own. (Source: Photo by Dianchetong) In the past, under the battery swapping model, users could quickly complete energy replenishment without getting off the vehicle. Now, users do not even need to consider the energy replenishment of their vehicles at all, as the system can handle everything. This sci-fi-like scenario has become a reality. In contrast, at charging stations, users still need to manually open the charging port and insert the charging gun, which has not completely got rid of the demand for manual operation. In addition, battery swapping remains a shortcut to achieve differentiated competition. NIO has reached cooperation on the battery swapping model with many automakers including Changan, Geely, JAC, Chery, FAW and GAC. However, up to now, other automakers have not launched models adapted to NIO's battery swapping stations, and most non-NIO battery swapping models are commercial vehicles. The number of household cars that support battery swapping is relatively small, and NIO is the only player in the high-end market. The two brands Yijing and Qijing, which are cooperatively developed by Huawei Yinwang, Dongfeng and GAC, can quickly achieve differentiated competition by matching the battery swapping model with Qiankun Intelligent Driving. (Source: Photo by Dianchetong) More importantly, at the recent performance meeting, CATL stated that more than 2500 Choco-Swap stations for passenger vehicles have been built, covering 200 cities across China, and the number will increase to 3000 by the end of the year. Unconsciously, the scale of CATL's battery swapping stations has been large enough to meet users' daily energy replenishment needs. CATL is different from NIO. NIO is an automaker, and its battery swapping ecosystem is relatively closed. Although it is moving towards openness, there are still many restrictions, so many automakers are unwilling to join NIO's battery swapping ecosystem. CATL is a battery manufacturer, and Choco-Swap is built on an open attitude. In addition to CATL building battery swapping stations itself, other enterprises can also independently build battery swapping stations based on CATL's standardized battery modules and construction standards. This cooperation model can rapidly expand the coverage of battery swapping stations after being recognized by partners. Perhaps it is precisely because the battery swapping model has inherent advantages in energy replenishment and differentiated competition, coupled with the huge battery swapping ecosystem that CATL has built to meet the energy replenishment needs of users of Yijing and Qijing battery swapping models, that Huawei has firmly chosen to join the battery swapping ecosystem even when the charging speed is getting faster and faster. It is never too late to join the marathon of battery swapping It is undeniable that with the current increasingly fast charging speed, the advantages of battery swapping are shrinking, but considering the carrying capacity of the power grid, it is almost impossible for charging to be faster than battery swapping. The more stable and faster battery swapping will always have its value to exist. In 2018, NIO's first battery swapping station was put into operation in Nanshan Science and Technology Park, Shenzhen. artigo.texto: Retail investors' cumulative net purchases reach 75.4 billion won since listing One-month return at 11.99%, three-month return at 34.98% Samsung Asset Management said Wednesday that its KODEX Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus ETF has surpassed 200 billion won ($151 million) in net assets, just four months after its June 23 listing. As of Tuesday's close, net assets stood at 237.6 billion won. The milestone has been driven largely by retail investor inflows. Cumulative net purchases by retail investors since listing have reached 75.4 billion won, with about 23.3 billion won flowing in over the past month alone. The fund's one-month return of 11.99% and three-month return of 34.98% rank among the top performers of domestically listed ETFs. Since its June 23 listing, the fund has posted a return of 6.88%, placing it first among all secondary battery and materials ETFs listed in South Korea. Investor interest in solid-state batteries and ESS has grown as AI spreads rapidly, driving demand for power infrastructure to support data centers, humanoid robots and other AI-related industries. The KODEX Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus invests simultaneously in the two growth pillars of the battery industry — solid-state batteries and ESS. About 50 percent of the fund is concentrated in LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI. LG Energy Solution has been ramping up ESS production facilities in the United States to target the North American market, while Samsung SDI is preparing to launch new lithium iron phosphate-based ESS products and begin mass production of solid-state batteries in the fourth quarter. The remaining half of the fund holds ESS value-chain companies — including Sangsin EDP, Seojin System, Han Jung N.C.S. and SFA Nexcel — alongside solid-state battery value-chain firms such as ISU Specialty Chemical, Daejoo Electronic Materials, Lotte Energy Materials, Posco Future M and L&F. "ESS is seeing sales growth driven by the expansion of AI power infrastructure, and solid-state batteries are an area where the next wave of growth is anticipated as mass-production timelines become more concrete," said Shin Hyun-jin, a fund manager at Samsung Asset Management. "We expect KODEX Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus to serve as an effective vehicle for investors to participate in both the present and future growth of the battery industry." Samsung Asset Management has been actively expanding its ETF lineup. On Tuesday it listed the KODEX US Dividend Dow Jones Active, and on Oct. 13 it launched the KODEX US AI Agent Active. The net assets of the KODEX US NASDAQ 100 also surpassed 10 trillion won on Thursday. yuni@heraldcorp.com

The company's third-quarter results, announced the previous day, fell far short of market expectations. CATL shares listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in China closed at 227.9 yuan, down 12.03% from the previous session. Based on closing prices, that was around half the May 6 peak of 460 yuan, a decline of 50.4%. CATL shares listed in Hong Kong also fell 11.41% that day. CATL said the previous day that its net income for the third quarter rose 14.54% year on year to 21.25 billion yuan (about 4.2 trillion won). That was well below both the second-quarter net income growth rate of 36.5% and the market forecast of 41.2%, compiled by the UK-based London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). It was also the lowest rate since the fourth quarter of 2024, when it was 13.6%. Third-quarter revenue grew 58.58% year on year to 165.22 billion yuan (about 32.8 trillion won). The growth rate was higher than the 56.9% recorded in the previous quarter, but fell short of the 60.2% market forecast. The Hong Kong-based English-language newspaper South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that CATL shares have been weak since Chinese EV makers Xiaomi and Li Auto announced last month that they would work with other battery manufacturers. U.S. investment bank JPMorgan said recent tax changes and other factors have caused profitability in China's EV industry to deteriorate faster than expected, potentially affecting demand for CATL's battery products. It also downgraded its investment rating on CATL's Hong Kong-listed shares to “Neutral.” [email protected] Park Jong-won Reporter

artigo.texto: A domestic alternative to Russia’s battery conductive-additive monopoly: Graphene ENG bets on cutting costs - Input - 2026-10-22 16:13:55 - Updated - 2026-10-22 16:13:55 [Financial News] A startup has taken on the challenge of developing a substitute for the “conductive additive,” for which Russia controls at least 95% of global supply. It is Graphene ENG, founded in December 2023. Graphene ENG CEO Lee Jae-young said on the 22nd, “We have developed a technology that uses graphene, a thin sheet, instead of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), which are shaped like slender tubes, to maintain electrical connections in silicon anode material, and we are on the cusp of commercialization.” Graphite, the main component of pencil lead, consists of thin layers of carbon stacked on top of one another. Graphene is made by peeling away a single layer of carbon atoms. Thin, electrically conductive and flexible, graphene has attracted attention as a material for next-generation electronic devices and batteries. Graphene plays an important role as a conductive additive in batteries. A conductive additive is an ingredient that creates pathways for electricity to flow between the particles that make up an electrode. Only a small amount is used in a battery, but it plays a key role in maintaining electrical connections between particles as the battery repeatedly charges and discharges. This role is especially important in silicon anode material, a next-generation battery material. Anode material stores lithium ions during charging. At the same weight, silicon has about 10 times the theoretical capacity of graphite, which is widely used today. But as it takes in lithium, its volume can swell to as much as four times its original size. Repeated expansion and contraction damage the particles and break electrical connections, reducing battery performance. A leading conductive additive used to address this problem is SWCNTs. Made of carbon, the extremely slender, tube-shaped material connects electrode particles like wires. However, a Russian company has been its exclusive supplier for more than a decade. Lee developed a replacement for SWCNTs using graphene. But to apply it in industrial settings, the company also had to address manufacturing costs and production scale, in addition to performance. Lee saw cost competitiveness as the starting point for expanding the market. “Convinced that the market would open up only once graphene became affordable, I started by changing the manufacturing process,” he explained. Lee, who had been struggling to expand the business, found a way forward through the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation’s “Industrial Complex Open Innovation (KICXUP)” program. Through the program, he was introduced to large companies interested in rechargeable-battery materials. The company is now validating performance with them under real-world application conditions. The next challenge is to reproduce the results achieved in the lab using customers’ materials and manufacturing processes as well. The company is also working to secure intellectual property rights. It has built a technology portfolio that includes one patent registered in the United States and three registered in Korea. Collaboration with customers is also ongoing. Last year, the company signed memorandums of understanding with multiple large companies and began joint proof-of-concept (PoC) testing to develop alternatives to nanomaterials currently sourced from overseas. The experiments are underway. The next step is to expand production. Graphene ENG plans to raise a pre-Series A round this month and set up scale-up equipment by the first half of next year. It aims to reproduce its technology at consistent quality using larger equipment, while also securing supply contracts with customers and certified test reports. In 2028, the company plans to build a large-scale commercial plant backed by Series A funding. Its goal is to increase production, lower the unit price of its products and establish a reliable supply base for customers. “We will prove that domestic technology can produce longer-lasting silicon anodes and carry that effort through to a commercial plant by 2028,” Lee said.Jointly planned by Financial News and the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation[email protected] Kim Hyun-chul Reporter

artigo.texto: On the Dash: - General Motors’ eyes-off driving will expand to large pickups and SUVs, with no timeframe given. - GM led a $108 million round in sodium-ion battery startup Peak Energy. - The company’s digital revenue could reach $9.6 billion by 2036, UBS estimates. General Motors (GM) led a $108 million funding round in Peak Energy, a sodium-ion battery startup, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. While the automaker is developing sodium-ion cells at its Michigan labs that Peak plans to use later in its energy-storage systems, it is also planning to offer eyes-off driving on its highest-selling, most profitable vehicles, large pickups and SUVs. Executives outlined the plan at a New York event on Wednesday. Peak Energy holds $1.1 billion in customer orders Peak reports about $1.1 billion in orders, mostly from a 4.75 gigawatt-hour agreement with Jupiter Power and a 1.5 gigawatt-hour deal with Energy Vault. It expects to finish its first commercial facility in the first quarter, CEO Landon Mossburg said. While sodium-ion cells remain far from mature and cost more than lithium-ion, most manufacturing for both is in Asia. Sodium-ion still offers an easier, cheaper path to domestic manufacturing, said Greg Reichow, a partner at Eclipse Capital and a Peak investor. GM extends eyes-off driving beyond the Cadillac Escalade IQ Last year, GM said it would offer autonomous highway driving in 2028 on the Escalade IQ, a pricey but light-selling electric SUV. It now plans to add pickups and other large SUVs, with no timeframe. Only a few automakers, including Mercedes-Benz, have launched eyes-off systems, typically limited to small areas at low speeds. Some industry executives say handing control back and forth raises safety and liability questions. General Motors will begin on highways and eventually expand to other roads, Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson said. A new in-house central computer will receive remote updates like a smartphone. The plan is crucial for GM to compete with Chinese automakers and EV-only brands such as Tesla, said Sam Abuelsamid, vice president of market research at Telemetry. Automakers earn average margins of around 10% on vehicles. Software-related services can reach 30% to 40%, according to PwC. UBS estimates the company’s digital revenue will grow to $9.6 billion by 2036, from $3.2 billion this year. GM can’t charge for the core experience owners have always had, said Ed Nightingale, GM’s vice president of digital products. An AI assistant will come to the Cadillac Lyriq in the coming months.

artigo.texto: CATL Photo: VCG Shares of Chinese battery giant CATL fell more than 10 percent in Shenzhen and Hong Kong stock exchanges on Wednesday, while the company pointed to growth potential in global power and energy-storage battery demand in 2027, supported by rising vehicle electrification and expanding storage markets. CATL's Shenzhen-listed shares were down 12.03 percent at Wednesday's close, while its Hong Kong-listed shares fell 11.413 percent. Results released on Tuesday showed third-quarter revenue rose 58.58 percent year-on-year to a quarterly record of 165.22 billion yuan, while net profit attributable to shareholders increased 14.54 percent to 21.25 billion yuan. But company gross margin fell to 20.69 percent, declining for a second consecutive quarter. At its earnings briefing on Tuesday, CATL attributed the pressure on profitability to changes in its product mix, the resumption of battery consumption tax, and reductions in export tax rebates. The company management said it was discussing how to share the impact with customers while accelerating the introduction of new technologies and products to limit the impact on profitability, the Securities Times reported on Wednesday. And, more tax changes are expected in 2027. The consumption tax, reinstated at 2 percent in September, is set to rise to 4 percent in September 2027. And, battery export VAT rebates were reduced from 9 percent to 6 percent in April and are scheduled to be removed in January 2027. Regarding market demand, however, CATL pointed to more potential opportunities. Responding to investor concerns about 2027, the company cited rising electrification rates and battery capacity per vehicle in China, competitive new electric models in Europe and continued growth in global energy-storage demand. Industry figures showed continued year-on-year growth in both sales and exports. China's combined sales of power and energy storage batteries rose 57.6 percent to 1,681.7 GWh in the first nine months of 2026, while combined exports increased 51.6 percent to 302.9 GWh, according to data released by the China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance on October 15. In September, combined sales grew 52 percent year-on-year, although they edged down 0.2 percent from August, while exports rose 64.5 percent year-on-year and 3.7 percent month-on-month. "Global demand for power and energy storage batteries may not be as pessimistic as the market expects," CATL management said at the briefing, adding that there was still considerable growth potential. Photo: VCG China has established the world's largest carbon emissions trading market, with cumulative trading volume in its national carbon emissions trading market surpassing one billion tonnes, an official from the Ministry of Ecology and Environment said on Wednesday, highlighting it as one of China's key achievements in tackling climate change. The figures were released at a press conference on Wednesday ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which will be held in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9 to 20. A Chinese expert said China's sustained efforts in climate action can offer valuable experience for other countries. In just over five years, China has established the world's largest carbon emissions trading market, covering about 8.3 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide, or more than 65 percent of the country's total emissions , said Li Gao, vice minister of ecology and environment, during the press conference held by the State Council Information Office, per Xinhua. In terms of emissions reduction and efficiency gains, China helped reduce carbon dioxide emissions from the thermal power sector by approximately 530 million tonnes during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-25). Internationally, China's carbon market has received widespread recognition for its achievements and has become an important platform for showcasing the country's efforts to address climate change, the CCTV report said. During the same conference, Li also said that China will send a delegation to attend COP31 and will actively advance international climate negotiations. COP31 will conduct negotiations and consultations on nearly 100 agenda items related to the implementation of the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, covering mitigation, adaptation, finance and just transition, per CCTV News. "As a responsible major developing country, China has consistently participated in and advanced international climate negotiations in a proactive and constructive manner," Li said, adding that China will contribute Chinese wisdom, solutions and strength to the success of COP31. Ma Jun, director of the Institute of Public and Environmental Affairs, told the Global Times that the gap between emission reduction pledges and real action remains wide, with current global efforts falling short of global climate targets and climate overshoot increasingly unavoidable. Geopolitical divisions fragment global governance, hinder climate cooperation and complicate efforts to balance energy, food and climate security, he noted. Some developing countries also struggle to balance climate mitigation and adaptation with economic growth and poverty alleviation, constrained by severe shortages of finance, technology and capacity, Ma added. The expert noted that China's sustained climate action offers a valuable lesson by integrating emissions reduction with pollution control and green transformation. Linking clean energy, energy-efficiency upgrades and electric vehicles with environmental improvement, resource recycling, industrial upgrading and job creation can address climate change while creating new sources of green growth. Through South-South cooperation, China can help other developing countries strengthen their capacity for independent climate action and reduce transition costs by sharing appropriate technologies, project experience and training. These lessons should, of course, be adapted to each country's resource endowments and stage of development, Ma noted. Li said during the press conference on Wednesday that China has built the world's largest and most complete clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries becoming an important engine of economic growth, according to a report by the Xinhua News Agency. By the first half of 2026, the country's total installed renewable energy capacity reached 2.46 billion kilowatts, accounting for 60.7 percent of total national power generation capacity. At the end of July, installed solar power capacity surpassed coal power for the first time in history, making it China's largest single power source. Moreover, China's combined installed capacity of operational and approved nuclear power units has risen to first place in the world. New energy vehicle production and sales have ranked first globally for 11 consecutive years. On Wednesday, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment also released an annual report on China's policies and actions for addressing climate change 2026, outlining China's basic position and proposals for the COP31. "China will continue to play a proactive and constructive role, support Turkey in its capacity as the COP31 Presidency and Australia as the President of Negotiations, and work with other Parties in the spirit of a community with a shared future for humanity to ensure that COP31 focuses on implementation and cooperation," it reads.

artigo.texto: When we asked writer-director Woody Bess what inspired Portal to Hell, his horror comedy about a gateway to hell that opens inside a laundromat, he pointed to grief. His college roommate died by suicide a couple of months into the pandemic, after the two had drifted apart, and Bess said he did not know his friend was struggling until he got the call. In the film, Trey Holland plays Dunn, a debt collector who finds the portal at his local laundromat. Richard Kind plays Chip, the demon who comes through it to drag Dunn’s neighbor, Mr. Bobshank, to hell over an unpaid debt, and Chip offers a deal: three souls in exchange for Bobshank’s. Keith David (The Thing) plays Bobshank, Romina D’Ugo plays laundromat attendant Ed, and Michael McDonald also stars. Bess wrote, directed and shot Portal to Hell, his feature debut. It premiered at Slamdance in 2025, won the Dangerous Visions Award at the Chattanooga Film Festival and played FrightFest, Calgary Underground and Vancouver Horror Show before Cineverse released it on Digital and VOD in the US on September 8, 2026. In a written interview, we asked Bess about his comedic influences, why the people in his film barely react to a portal to hell, and what the story means to him. His answers follow, lightly edited for spelling. Edgar Wright Was His Biggest Influence iHorror: The comedy of the movie is done really well. Did you have any major comedic inspirations when writing the script, be they movies, comedians, etc.? Woody Bess: I love Edgar Wright’s movies. I’d say that’s probably the single biggest inspiration. Shaun of the Dead is really funny, it’s got horror but it’s about a friendship at its core. Structurally, we ripped off Little Shop of Horrors. The Portal Stands In for Everyday Evils iHorror: A constant point of amusement for me was how casual everyone was about the things that were happening. A few times a character would note that there’s a portal to hell with the same level of import as one pointing at an uncommon, but not entirely rare butterfly. Did you write it this way only for comedic purposes, or were you trying to say something deeper? Woody Bess: For the Portal, people acknowledge it in the film but outside of Dunn and Ed, nobody really does anything about it. The idea behind it was to make a film about the mundane evils we encounter every day: our healthcare system, wealth inequality, wars, mass shootings, etc. Those are all evils we’ve learned to tolerate. They’re too big for any one person to fix and we all have bills to pay, we have our own problems. How people treat the portal in the film is the same numbness we’ve learned to get through the day. Dunn Believes People Are Black and White iHorror: I found Dunn’s moralizing interesting. You’ve said in other interviews that Dunn is not a dumb man (at least that’s not how Trey plays him), so why did you write him as trying to place everyone in a “good” or “bad” box? What can we learn from Dunn’s story in this regard? Woody Bess: We tried to keep it simple, mostly to keep costs down. There’s a book I love called Creating Character Arcs. In it, each character believes a lie that’s holding them back. For Dunn, it’s that people are black and white. The truth he has to embrace is that we’re all these messy gray blobs. We’re the heroes in our story and the villains in someone else’s. We’re hypocrites and liars and one bad day or bad decision away from being monsters. But also one good decision away from being angels. Ed Is a Friend Who Runs From Her Mistakes iHorror: If I view the movie as a metaphor, I feel like I understand the point of most of the elements. But one I haven’t quite understood is Ed. What was Ed meant to represent for Dunn? Or was she just meant to be a fun accomplice for Dunn on his demonic mission? Woody Bess: She wasn’t meant to represent anything but a friend for Dunn. I guess a part of the film is how we reconcile the mistakes we make. For Bobshank, it’s to give it all away and mind his own business. I think Ed represents the most common, which is to run from those mistakes. I feel like in 10 years or so she’d stop running and try to make amends head on. There will never be a sequel but if there was it’d probably be about that. A Friend’s Death Inspired the Film iHorror: I’m sure different viewers interpret this story differently. Some might see it as a fun, straightforward story about a hellish laundromat, while others might see it as a story about self-forgiveness, loneliness, and grief. Was this story personal for you and, if you’re comfortable talking about it, why? What inspired this? Woody Bess: My friend passed away by suicide a couple months into the pandemic. He was my college roommate and we used to do everything together. But I moved to LA after school and we grew apart. We talked less and less. When I got the call that he had died, I didn’t even know he was struggling. We can all fall into hells of our own making. Portal to Hell is available now on Digital and VOD in the US from Cineverse. If you or someone you know is struggling, you can call or text 988 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US. Fan verdict and scores by iHorror

Please enter the email address you use for your account so we can send you a link to reset your password: The zero-emission pioneer is doing the dirty work for the AI boom. All kinds of companies have refashioned themselves to exploit the AI boom. A bitcoin miner became a data center developer, a shoemaker is building GPUs, and an electric vehicle company is integrating its powertrains into server racks. Now, a company that once aspired to build one of the lowest-emitting power plants has pivoted to building one of the dirtiest in order to meet data centers’ requirement for speed to power above all. Net Power was founded to pioneer a new form of natural gas power plant with zero emissions, but it has given up on that technology and recently acquired 10 natural gas reciprocating engines that it plans to co-locate with a data center on the site intended for its first commercial plant. “We believe the clean piece is important,” Net Power CEO Danny Rice said during an August earnings call when he announced the company’s pivot to building unabated natural gas plants. “But just as it’s always been, it will only come at scale once society’s basic energy pillars of reliable, affordable power are fully in place. Power demand is outstripping supply today.” Net Power’s pivot is a sign not only that the AI boom has eroded market appetite for clean power, but that U.S. policies supporting carbon capture — primarily the 45Q tax credit that President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act recently expanded — are still not enough to support the technology’s deployment in the power sector. “The long history of doing CCS in the United States is there isn’t enough public funding to get companies to deploy it at scale,” Jack Andreasen Cavanaugh, a senior research associate at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy, told me. This is actually the second major pivot the company has made in less than a year. Last November, Net Power was still testing its proprietary oxy-combustion technology at its demonstration site in La Porte, Texas. The tech was designed to burn natural gas in a chamber with pure oxygen, producing a purer stream of CO2 than when natural gas is burned in regular air. Net Power’s system could recycle some of that CO2 for power generation and capture the rest more efficiently than a conventional gas plant could. The company had not yet demonstrated that the system could generate more energy than it used, however. By that point, Net Power had determined that its oxy-combustion plants, if they ever even did generate net power, would not be economically competitive anytime soon. In its 2025 Q3 financial report, the company said it had “decided to broaden the scope of its business” and develop more conventional natural gas plants with carbon capture equipment tacked on. It signed a letter of intent with Entropy, a Canadian company building “post-combustion” carbon capture equipment, to bring the tech to the United States, and ordered two 30-megawatt Siemens natural gas turbines for 2028 delivery. “For us and everyone else in the power and data center space these days, speed is everything,” Rice said at the time. “We believe gas turbines with [post-combustion capture] can and should be the fastest-to-market and most cost-competitive clean, firm solution for our prospective customers.” He told investors that rising costs were one of the setbacks Net Power faced in building its first-of-a-kind oxy-combustion plant. It was highly unlikely the company could finance and build a $1.7 billion, 200-megawatt plant before completing all its testing, he said. The best-case scenario for the plant to come online was 2030 or 2031, and costs might keep rising with inflation. The company could either bet on that prospect and keep bleeding cash, or “slow down that spending in order to free up some of our resources for near-term accretive opportunities.” As a public company with shareholders to answer to, there was really only one choice. By the end of 2025, Net Power decided to suspend its oxy-combustion development and testing activities altogether, according to its year-end SEC filing. Six months later, the company’s thesis changed again. Gas turbines with post-combustion capture, it turned out, were not the “fastest-to-market and most cost-competitive” solutions that the company had hoped they’d be. Whereas once upon a time, electricity buyers considered a range of factors when shopping around for power, including carbon emissions, the reality was that they were now only looking for three qualities: speed, reliability, and scale. “Natural gas power generation, co-located with customer load, and deployable on a fast timeline, is how we expect to meet that demand today,” Rice told investors, ad

artigo.texto: 'Chinese Battery Maker' CATL Shares Plunge 11% on Profitability Concerns Third-quarter revenue rose, but net profit grew just 14.5%, its lowest rate in two years China's consumption tax reinstatement and reduced export tax rebates weigh on results CATL, China's leading electric vehicle battery maker, saw its shares plunge as much as 11% intraday after reporting third-quarter results that fell short of market expectations. The increase in quarterly net profit slowed to 14.5%, its lowest level in about two years. According to Bloomberg on October 21, CATL shares fell as much as 11% in early trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and as much as 9.3% on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The declines followed the company's third-quarter results, announced on October 20, which fell short of market expectations. CATL's third-quarter revenue rose 58.6% year on year to 165.2 billion yuan (approximately 32.76 trillion won), while net profit increased 14.5% to 21.25 billion yuan (approximately 4.21 trillion won). The net profit growth rate was the lowest in about two years and well below the market forecast of 41.2%. Revenue surged, but profitability deteriorated because of rising costs and reduced tax benefits. China's tax reform plans are also weighing on the company. In July, the Chinese government ended a consumption tax exemption for lithium-ion batteries that had been in place for 10 years and began imposing a 2% consumption tax in September. It also reduced value-added tax rebates on battery exports and plans to eliminate them entirely starting in 2027. The measures are seen as an effort to curb overproduction and cutthroat competition in the battery industry. Markets expect the impact to extend beyond CATL, the industry leader, to small and midsize battery makers. Citigroup said, "If even CATL cannot fully pass the consumption tax burden on to its customers, it will be difficult for second-tier companies to absorb it." Inside the battery cell factory of Chinese battery maker CATL in Debrecen, Hungary, on October 1, 2026 (local time). AFP-Yonhap News View original image Automakers' efforts to reduce their dependence on CATL are also seen as a headwind. Some automakers are diversifying their suppliers by turning to small and midsize battery makers to reduce their reliance on CATL, intensifying price competition. CATL's shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange have fallen to about half their peak in May 2026. However, on its earnings conference call on October 20, CATL said it was "actively communicating" with customers to mitigate the impact together. The company added that it was "advancing new technologies and products to reduce the impact on profitability." CATL maintained a positive outlook for next year. The company said global demand for batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems (ESS) "may not be as pessimistic as the market expects and has good growth potential." artigo.texto: - Third-quarter net profit rose 14.54% year-on-year, while revenue increased 58.58%. - Gross margin for the first 9 months was 22.72%, down from 25.31% a year earlier. CATL (HKEX: 3750), the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, reported higher third-quarter net profit from a year earlier, but earnings fell from the second quarter as profit growth failed to keep pace with its business expansion. Net profit attributable to shareholders rose 14.54% year-on-year to 21.25 billion yuan ($3.16 billion) in the third quarter, according to financial results CATL released on Tuesday. That was down 5.77% from 22.55 billion yuan in the second quarter, CnEVPost calculations show. Third-quarter revenue rose 58.58% year-on-year to 165.22 billion yuan. Net profit attributable to shareholders excluding non-recurring gains and losses increased 14.86% to 18.86 billion yuan. For the first 9 months of the year, CATL's net profit attributable to shareholders rose 31.60% year-on-year to 64.53 billion yuan, while revenue increased 56.19% to 442.14 billion yuan. The company attributed its revenue growth over the period to business expansion. However, cost of sales rose faster than revenue, increasing 61.61% to 341.7 billion yuan. Gross margin for the first 9 months was 22.72%, down about 2.59 percentage points from 25.31% a year earlier, according to calculations based on revenue and cost of sales in the financial report. Research and development expenses rose 22.89% year-on-year to 18.52 billion yuan over the same period. Investment income increased 73.11% to 9.07 billion yuan, which the company said mainly reflected its share of investee companies' net profits. Despite the earnings growth, net cash generated from operating activities fell 23.60% year-on-year to 61.63 billion yuan in the first 9 months. As of the end of September, CATL's accounts receivable had risen 47.78% from the end of last year to 112.91 billion yuan, while inventories increased 53.15% to 144.77 billion yuan. The company attributed both increases to business expansion. CATL maintained its lead in the global EV battery market. Its global battery installations rose 25.2% year-on-year to 333.0 GWh in the first 8 months, according to South Korean market research firm SNE Research. Its global market share increased to 39.4% from 37.7% a year earlier, ahead of second-place BYD (HKEX: 1211) at 15.1%. China's battery market also continued to expand. Domestic power battery installations rose 14.7% year-on-year to 87.2 GWh in September, setting a new high for the year for the second consecutive month, according to the China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance (CABIA). Energy storage batteries grew faster. China's energy storage battery sales rose 104.4% year-on-year to 73.5 GWh in September, accounting for 33.0% of combined power and energy storage battery sales. CATL ranked first in China's power battery market in September, with installations of 35.49 GWh and a market share of 40.92%. ($1 = 6.7200 yuan)

artigo.texto: Samsung Asset Management's KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus Surpasses 200 Billion Won in Net Assets Samsung Asset Management's exchange-traded fund (ETF) focused on energy storage systems (ESS) and solid-state batteries has surpassed 200 billion won in net assets just four months after its listing, buoyed by inflows from individual investors. On October 21, Samsung Asset Management announced that its KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus ETF had surpassed 200 billion won in net assets. The milestone came four months after its listing on June 23, with net assets reaching 237.6 billion won as of the market close on October 20. The ETF's performance was driven by strong net buying from individual investors. Cumulative net purchases by individuals since its listing totaled 75.4 billion won, with approximately 23.3 billion won flowing in over the past month alone. Its return over the past month was 11.99%, and its return over the past three months was 34.98%, placing it among the top-performing ETFs listed in Korea. In particular, its return since listing was 6.88%, ranking first among battery and materials-related ETFs listed in Korea. This reflects the combination of expanding orders for Korean ESS companies and rising expectations for the commercialization of solid-state batteries. KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus invests in both solid-state batteries and ESS, the two growth pillars of the battery industry. Solid-state batteries use solid electrolytes instead of liquid ones, reducing fire risks and increasing energy density, making them a next-generation battery technology. ESS are systems that store electricity generated and supply it when needed. Applications for solid-state batteries and ESS are steadily expanding beyond the industry's traditional focus on electric vehicles to include humanoid robots, urban air mobility (UAM), and aerospace. The ETF allocates approximately 50% of its investments to LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI, leaders in the solid-state battery and ESS sectors. LG Energy Solution is targeting the North American market by successively bringing ESS production facilities in the United States online. Samsung SDI is preparing to mass-produce a new lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-based ESS product and solid-state batteries in the fourth quarter. The remaining half is invested across companies in the value chains of these two growth areas. The ETF includes ESS value-chain companies such as Sangsin EDP, Seojin System, HANJUNG NCS, and SFA Nexel, as well as solid-state battery value-chain companies such as Isu Specialty Chemical, Daejoo Electronic Materials, Lotte Energy Materials, POSCO Future M, and L&F. artigo.texto: ▲ Chinese EV battery manufacturer CATL The shares of CATL, the world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, plummeted over 10 percent on the 21st local time following third-quarter earnings that fell short of expectations. Shares of other Chinese battery makers also showed a synchronized decline. According to Chinese portals such as Baidu, CATL's shares closed down 12.03 percent from the previous session at 227.9 yuan on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. This is about half of its peak of 460.0 yuan reached on May 6 on a closing price basis. On the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, where it is dually listed, CATL's shares also dropped 11.41 percent on the same day. CATL's market capitalization shrank from 1.22 trillion yuan (approximately 242.1 trillion won) the previous day to 1.07 trillion yuan (approximately 212.4 trillion won) as of the closing price. Amid intensifying competition in the EV battery market, CATL announced in its third-quarter earnings release the previous day that its net profit increased by 14.54 percent year-on-year to 21.25 billion yuan (approximately 4.2 trillion won). This figure fell significantly short of not only its second-quarter net profit growth rate but also the market consensus of 41.2 percent compiled by market research firm London Stock Exchange Group. It is also the lowest since the fourth quarter of 2024, when it recorded 13.6 percent. The South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that CATL's shares have been on a downward trend since Chinese EV makers Xiaomi and Li Auto announced last month that they would cooperate with other battery manufacturers. In the market, there are also observations that automakers have recently shown a trend of moving away from CATL. Investment bank JPMorgan recently downgraded its investment rating on CATL's Hong Kong shares to "Neutral," citing that the profitability of China's EV industry is deteriorating faster than expected due to tax changes and other factors, which could affect demand for CATL battery products. Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, and others have warned of the possibility that market consensus forecasts could be lowered. According to Chinese media such as the Securities Times, CATL addressed concerns over demand that day by stating, "Demand is not that pessimistic," and adding that "industrial capacity utilization remains at a relatively high level." Regarding next year's battery demand, it stated that it is "still worth looking forward to." Regarding the 23.6 percent year-on-year decline in operating cash flow for the first three quarters, CATL stated that it was due to proactively adjusting payments to partner suppliers and does not affect the company's long-term cash generation capability. However, the market views that the resumption of China's battery consumption tax collection to prevent overcapacity and the reduction of value-added tax rebate rates for new energy vehicle exports will act as a burden on the earnings of CATL and the broader Chinese battery industry. Bloomberg reported that CATL's sluggish earnings are fueling concerns over Chinese battery companies. Citigroup analysts noted that CATL's latest earnings carry negative implications for other players as well, stating, "If CATL cannot do it, other companies will not be able to fully pass on the consumption tax." Other Chinese battery stocks also closed lower that day, including Gotion (-6.94%) and EVE (-5.27%) on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, and CALB (-3.57%) on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. artigo.texto: TORONTO, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HiTHIUM, an integrated full-scenario energy storage solutions provider, has announced its entry into the Canadian market. Ranked in the top two globally for energy storage component, the manufacturer has surpassed 200 GWh in cumulative delivered capacity, focusing exclusively on stationary energy storage technologies. Canada's energy storage expansion requires reliable large-scale suppliers and local presence Mizhi Zhang, HiTHIUM President of Global Business, commented: "We are committed to delivering Canadian customers advanced, robust solutions, from 8-hour long duration energy storage to extreme-weather-ready sodium-ion BESS. But this also means being present for customers wherever they are, able to serve them quickly and locally. While Toronto serves as the main hub for our Canadian operations, we have subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, as well as operating sites in Quebec, Yellowknife, and Fort Smith." HiTHIUM has introduced 4-hour and 8-hour BESS solutions to serve the market's rapid buildout of utility-scale energy storage. With installed Canadian storage expected to double between 2025 and 2027, and the country's total wind, solar, and energy storage capacity on track to reach 50 GW by 2035, HiTHIUM is positioned to fill the growing demand for BESS on a large scale. The company has also revealed a new 4 MWh sodium-ion storage solution, which is designed for an extra-long service life, supports storage durations from 2 to 8 hours, and is perfect for extremely cold climates, like Northern Canada. "Canada's ambitious clean energy targets, as well as its high safety and regulatory standards, require partners who can deliver advanced technology that's also tested and compliance-ready. At the same time, project developers have to consider the tough climate. As a vertically integrated, global solutions provider, HiTHIUM is structured to meet exactly this nexus of challenges. Our strategy of advancing both lithium-ion and sodium-ion storage is designed to offer customers in markets like Canada the benefits of flexibility, since we see these technologies as highly complementary," continued Zhang. "Our partners, whether major energy developers, public utilities, or industrial enterprises, rely on our readiness for local certification and our long-term bankability to support them, from permitting through project commissioning," added Jordan Hebbert, HiTHIUM Senior Manager of Canada. "Likewise, they depend on the proven durability of HiTHIUM technology-including performance even in extreme weather conditions. In fact, long-term operational data from North American and European projects has recently demonstrated systems outperforming even our guarantees. And we offer customers a wider range of durations and choice of chemistries because we understand that they're coming to us with a very diverse range of energy storage needs." 4-hour or 8-hour BESS: Matching duration to project specifications The manufacturer's 4-hour BESS solution consists of its "∞Power" 6.25 MWh container, built on HiTHIUM's own 1175 Ah cell. Most Canadian projects are currently designed around the 4-hour unit. This enables them to shift wind, solar, and baseload output to later peak times, strengthen grid reliability, and drive the consumption of more renewables, particularly as electrification increases demand. The ∞Power system design fits more capacity into the typical 20-foot container but also reduces a project's overall footprint, because the containers can be placed back-to-back and side-to-side. In a groundbreaking step for long duration energy storage, HiTHIUM also developed the first ever native 8-hour solution based on lithium-ion technology. Its 6.9 MWh 8-hour BESS, built with HiTHIUM's own 1300 Ah cells, fewer components overall, and a 25-year lifespan, is designed to address issues like curtailments and to fill key gaps for zero-downtime industrial segments like AI data centers. For wind project developers and data center operators alike, 8-hour BESS offers risk reduction and greater revenue reliability. Extreme fire test validates safety architecture HiTHIUM additionally worked with UL Solutions at the start of 2026 on an independently conducted, extreme fire test of its 6.25 MWh block's intrinsic safety systems. A container was subjected to 24 hours of extreme combustion conditions, with its doors opened for maximum thermal spread, while neighboring containers were placed just 15 cm away. Only the containers' passive safety systems were enabled. The results validated HiTHIUM's multi-layer safety architecture, with the tested container structurally intact after the test, no thermal propagation across the containers, and the temperatures of cells in adjacent containers remaining below safety thresholds.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- CATL addressed recent investor concerns over demand for the new energy sector in 2027 in an investor relations filing dated October 20. From the company's vantage point, industry demand that year remains promising. CATL noted that while overall domestic passenger car sales dipped in 2026, the electrification rate is climbing rapidly. So is the average battery capacity per vehicle. As a result, the power battery market for domestic new energy passenger cars still managed positive growth. Image source: CATL Electrification among domestic commercial vehicles is accelerating as well. In Europe, the shift to electric power shows continuity, with a steady stream of competitive new models hitting the market. Meanwhile, the potential for electrification in other regions is gradually unlocking. Data shows domestic power battery installations climbed 17% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, while sales (including exports) surged 38%—growth driven largely by higher battery capacity per vehicle. The average battery capacity for new energy vehicles hit 69.5 kWh during that period, a 32% jump, with both pure electric and plug-in hybrid models seeing significant gains. Image source: Baidu Stock Tong CATL's response comes against a backdrop of sustained pressure on its stock price. As of October 21, shares had halved from their historical peak. Several brokerages have already trimmed their profit forecasts for CATL for 2027. Adding to the strain are shifts in tax policy: the value-added tax rebate on battery exports was cut from 9% to 6% starting April 1, 2026, and will be eliminated entirely on January 1, 2027. CATL indicated it is in talks with customers to share the burden of these policy shocks.

artigo.texto: Commission welcomes political agreement on rules enhancing stability and long-term resilience of EU carbon market The European Commission welcomes the provisional political agreement reached by the European Parliament and the Council on a targeted amendment to strengthen the Market Stability Reserve (MSR) of the EU’s Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). Following the Commission’s proposal in April 2026 and delivering on the European Council conclusions last week on 16 October, this swift agreement will help to ensure a stable, well-functioning carbon market in the EU and enhance EU ETS’ resilience to excessive price volatility. Commissioner for Climate, Net-Zero and Clean Growth, Wopke Hoekstra, said: “This agreement is an important deliverable in making the ETS fit for the future and a strong response to the calls of EU leaders last week. It will strengthen market stability and predictability over the next decade, enhance EU industry and competitiveness, and give businesses greater certainty to invest. It will also support industrial decarbonisation by reinforcing the resilience of the EU ETS against future shocks and excessive price volatility.” Under the current system, all emission allowances in the reserve above 400 million are invalidated. Thanks to the agreement, the reserve will be able to retain up to 700 million allowances as a buffer to support future market stability and predictability. It is a first step towards a wider modernisation of the Market Stability Reserve, for which further reforms have been proposed by the Commission as part of the separate MSR reform and the EU ETS review on 17 July 2026. A press release on the MSR agreement is available online.

artigo.texto: Though far from Kansas, Doña Ana County dealt with Dorothy-level weather events this week. A tornado touched down south of Animas Tuesday afternoon, less than 24 hours after a different storm in Deming on Monday brought golf-ball sized hail and heavy rain to the region. And, the National Weather Service service issued a flood watch for much of the western half of New Mexico through 6 a.m. Friday. This comes after recent flooding devastated Southern New Mexico, destroying crops and prompting evacuation. In Washington, U.S. Rep. Gabe Vasquez urged House leadership Thursday to pass his CHILE Act, which would provide $5 billion in direct assistance to specialty crop producers. “When these farmers lose their crops, the impacts ripple through the entire food supply chain, hurting farmworkers, local businesses, and families who depend on a reliable supply of American-grown food,” Vasquez wrote in a statement. “Without meaningful federal assistance, we risk losing family farms, weakening domestic food production, and becoming more dependent on foreign growers. Protecting our specialty crop farmers is not just an agricultural priority — it is a matter of food security and economic stability for the entire country.” At a more local level, Doña Ana County is asking for community feedback to improve their responses to natural disaster — specifically regarding roadway hazards like floods, wildfires, landslides, dam failures and earthquakes. The county will leave open a survey and interactive map until Nov. 1, to “help identify roadway vulnerabilities and inform strategies for a safer, more reliable and resilient road network,” county officials said in a news release Thursday. ‘No data centers in New Mexico’ rally Youth United for Climate Crisis Action, or YUCCA, and other advocacy groups are convening in Las Cruces this weekend to strategize against data center development in the state. The three-day event culminates in a rally Sunday at New Mexico State University’s Corbett Center. Sunday’s rally “will publicly launch the campaign’s next phase: sustained statewide pressure heading into the 2027 New Mexico Legislative Session, including efforts toward a statewide ban and legislated moratorium,” according to the group’s news release. The convening comes on the heels of Grant County’s one-year data center moratorium, which passed Thursday. What to do: Organ Mountains Jubilee: In honor of the Bureau of Land Management’s 80th birthday and America’s 250th, join educators, performers and BLM wildlife biologists for guided hikes and desert education from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday at Dripping Springs Natural Area. The event at 15000 Dripping Springs Road, Las Cruces is free, but tickets must be picked up in advance. Zombie walk: The annual, free event on Main Street features live music, performances, vendors and of course, the titular Zombie Parade starting at 5 p.m. Saturday. Prizes will be given to the best costumes. Great Pumpkin Candy Drop: At 1 p.m. Sunday, a pumpkin will drop candy from the sky at Maag Field, 1700 E. Hadley Ave. in Las Cruces, with music and games for the community from 11 a.m. through the afternoon. Julia Gentin is a reporter for The Las Cruces New Mexican, The Santa Fe New Mexican and Searchlight New Mexico through a partnership with Report for America, a national service program that places journalists into local newsrooms. She covers the Southern New Mexico region. Learn more about Report for America at reportforamerica.org.
