artigo.texto: China's CATL Plunges 12% in A-Shares; Management Says 2027 Demand Still Worth Anticipating On Oct. 21, CATL's (300750.SZ) A-shares fell as much as 12% intraday before closing at 227.9 yuan, more than 50% below the all-time high of 460 yuan set on May 6. Its Hong Kong shares fell 11.41% the same day, dragging the combined A+H market capitalization to around 1.1 trillion yuan (approximately $165 billion), with single-day turnover exceeding 16 billion yuan (approximately $2.4 billion). The immediate trigger for the selloff was the third-quarter report released the previous evening: revenue of 165.221 billion yuan, up 58.58% year on year, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 21.246 billion yuan, up just 14.54% year on year and down 5.77% from the prior quarter, with profit growth lagging far behind revenue growth. Facing market doubts, CATL responded intensively on the morning of Oct. 21, with its core message being that "industry demand is not that pessimistic, and capacity utilization will remain at a relatively high level going forward." The company also addressed three focal points one by one: 2027 demand, the cash flow decline and rising inventory. The triple squeeze behind the profit slowdown The third-quarter report showed CATL's revenue for the first nine months at 442.137 billion yuan (approximately $66.3 billion), up 56.19% year on year, with net profit attributable to shareholders of 64.53 billion yuan (approximately $9.7 billion), up 31.60%. But quarterly profit growth slowed steadily, from 48.52% in the first quarter and 36.46% in the second to 14.54% in the third, a pace of margin deterioration that exceeded market expectations. The sources of margin compression are not singular. Management attributed the third-quarter margin decline to an unfavorable product mix, a higher share of low-margin products, and reduced VAT rebates combined with a 2% domestic consumption tax that took effect in September — the two together adding about 1.5 billion yuan (approximately $224.8 million) in costs versus the second quarter. Institutional estimates show per-wh profit on a battery basis fell to about 0.057 yuan in the third quarter, or about 0.081 yuan on a company-wide basis, below the 0.10 yuan of the first half, while gross margin fell 2.5 percentage points quarter on quarter to 20.7%, the lowest since the fourth quarter of 2022. Morgan Stanley analysts Jack Lu and Kaylee Xu noted in a report that unit net margin plunged from 0.10 yuan/Wh in the first half to 0.08 yuan/Wh, a significant drop, and that consensus earnings forecasts are expected to see material downgrades after the results. The bank expects margins to recover somewhat from the trough, but the extent of that recovery increasingly depends on product mix changes and the intensity of competition in the energy storage market. The structural nature of the tax burden deserves more attention. The consumption tax and export rebate adjustments are not one-off shocks: the consumption tax will rise further to 4% in 2027, and the export rebate will be eliminated that year. That means the downward shift in the unit profitability center will not disappear automatically with stabilizing lithium prices or a demand rebound in any single quarter. Company response: demand, capacity and cash flow Addressing investor concerns about new-energy industry demand next year, CATL offered a relatively upbeat assessment. The company said that although overall domestic passenger car sales have declined, the electrification rate is rising rapidly and battery capacity per vehicle is growing quickly, so power battery growth for new-energy passenger cars remains positive; the electrification rate of new-energy commercial vehicles is also climbing fast; Europe's electrification trend is continuous, with competitive new models being launched; and electrification potential in other markets "may be underestimated by the market." In energy storage, growth remains solid both in China and abroad, with demand particularly strong in some overseas markets. The company concluded that global demand for power and energy storage batteries may not be as pessimistic as the market expects. On capacity utilization, the company said the first half was "very saturated," and that tightness has eased somewhat as new capacity came on stream this year, but with demand continuing to grow, utilization will remain at a relatively high level and in healthy shape. A 23.60% year-on-year decline in third-quarter operating cash flow was another core metric that drew attention in the report. The company explained that upstream lithium battery supply chain companies have faced cash flow pressure in recent years, and that from the third quarter it proactively adjusted payment arrangements with suppliers, prioritizing partners with R&D capabilities that actively support capacity expansion — measures including shorter payment terms, prepayments and R&D funding support, which may persist for some time. The company stated clearly that operating cash flow will be affected for a period but that this will not affect cash profitability over the long run, and that it will return to a relatively healthy level. On the quarter-on-quarter inventory increase, the company said it mainly stems from business growth, with inventory turnover days relatively stable in recent quarters and no problems with sales or shipments; the increase is mainly goods shipped, which will gradually be recognized as revenue. The energy storage business's extension from battery cells and DC-side products to AC-side and system products has lengthened delivery and revenue recognition cycles, also contributing to the temporary inventory build. artigo.texto: CATL's Q3 Institutional Ownership Falls 2.25 Percentage Points; Company Says 2027 Demand Still Has Upside CATL (300750.SZ) on October 21 disclosed its third-quarter 2026 financial report. As of October 20, a total of nine institutional investors had disclosed holdings of the company's A-shares, together holding 2.157 billion shares, or 46.61% of total share capital, down 2.25 percentage points from the previous quarter. At the earnings briefing the same day, management sent a relatively bullish signal on next year's market conditions, saying outright that global demand for power batteries and energy storage batteries "may not be as pessimistic as the market expects." Looking at the shareholder list, Xiamen Rueting Investment, Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company and Ningbo United Innovation New Energy Investment Management Partnership remain among the top holders. E Fund ChiNext Exchange-Traded Open-End Index Securities Investment Fund, Futaihua Industry (Shenzhen), China Life Insurance Traditional Ordinary Insurance Products and Beijing Huading New Power Equity Investment Fund were also within the disclosure scope. The more than 2 percentage point quarter-on-quarter decline in institutional ownership reflects some institutions trimming positions in the third quarter. Yet the company did not shy away from market concerns at its earnings briefing, instead proactively breaking down the structure of demand. CATL noted that some investors have recently worried about industry demand next year, but from the company's perspective, industry demand in 2027 is still worth anticipating. In China's passenger car market, although overall sales have weakened this year, the electrification rate has risen rapidly, and battery capacity per vehicle has increased markedly, keeping growth in power batteries for new energy passenger cars in positive territory. The electrification rate of new energy commercial vehicles is also accelerating. In Europe, the electrification trend is continuing, with competitive new models steadily being launched. Electrification potential in other markets may be underestimated. The energy storage business is likewise key to supporting the company's optimistic view. CATL said energy storage is maintaining solid growth both in China and outside it, with demand in some markets outside China particularly strong, providing an important buffer for overall demand. The company's conclusion is that the global power battery and energy storage battery markets still have solid growth potential, and actual market conditions may not be as weak as outsiders imagine. For investors, this disclosure presents two clues at once: on one hand, institutional ownership has declined, putting short-term pressure on the supply-demand picture for the stock; on the other, the company has offered a relatively positive framing of 2027 demand. The gap between the two will be a key focus going forward. If electrification rates and battery capacity per vehicle maintain their current pace, and demand for energy storage outside China remains strong, the shipment base of the power battery leader still has support. Conversely, if the market's conservative expectations for next year's demand prove correct, institutional trimming may continue.

artigo.texto: September energy storage tenders hit 22GW, up 83% year-on-year, as overseas utility-scale storage orders keep flowing Overseas demand for the energy storage supply chain and Chinese domestic tender data are sending positive signals in tandem. At a recent "Zhejiang Wins Together" international procurement and "Ten Chains, a Hundred Events, Ten Thousand Enterprises" matchmaking event for the energy storage supply chain held in Hangzhou, 49 representatives of overseas institutions and buyers from the European Union, Southeast Asia and elsewhere attended for matchmaking, with intended purchases of about $450 million. According to Xunshang Research Institute and Energy Storage & Power Market, China's energy storage project bidding data continued to grow rapidly in 2026. In September, energy storage tenders reached 22.0GW, up 83.03% year-on-year. Energy storage bidding volume is typically seen as a leading indicator of installed capacity. After the mandatory storage co-location requirement was scrapped, bidding volume has continued to grow at a rapid pace, indicating resilient installation demand and offering support for subsequent growth in energy storage installations. Huaxi Securities believes that driven by energy transition policies, demand for utility-scale storage continues to be released in North America, Europe and China. Among these, storage paired with wind and solar is mainly used to smooth fluctuations in renewable output and participate in grid demand response; data-center storage, as an emerging scenario, is chiefly aimed at easing local grid congestion and ensuring stable power supply for high-computing-power loads, thereby opening up new demand space for energy storage. The brokerage also noted that overseas utility-scale storage demand is notably resilient, and Chinese energy storage supply chain companies, relying on mature products and overseas channel advantages, are expected to keep winning overseas project orders. Among listed companies in the supply chain, XJ Electric (000400.SZ) offers energy storage converters and related products and solutions for new-type energy storage; its grid-forming energy storage converter passed appraisal by the China Electrotechnical Society in 2024 and has been applied in multiple projects in China. Sunwoda (300207.SZ) continues to advance global market expansion and product matrix upgrades in its energy storage business, with R&D rolling out 280Ah and 500+Ah large-capacity cells for residential storage, commercial and industrial storage, network energy and utility-scale storage system businesses, along with differentiated products such as air-cooled and liquid-cooled systems and containers in multiple sizes. From a demand-structure perspective, the current energy storage boom is not driven by a single market. Utility-scale storage projects in Europe and North America continue to advance under energy transition policy frameworks, while China benefits from renewable installation co-location and grid regulation needs; the rise of data-center storage has opened an incremental scenario tied to computing infrastructure. For the supply chain, the pace of overseas order fulfillment and the efficiency of converting Chinese domestic tenders into installations will be two key variables for watching subsequent earnings delivery. Companies with accumulated overseas channels and product certifications may have an edge in winning orders, while upgrading cell capacity to 500+Ah and differentiating liquid-cooling and container solutions are also becoming competitive focal points in the system integration segment.

artigo.texto: New-energy heavy trucks top 50% of China's September sales for first time as CATL pushes battery-swap plan for long-haul routes China's heavy-truck market is contracting overall, but the new-energy offensive shows no sign of stopping. According to compulsory-traffic-insurance registration data published Oct. 19 by First Commercial Vehicle Network, China's heavy-truck sales fell 21% year-on-year in September, while new-energy heavy trucks grew 37% over the same period. Monthly penetration rose to 50.28%, up nearly 3 percentage points from 47.43% in August and above the halfway mark for the first time this year. The oil-versus-electric battle is thus extending from short-haul scenarios such as ports and mining areas to cross-province trunk-line transport. On a cumulative basis, the picture has yet to reverse. New-energy heavy trucks accounted for 38.10% of sales in the first three quarters, while diesel models still led with a 40.31% share. Electrification is proceeding faster in the tractor segment, where new-energy penetration reached 64.48% in September and has stayed above 60% for three consecutive months. However, short-haul tractors at ports and mining areas differ sharply from cross-province trunk lines in vehicle scheduling and refueling conditions. For new energy to expand its share further, it must win more long-distance routes. Registration data is summarized below: September's new-energy heavy-truck sales hit a record high for the month and marked the third month this year in which monthly sales exceeded 30,000 units. Refueling efficiency and fuel savings compete side by side The two powertrain routes are going head-to-head over high-mileage, high-utilization transport demand. XCMG's Hanjing, launched in September, focuses on megawatt-level ultra-fast charging; the company says it can charge from 20% to 80% in under 20 minutes. The Volvo FH Aero, unveiled in the Chinese market in October, continues to pursue fuel-saving potential; Volvo says it uses 4% less fuel than an equivalently configured FH TC model. With one side compressing refueling time and the other cutting fuel consumption, combustion models have not stopped iterating. For electric trucks to be convincing, the energy savings must offset the costs of purchase, refueling and payload. Those costs are already visible in real operations. A study published this year by ICCT and CATARC, based on 2025 research on an auto-parts transport fleet in the Yangtze River Delta, found that on routes exceeding 400 kilometers one way, electric box trucks relying on 60-kilowatt charging facilities at their destination for overnight charging typically take about half a day longer to complete a round trip than diesel trucks, and their maximum effective payload is 2.2 tons lower. Based on a five-year holding period, the study estimated that under ideal conditions — 140,000 kilometers a year, full coverage of 240-kilowatt charging facilities, same-day round trips, no payload loss and no cold-weather degradation — electric trucks have a total cost of ownership per ton-kilometer about 19% lower than diesel. If annual mileage falls to 32,000 kilometers with all other conditions unchanged, electric trucks instead incur a cost disadvantage of about 2%. For fleets, the more a vehicle runs, the more likely energy savings are to cover upfront investment. Fixed routes, stable cargo sources and predictable refueling times therefore directly affect replacement decisions; vehicles whose routes change frequently and that must look for refueling points after taking orders bear additional scheduling costs. The same study separately modeled refueling efficiency, payload loss and cold-weather range, and found that deterioration in any one condition is enough to change the conclusion: The study identified 38,000 kilometers as the break-even threshold; under the ideal scenario, the ton-kilometer TCO for electric heavy trucks was 0.75 yuan, with energy-cost savings exceeding 50%. CATL enters trunk-line market with "electric-electric range extension" On Oct. 20, CATL (300750.SZ) held a launch event for its Tianxing II heavy-truck product and Qiji battery-swap ecosystem, unveiling an "electric-electric range-extender" battery-swap solution, updating policies for swap stations, battery leasing and partners, and releasing four charging products. The solution uses an "A+B" dual-battery architecture: a bottom-mounted swap pack serves as the main-drive battery and is used under a leasing model, while an onboard range-extender pack provides supplementary power and switches in when the battery is low. CATL said that with the range-extender battery providing power backup, the bottom-mounted main-drive battery can return to the station with less than 5% charge, improving energy utilization. The system can switch power sources in milliseconds and, combined with five-minute battery swaps, shortens vehicle refueling and waiting time. Standardized batteries are the foundation of the architecture. Qiji Battery Swap released two swap blocks, 260# and 300#, with capacities of 432 kWh and 513 kWh, respectively, suited to models with 3.8-meter and 4.2-meter wheelbases, forming combinations with a 77-kWh onboard battery pack. Wang Jingzhu, executive president of CATL's heavy-industry business unit, said heavy-truck electrification requires attention to full-lifecycle value. Separating the vehicle from the battery can lower upfront purchase costs, and combined with battery leasing, financing and residual-value policies, it addresses users' needs regarding payback periods, operating returns and vehicle disposal. According to company information, the solution is in mass production at launch, with initial sign-ups totaling 13,000 units. Partners include China Post, Hunan Iron & Steel, SF Express, Jianlong Group and STO Express. artigo.texto: GM Puts $108 Million Behind Sodium-Ion Batteries as Peak Energy Plans Sacramento Gigafactory General Motors is deepening its bet on grid storage, leading a $108 million Series B round for sodium-ion battery developer Peak Energy, the companies said. The Burlingame, California-based startup said the oversubscribed financing will fund domestic manufacturing scale-up, delivery of more than $1 billion in existing customer orders and a push into the data center power market. GM Ventures led the round, joined by Maverick Silicon, Infinite Capital, Eclipse, Xora Innovation and LG Technology Ventures. The investment builds on a partnership the two companies struck in June to jointly develop next-generation sodium-ion cells for stationary storage, drawing on GM's U.S. battery cell industrialization experience. For the Detroit automaker, the deal widens a strategy that until now has centered on electric vehicles. Peak Energy, founded in 2023 by veterans of Tesla, Enovix and Fluence, unveiled a 4 gigawatt-hour factory in Sacramento in July. Production there is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027, and the company bills it as the country's first sodium-ion gigafactory. Its passively cooled storage systems, which do without cooling equipment and planned maintenance, cut energy costs by as much as 20% versus conventional systems, according to the company. Commercial agreements already in hand include deals with Jupiter Power, RWE and Energy Vault. The technology's long-run demand outlook is substantial. BloombergNEF forecasts sodium-ion battery demand climbing from slightly above 1 gigawatt-hour in 2025 to 257 gigawatt-hours by 2035, when it could supply nearly 10% of stationary storage. Sodium-ion cells remain at an early stage, however, and still cost more than lithium-ion alternatives. The International Energy Agency estimates China will hold most installed and announced sodium-ion manufacturing capacity through 2030, a supply-chain concentration that U.S. production plans will have to overcome.

artigo.texto: BAIC Group Teams Up with CATL to Build Battery-Swap Ecosystem; CATL Shares Rebound Nearly 3% Intraday In early trading in Hong Kong on October 23, shares of CATL (03750.HK) swung higher, climbing nearly 3% intraday to HK$348.8 (approximately $44) as of press time, up 2.96%, with turnover of HK$1.302 billion (approximately $166.0 million). The market's focus is a group-level strategic cooperation the company reached with BAIC Group in the battery-swap sector. According to a disclosure on CATL's official WeChat public account, BAIC Group and CATL signed a strategic cooperation agreement on one million battery-swap vehicles in Beijing on October 22. The two sides will pursue full-chain cooperation spanning vehicle development, battery-swap battery supply, battery-swap networks, battery banks and business-model innovation, with the goal of advancing the standardized and scaled development of the battery-swap industry. Under the agreement, BAIC Group will bring adapted models from multiple brands under its umbrella into CATL's Chocolate battery-swap ecosystem, and the two sides will jointly push toward the target of 1 million battery-swap vehicles. On charging-network construction, BAIC Group will open its dealer network resources, and CATL's Chocolate battery swap will use these stores to accelerate the pace of station building. The two sides will also explore a joint-operation model to co-build public charging facilities that cover the whole country and are efficiently interconnected, creating a "10-minute battery-swap circle." Judging from the scope of cooperation, this is not merely a tie-up at the battery-procurement level but an attempt to connect vehicle R&D, battery supply, battery-swap station networks and battery-asset operations. The agreement explicitly calls for building China's first million-vehicle-level battery-swap industrial ecosystem and for promoting unified battery-swap standards and network sharing, which means the two sides hope to form a reusable public platform at the charging-infrastructure level rather than each operating in a closed loop. For CATL, the battery-swap business is a key lever for extending from a battery manufacturer into an energy-services provider. The Chocolate battery-swap ecosystem has already been deployed in a number of cities, and winning group-level adoption by BAIC Group, a central state-owned automaker, should help raise the supply scale of battery-swap models and the utilization rate of battery-swap stations. For BAIC Group, connecting to a third-party battery-swap network can lower the capital expenditure of building its own charging system and, with battery-swap models, help drive sales across its multiple brands. At the market level, the battery-swap model has long been constrained by insufficient station density, non-uniform battery standards and relatively long profitability cycles. This cooperation connects automakers' vehicle resources with battery makers' network resources, and if the 1 million-vehicle target can be gradually achieved, it may offer an observable sample of a commercial closed loop for the battery-swap industry. However, the agreement remains at the strategic-framework level for now; the pace of specific model rollouts, the number of stations to be built and the scale of investment have not been disclosed, and the progress of subsequent execution remains the key to judging its impact. As of press time, CATL's share price had recovered part of its earlier decline, with turnover holding at a relatively high level, indicating that funds have given a positive response to the news.

artigo.texto: South Korea's SK On Buys First Zeekr 7X in the Country for Corporate Use, Opting for CATL-Battery Model SK On has become South Korea's first customer for the 7X, a mid-size SUV from Zeekr, the electric vehicle brand under China's Geely Group, adopting the vehicle for corporate use. It marks a case of a South Korean battery maker buying an EV equipped with batteries from its Chinese rival CATL, and industry observers interpret the move as an effort by SK On to shore up its cooperative relationship with Geely Group. Zeekr Korea said on the 22nd that it has begun domestic customer deliveries of the Zeekr 7X and handed over the first vehicle to SK On. The handover ceremony was held the previous day at the brand's flagship store in Gangnam, Seoul, with officials from both companies in attendance. SK On plans to operate the vehicle for business purposes while also giving employees the chance to experience it firsthand. The delivered vehicle is a single unit of the "Ultra," the top trim in the 7X lineup, priced at 69.99 million won (approximately $53,000) in South Korea. Powered by a 100 kWh NCM (nickel-cobalt-manganese) battery, two electric motors integrated into the front and rear axles produce a maximum output of 645 horsepower and maximum torque of 72.4 kg·m. With the traction and control characteristic of all-wheel drive (AWD), it accelerates from a standstill to 100 km/h in 3.9 seconds, with a single-charge range of 440 km under the South Korean Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment's room-temperature combined certification standard. Besides the Ultra, the 7X is also sold in a Pro trim using a 75 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a Max trim carrying the same battery as the Ultra. The Pro and Max use a single rear motor with 421 horsepower and 45 kg·m of torque, offering single-charge ranges of 375 km and 483 km, respectively. Note: Range figures are based on the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment's room-temperature combined certification standard. The purchase is drawing attention because SK On has yet to secure a Chinese automaker as a battery customer. It has also never signed a battery supply contract with Geely Group. Still, executives of the two companies are said to have maintained a cooperative relationship by traveling frequently between the two countries. Analysts say the move is meaningful for SK On, which is pursuing orders from Chinese automakers, in that it publicly announced its role as Zeekr's first South Korean customer to strengthen ties. In November 2023, SK On signed a contract with Polestar, a Geely Group affiliate, to supply battery modules for the "Polestar 5." Regarding the vehicle purchase, some in the industry speculated that a battery supply deal between the two companies may be imminent. An SK On official drew a line, saying, "Geely Automobile is an important partner for SK On," but adding, "This first-vehicle purchase is unrelated to any new battery supply contract." Also notable is that the vehicle SK On bought is equipped with CATL's NCM battery. For SK On, which has strengths in NCM batteries, the purchase means it has directly bought a vehicle using the same type of battery as its flagship products, prompting interpretation that the move is intended with an eye toward possible battery business cooperation with Geely Group down the road. Zeekr said it plans to accelerate its push into the South Korean market. A Zeekr official said, "We are pleased to be able to deliver the 7X, which embodies the technology and sensibility of the luxury technology brand Zeekr, to South Korean consumers," adding, "Starting with the delivery to our first South Korean customer, SK On, we plan to bring Zeekr's unique brand experience to many more customers going forward." Orders for the Zeekr 7X began in June at nine stores nationwide, including in Seoul, Gyeonggi Province, Daejeon and Busan, and surpassed 1,000 units within a month. Zeekr Korea plans to expand its network to 14 locations in major hubs nationwide, including Seoul, by the end of the year, and to establish 11 service centers, including on Jeju Island. The development comes as Chinese-made EVs make a full-fledged push into the South Korean market. If sales by Chinese automakers grow in South Korea, the battery and parts supply chain could also change, putting South Korea's battery industry in a position where it must weigh both securing potential customers and intensifying competition. Whether SK On can turn its relationship with Geely Group into actual orders is seen as a key point to watch.

artigo.texto: South Korea's Samsung Asset Management All-Solid-State Battery/ESS ETF Tops approximately $179 Million in Net Assets Four Months After Listing Samsung Asset Management's "KODEX All-Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus" exchange-traded fund (ETF) has surpassed 200 billion won (approximately $150.9 million) in net assets just four months after listing. Net assets stood at 237.6 billion won (approximately $179.2 million) as of the Oct. 20 close. The product was listed on South Korea's KOSPI market on June 23. Since listing, individual investors have bought a cumulative net 75.4 billion won (approximately $56.9 million), with roughly 23.3 billion won (approximately $17.6 million) of retail money flowing in over the past month alone. Returns also stand out. The fund posted an 11.99% gain over the past month and 34.98% over three months. Since listing it has returned 6.88%, the highest among ETFs tied to secondary batteries and battery materials listed in South Korea over the same period. The ETF is structured to invest simultaneously in two growth axes of the battery industry: all-solid-state batteries and energy storage systems (ESS). All-solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte instead of a liquid one, lowering fire risk and raising energy density — a next-generation technology cited for potential use in humanoid robots, urban air mobility (UAM) and aerospace. ESS is growing on the back of power infrastructure demand driven by the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. About half the portfolio is concentrated in LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI. LG Energy Solution is targeting the North American market by successively bringing ESS production bases in the United States online, while Samsung SDI is preparing to launch new lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-based ESS products in the fourth quarter and to mass-produce all-solid-state batteries. The other half is filled with companies across the ESS value chain and makers of all-solid-state battery materials, components and equipment. Note: Based on Samsung Asset Management disclosures and press releases Shin Hyun-jin, a manager at Samsung Asset Management, said, "ESS revenue is rising as AI power infrastructure expands, and all-solid-state batteries are a field where the next stage of growth is expected as mass-production schedules take shape." He added that "KODEX All-Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus will be an effective means for investors to invest in both the current state and future growth potential of the battery industry." Samsung Asset Management has been rapidly expanding its ETF lineup. On Oct. 20 it newly listed "KODEX US Dividend Dow Jones Active," and on Oct. 13 it launched "KODEX US AI Agent Active." On Oct. 15, the total net assets of "KODEX US Nasdaq 100" topped 10 trillion won (approximately $7.5 billion). The milestone is seen as the result of expectations that AI's spread will translate into demand for power infrastructure and next-generation batteries, drawing in retail money. With South Korean ESS companies expanding order books and all-solid-state battery commercialization schedules taking concrete shape, funds have flowed into a thematic product bundling the related value chains. One caveat: because the structure concentrates investment in a specific industry, volatility could increase depending on battery industry conditions and individual companies' mass-production timelines.

Greg Abbott and issued multiple stormwater permits related to data center construction. The agency said it had suspended specific data center permits identified by the watchdog groups this week. On Wednesday, TCEQ also announced on its website that its electronic filing system “used for automatic authorizations” was being temporarily disabled. “To ensure all applications are thoroughly reviewed by agency staff to determine if they are related to data centers, applications must be physically provided to TCEQ,” agency spokesman Ryan Vise said in a statement. The online system, called the State of Texas Environmental Electronic Reporting System, or STEERS, is used for a wide array of permit applications, including those related to air and water pollution. Public Citizen , an advocacy group that’s been fighting data center development along with concerned residents, and FracTracker Alliance , a nonprofit that researches environmental impact from industrial development, identified multiple stormwater permits that the groups said had been approved by TCEQ for large construction projects related to data centers. Their findings came a month after Abbott told TCEQ to stop issuing “all permits related to data center projects” while other state agencies and the state electric grid operator gathered and checked information about data centers’ proposed water and power use. The agency’s chaotic messaging and actions along with the shutdown showed the pause wasn’t real until the media and watchdogs scrutinized it, Sam Law, research and communications manager for FracTracker Alliance, wrote in an email. The groups identified other types of permits they said TCEQ had been advancing. “If our own environmental regulator can’t figure out which permits belong to data centers or have to take down their entire system because of them, it’s a real sign that we need a real moratorium backed by legislation,” Law wrote. Stormwater permits help regulate water quality impacts from water flowing over a construction site that can have pollutants, according to the agency’s website . Companies submit a “notice of intent” in the online system, which would then get automatically approved. “In this case, the agency’s rubber stamp worked so well, even the agency had difficulty stopping it,” said Kathryn Guerra, director of Public Citizen’s TCEQ Watchdog Campaign, in a prepared statement. “Texans don’t need another reason to distrust TCEQ, but here it is.” This article first appeared on The Texas Tribune . artigo.texto: AI is a transformational technology worth investing in — but investors must be selective when investing in data centers, according to the head of one of the world's biggest banks. Speaking to CNBC's Dan Murphy on Tuesday, HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery called artificial intelligence "a major enabler to re-engineer and reimagine all our businesses, all our activities." "It's going to put a lot of power back in the hands of our colleagues because of the level of productivity it gives them, so it's going to be transformational, and we're certainly very much on a journey to adopt it," he said, adding that AI would help to "re-engineer the bank." But when it comes to investing in infrastructure underpinning the technology, he advised discernment over an all-in approach. "One has to be selective," Elhedery said. "You have to look at the quality of the tenancy agreements. You have to look at the pricing of these contracts. Not all of them are of that level of virtuosity that you can support strongly. Some of them may be more challenging." HSBC was ranked as the seventh-largest bank in the world and the biggest lender in Europe by S&P Global last year, with assets worth close to $3 trillion. The bank — headquartered in London — is both a financier and operator of data centers. In its 2025 annual report, HSBC said it intends to become "the leading bank for fast-growing transition ecosystems," noting that its customer base spans areas including data centers and the AI sector. Data center campuses house the servers that power AI and cloud computing, and have seen a multibillion-dollar boom in recent years. Global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030, according to McKinsey, with Big Tech increasingly tapping private credit and taking on debt to fund the development of the facilities. But AI borrowing is becoming a source of tension in financial markets, as the cost of capital soars and corporations add to huge debt piles as they race to finance AI and the build-out of data centers. Speaking at LSEG and Eurasia Group's GZERO Summit in London earlier this month, Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser of Allianz and former CEO of PIMCO, highlighted the competition for financing between governments and AI-related companies as a source of pressure in bond markets. "Governments are borrowing what they're borrowing, plus they're refinancing debt at a higher level of rates," he said. "[And] you have hyperscalers who last year raised $200 billion in bond financing, and are probably going to raise a trillion in bond financing this year. They are yield insensitive. They are spread insensitive because they are betting on something that is truly transformational." Bond yields issued by various major economies have hit multi-decade highs in 2026, amid concerns around elevated government deficits and mounting debt levels alongside fears of sticky inflation and more hawkish central banks. JPMorgan Chase estimated earlier this year that $4.1 trillion in AI-related debt will be issued by the end of the decade, as data center and other AI-adjacent companies splurge on building capacity.

artigo.texto: A disponibilidade de energia renovável e a atualização das normas de licenciamento ambiental colocam o Rio Grande do Norte em posição de disputar investimentos ligados à economia digital e à transição energética. A avaliação é do presidente da Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte (Fiern), Roberto Serquiz, que participou, nesta quarta-feira 21, da sétima edição do Energy Storage Brasil, realizada na Casa da Indústria, em Natal. O encontro reuniu empresários, investidores, especialistas e representantes do poder público para discutir as oportunidades de negócios no mercado de armazenamento de energia. Segundo Serquiz, a combinação entre recursos naturais, formação profissional e segurança jurídica pode ampliar a capacidade do Estado de receber empreendimentos de tecnologia e infraestrutura energética. O presidente da Fiern ressaltou, entretanto, que a disponibilidade de energia eólica e solar não é suficiente para garantir a instalação de empresas, sendo necessário oferecer condições regulatórias que permitam aos investidores planejar a implantação dos projetos. “Temos algumas das maiores riquezas do mundo contemporâneo, que são o sol e o vento. Mas isso por si só não garante investimentos, então é necessário oferecer segurança jurídica e é nesse ponto que a Fiern tem dado sua contribuição”, afirmou. O Rio Grande do Norte está entre os principais produtores de energia eólica do Brasil e vem ampliando sua capacidade de geração solar. A expansão dessas fontes, porém, também exige investimentos em infraestrutura de transmissão e tecnologias capazes de armazenar a eletricidade produzida nos períodos de maior geração. Os sistemas de baterias são considerados uma das alternativas para permitir o aproveitamento da energia em horários de maior demanda, reduzir oscilações no fornecimento e ampliar a flexibilidade da operação elétrica. A necessidade de armazenamento ganha espaço no debate sobre o futuro do setor energético brasileiro diante do crescimento das fontes renováveis. Como a geração eólica depende das condições dos ventos e a solar varia conforme a incidência de luz, os sistemas de baterias podem contribuir para equilibrar a oferta e o consumo de eletricidade. A implantação dessas estruturas também representa oportunidades para fabricantes de equipamentos, empresas de engenharia, prestadores de serviços e investidores interessados em novos modelos de negócio. Para a indústria potiguar, a expansão do armazenamento pode criar condições para atrair atividades econômicas que exigem fornecimento contínuo de energia, como os centros de processamento de dados. Esses empreendimentos dependem de infraestrutura elétrica, conectividade e sistemas de refrigeração, além de regras ambientais que permitam avaliar previamente os custos e os prazos de implantação. Regras ambientais entram na pauta industrial Durante o evento, Serquiz citou a atuação da Fiern, em parceria com o Governo do Estado, na elaboração e aprovação de resoluções do Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema) voltadas ao licenciamento de sistemas de armazenamento por baterias, data centers e empreendimentos de produção de hidrogênio. As normas estabelecem parâmetros para a análise ambiental dessas atividades e buscam oferecer maior clareza sobre os procedimentos exigidos dos investidores. A regulamentação é considerada pelo setor produtivo uma etapa necessária para viabilizar projetos que utilizam tecnologias ainda recentes no mercado brasileiro. “As resoluções foram fruto de um amplo diálogo para trazer exatamente um ambiente eficiente, moderno e competitivo para quem quiser aportar no Estado”, declarou o presidente da Fiern. A atualização da legislação ambiental estadual também integra a agenda defendida pela federação. Segundo Serquiz, a entidade mantém conversas com parlamentares para avançar na revisão das normas e estabelecer condições de maior previsibilidade para os processos de licenciamento, preservando a autonomia técnica dos órgãos responsáveis pela avaliação dos empreendimentos. “Temos conversado com nossos parlamentares e estamos confiantes para aprovar uma política que traga a previsibilidade do processo de licenciamento e a independência técnica do órgão ambiental”, afirmou. A discussão envolve aspectos como prazos de análise, exigências documentais, critérios técnicos e procedimentos aplicáveis a diferentes tipos de projetos. Para investidores, essas definições a estimativa de cuse o cronograma de execução obras. Para os órgãos ama atualização das regras precisa assegurar conde fiscalização e avaliação possíveis impactos sobre o e as comunidades. “Queremos que a nova norma sobretudo, a condição de onde realmenos investimentos possam cheao Rio Grande do Norte para todo esse potencial do processo de transição completou Serquiz. Armazenamento pode ampliar cadeias produtivas potiguares A expansão do mercado de armazenamento de energia representa uma possibilidade de diversificação da economia potiguar, tradicionalmente associada à geração eólica e, mais recentemente, à solar. A instalação de sistemas de baterias pode ampliar a demanda por serviços de montagem, manutenção, engenharia elétrica, automação e operação de equipamentos. Além da infraestrutura energética, o setor produtivo avalia que a formação de profissionais especializados poderá influenciar a decisão das empresas sobre a localização de novos empreendimentos. A operação de sistemas de armazenamento e centros de processamento de dados exige trabalhadores capacitados em áreas como eletrotécnica, tecnologia da informação, segurança operacional e manutenção industrial. A integração entre geração renovável, armazenamento e infraestrutura digital também poderá criar novas oportunidades para a indústria instalada no Estado. No entanto, a concretização desses investimentos dependerá de fatores como disponibilidade de conexão à rede elétrica, condições de financiamento, viabilidade econômica dos projetos e evolução das regras do setor. artigo.texto: CHARLESTON, W.Va. — Thousands of acres along West Virginia’s Ohio River are being targeted for massive data center developments, prompting the state’s agriculture commissioner to warn that industrial expansion could permanently reduce the farmland available for food production. Agriculture Commissioner Kent Leonhardt is urging developers to avoid productive agricultural land when selecting sites for data centers and the electrical infrastructure required to operate them. “When it comes to data centers and other large-scale developments, I strongly encourage developers to consider land that is less suitable for agricultural production,” Leonhardt said in a statement Thursday. “We should not be cutting ourselves short on the prospect of agricultural economic development by taking farmland out of production.” His comments come as developers advance plans for multibillion-dollar data centers in Mason County, where the Ohio River valley offers large tracts of relatively level land suitable for both agricultural and industrial construction. Among the largest is the Monarch Compute Campus near Point Pleasant, where technology company Nscale is developing a data center complex on a site encompassing as much as 2,250 acres. The development includes plans for a large natural gas-powered electrical generation facility. Another major development, the Tamarack Data Center, is also proposed by Starwood Digital Ventures in Mason County. Although the amount of productive farmland the developments would displace has not been independently established, their scale illustrates the potential competition for land in West Virginia’s river valleys. Why West Virginia’s river valleys attract data centers West Virginia’s mountainous terrain limits the availability of large, relatively level sites for industrial development. The Ohio and Kanawha River valleys offer comparatively broad expanses of land, established electrical infrastructure, and access to water that may be needed for cooling or power generation. Some of these same lowlands support agricultural operations, creating potential competition between farming and industrial development. Large rivers, however, are not essential to every data center. Some facilities use air cooling or closed-loop systems that reduce water consumption, while smaller modular data centers can operate on existing industrial sites. Reliable electricity, sufficient transmission capacity, and high-speed network connections are also major considerations in selecting sites. Depending on their computing requirements, some facilities could be developed on previously used industrial land rather than occupying new acreage. How data centers could change farmland values Large industrial developments can change the market for agricultural property by introducing buyers willing to pay for its development potential rather than its farming productivity. For landowners interested in selling, that demand can create opportunities to realize prices that traditional agricultural operations might not support. For farmers hoping to expand, competition from industrial buyers can make additional acreage more expensive to acquire. Effects on surrounding property values are less predictable. Land near a data center may gain value if it becomes attractive for additional industrial or commercial development. Nearby residential properties, however, could face different market pressures associated with changes in traffic, noise, appearance, and surrounding land uses. Local sales evidence is not yet sufficient to establish how the proposed Mason County data centers will affect neighboring property values. A 2023 study published in the Journal of Housing Economics examined more than 16,000 farmland transactions and approximately 1.9 million residential sales in the Midwest. Researchers found that proximity to electrical transmission lines was associated with lower residential property values but higher farmland values in some markets. The agricultural premium was stronger in areas with substantial wind-energy potential. Those findings concern transmission infrastructure rather than data centers themselves and do not establish how the Mason County developments will affect property prices. Billions in development proposed for Mason County The financial stakes are substantial. An October analysis released by West Virginia Treasurer Larry Pack estimates that the Monarch and Tamarack developments could eventually generate more than $231 million annually in property tax revenue, based on their announced plans and projected taxable values. The companies have announced planned investments totaling $64.9 billion for the first phase of Monarch and $12 billion for Tamarack. According to the treasurer’s analysis, the developments could generate approximately $90.3 million annually for Mason County schools and $47.5 million for the county commission. The estimates assume the projects reach their proposed scale and are not revenues currently being collected. West Virginia’s Power Generation and Consumption Act, approved in 2025, established a framework for high-impact data centers and associated power generation. The legislation also restricted local government authority over qualifying developments. Transmission lines raise additional concerns Leonhardt said protecting farmland requires attention beyond the property occupied by data centers. Large electrical transmission projects can require corridors extending for miles across privately owned land, potentially affecting agricultural operations far beyond the developments they serve. “That same consideration for our land must extend to proposed power transmission lines,” Leonhardt said. “I understand there are economic benefits for participating landowners. However, transparency throughout the entire process is essential.” Transmission rights-of-way can restrict construction, limit certain agricultural activities, and complicate the use of large farm equipment. artigo.texto: The cost of a delayed data center is enormous: roughly $3 million per megawatt in revenue loss per month according to some industry estimates. In popular markets, the queue to get connected to the grid can stretch for many years, which means those opportunity costs pile up. So as much as they might want to avoid complicating contracts and systems that have provided reliable compute for years, data centers are being forced to embrace flexibility. The open question, however, is how much and what kind. According to experts operating at the AI-energy nexus, who spoke onstage at Latitude Media’s inaugural Flex Summit last week, answering it is complicated by the fact that people who work primarily in the energy world underestimate the complexity of data centers, and vice versa. “I think a lot of conversations between those two counterparties miss the mark because folks don’t fully recognize that they’re talking to somebody different than they might think they are,” Jake Elder, SVP of research and innovation at Energy Impact Partners, told the roomful of people who mostly worked in distributed energy. Flexibility can exist either inside or outside the walls of a particular data center. A data center could, at least in theory, flex everything from cooling or power distribution to compute itself. They can also tack on on-site energy systems, anything from batteries to generators, in order to draw less from the grid in times of high demand. But regardless of how it’s achieved, the idea is that flexibility — or being “a good grid citizen,” as compute flexibility startup Emerald AI calls it — comes with benefits: quicker interconnection, most immediately, as well as keeping the grid stable even as more loads get hooked up. As data centers grapple with how to trade flexibility for speed, practically speaking, the industry is finding that not all flexibility approaches are created equal. As Peter Hans Hirschboeck, founder and managing director at impactECI, put it, “of the types of flexibility, the energy industry doesn’t understand that compute is probably the hardest.” (Incidentally, Hirschboeck is also an advisor to Emerald AI.) Elder concurred, adding that the majority of projects that he’s seen make the speed-for-flexibility trade have relied on on-site power, either front-of-meter or behind-the meter. That’s because “it doesn’t require any real conversation with the end customer.” “Your engineering teams don’t have to get comfortable with messing with your cooling processes. You don’t have to deal with any of the SLA conversations around workloads,” Elder said. “You can just kind of turnkey transact.” One prominent example is Aligned Data Centers, which signed a deal in 2025 with Portland General Electric to bring a 31-megawatt, 62-megawatt-hour battery alongside its facility, in exchange for a faster interconnection. While this is one of just a few public deals, Elder said he’s seen a number of private bilateral agreements to do the same thing. (There’s also a growing push to use virtual power plants as a part of a data center’s capacity stack, though that’s more about demonstrating that there’s enough room on the grid for the data center to get connected, rather than flexing the facility’s power draw on the day-to-day.) That said, the industry is hampered by the lack of a shared definition for flexibility. What duration of curtailment should be required? Should there be response time or location standards? When it comes to formalizing flexibility as a part of the grid planning process or even interconnection studies for a single facility, the uncertainty is a problem. That’s according to Seyed Madaeni, co-founder and CEO of Verse. “Do I cut the load for two hours, four hours, six hours, eight hours? Because that impacts the amount of capex that we need to bring in,” Madaeni said. “There’s not a one-size-fits-all [because] every location is different. There might be a capacity problem. There might be a transmission problem.” Depending on how much flexibility is needed — would the facility need to decrease power draw for a few minutes, or a few hours? — the solutions might look different. According to one Energy Impact Partners analysis, if a service territory has 200 hours of disruption per year, with a mix of lengths and depths, about half could be met with workload flexibility, while batteries could make up most of the rest, Elder said, with “maybe one outlier event per year” that requires something more dispatchable like fossil capacity. “But that’s just one indicative study,” he added. “It’s very much going to depend on the site and the market. And over time, as we clip the far left side of the load duration curve, it’s just going to get harder.” In practically evaluating flexibility solutions for a data center, Hirschboeck considers their cost (including revenue loss), capability (short- versus long-duration), benefit, and second-order effects like the pollution that comes from a gas generator. Ultimately, the panelists largely agreed that the majority of data centers coming online by 2030 will incorporate at least one if not several versions of flexibility. According to Nima Amirzadeh, chief operating officer of LōD Technologies, “Flexibility is not a one or other solution. It’s a combination of a software layer, a battery layer, and a generation behind the meter, or some sort of backup generation.” No one can afford to be picky about their solution of choice, because getting connected to the grid is simply much harder than it ever has been before. If data centers don’t embrace flexibility, as Madaeni said, they’ll be forced to go off-grid instead. But in the meantime, there are kinks to be worked out, both technically and definitionally. “There is absolutely a path for operations here,” Madaeni added. “I think what’s not clear, which creates uncertainty, is what are the rules around this.”

artigo.texto: European Union negotiators have reached a provisional agreement to revise the rules governing the bloc’s carbon market, increasing the number of emissions allowances that can remain in reserve before being permanently cancelled. The agreement, reached by the Council and European Parliament on 20th October and announced the following day, raises the invalidation threshold of the EU Emissions Trading System’s market stability reserve from 400 million to 700 million allowances. The compromise reached by EU negotiators follows months of pressure from energy-intensive industries concerned about carbon prices, electricity costs and competition from manufacturers operating under less restrictive environmental regimes. The measure requires formal approval before entering into force and forms part of a wider review of the EU’s principal carbon-pricing mechanism. A larger reserve for future market disruptions Established in 2019, the market stability reserve was designed to address the accumulation of surplus emissions allowances that had weakened the effectiveness of Europe’s carbon market. Under the Emissions Trading System, companies in covered sectors must surrender allowances corresponding to their greenhouse gas emissions. The total quantity available is progressively reduced, creating a financial incentive to cut emissions. The reserve adjusts the supply of allowances entering the market, withdrawing them when there is a substantial surplus and releasing them under specified conditions when supply becomes scarce. Existing rules also provide for the permanent cancellation of allowances held above a threshold of 400 million. Under the new agreement, that threshold would increase to 700 million, allowing a larger stock to remain available for potential future release. The change does not automatically introduce 300 million additional allowances into circulation. Releases would continue to depend on the reserve’s operating rules and market conditions. According to the Council, more than three billion allowances have been invalidated since the mechanism began operating in 2023. The Commission initially proposed ending automatic invalidation indefinitely, while the Council’s September negotiating position envisaged a temporary suspension followed by a higher threshold. The compromise retains invalidation but increases the amount protected from cancellation. Industry competitiveness enters climate negotiations The agreement follows growing concern about the cumulative cost of European climate regulation, particularly for steelmaking, chemicals, cement and other energy-intensive sectors. Manufacturers have warned that carbon costs, combined with relatively expensive electricity and industrial gas, complicate investment decisions and weaken their ability to compete internationally. Brussels must also consider the consequences of production shifting to jurisdictions with lower emissions-related costs, a phenomenon known as carbon leakage. Earlier this year, EU Today examined the Commission’s consideration of changes to industrial protections under the ETS, including the relationship between free allowances and the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The latest reserve agreement does not directly change the allocation of free allowances, the emissions cap or the obligations imposed on individual industrial installations. Its principal effect would be to preserve a larger buffer that could become available if future market conditions trigger the release mechanism. For manufacturers planning investments extending into the 2030s, the availability of allowances and the future trajectory of carbon prices influence production costs and the commercial case for decarbonisation technologies. Carbon market figures reveal changing conditions The European Commission reported in May that the total number of allowances in circulation during 2025 stood at approximately 1.023 billion. Its annual market stability reserve calculation provided for approximately 190.5 million allowances to be withdrawn from auctions between September 2026 and August 2027. These withdrawals reflect the existing mechanism for reducing market surpluses. The proposed higher invalidation threshold concerns how many allowances can subsequently remain in reserve rather than being cancelled. The overall emissions cap will continue to decline under the legislation already governing the ETS. Consequently, preserving a larger reserve does not remove the long-term constraint on emissions or guarantee lower carbon prices for European industry. The agreement also concerns the established ETS covering power generation, industry and certain other sectors, rather than the separate ETS2 regime for emissions associated with road transport and buildings. The latter has generated its own political controversy, as EU Today reported following the October European Council summit. Broader ETS reform remains unresolved The Council and Parliament have agreed that the question of gradually reducing the invalidation threshold should be considered during the broader ETS review. That exercise will address the carbon market’s operation over a longer period, when the declining supply of allowances could create tighter conditions. The present agreement therefore provides an adjustment to the reserve mechanism without reopening the entire emissions trading framework. Following legal and technical finalisation, the provisional deal must be endorsed by both institutions and formally adopted. The new 700 million threshold would apply after the legislation takes effect, while the larger review of the ETS continues through the EU legislative process.

artigo.texto: Google planeja data center – O Google planeja construir um data center de 780 megawatts em Pine Island, Minnesota, nos Estados Unidos, acompanhado de investimentos em energia renovável e armazenamento. O acordo com a Xcel Energy prevê ampliar a capacidade da rede elétrica além da demanda da instalação, mas ainda depende de aprovação da Comissão de Utilidade Pública do estado. Segundo a CNBC, a empresa financiará a adição de 1.400 MW de energia eólica, 200 MW de energia solar e 300 MW de armazenamento em baterias. A capacidade adicional busca compensar a geração intermitente das fontes renováveis. LEIA: Quanto de água uma pergunta ao ChatGPT realmente consome? Proteção contra a saída antecipada O contrato prevê que o Google pague pelo menos 75% da capacidade acordada, mesmo que utilize menos energia. Se encerrar o compromisso antes do prazo, poderá arcar com até oito anos de cobranças mínimas. “Ninguém quer ter uma grande expansão e depois não ter para onde mandar essa energia e ninguém para pagá-la”, diz Amanda Rome, vice-presidente executiva da Xcel Energy. “É aí que essas proteções entram.” A iniciativa ocorre em meio à crescente demanda por eletricidade dos centros de dados. A Corporação Norte-Americana de Confiabilidade Elétrica (NERC) aponta essas instalações como principal fator de expansão prevista do consumo na América do Norte na próxima década. Nos Estados Unidos, o envelhecimento da infraestrutura também pressiona o setor elétrico. Centros menores como alternativa Para Jigar Shah, sócio da consultoria Multiplier, empresas poderiam optar por instalações menores em regiões com capacidade disponível na rede, reduzindo custos para os consumidores. “Se você encaixar o crescimento de carga que os centros de dados querem na rede existente, as tarifas de todo mundo caem muito”, afirma. Segundo ele, construir unidades menores exige mais planejamento, mas pode evitar grandes expansões de infraestrutura. Incentivos das distribuidoras David Pomerantz, diretor-executivo do Energy and Policy Institute, observa que as distribuidoras têm incentivos financeiros para investir em novas estruturas. “Quando [as distribuidoras] constroem algo novo, financiam parte desse investimento com recursos de investidores de Wall Street e desfrutam de retornos incrivelmente altos, exorbitantes sobre esses investimentos, tipicamente em torno de 10%”, afirma. Uma alternativa seria os operadores de data centers financiarem melhorias na rede com capital mais barato. Pomerantz, porém, aponta que essa possibilidade gera conflitos com as distribuidoras. Apesar das ressalvas sobre o modelo, Shah avalia positivamente a proposta do Google, que aguarda autorização regulatória. artigo.texto: Segundo a Dra. Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, Diretora da Escola de Treinamento de Quadros do Agribank e Vice-Chefe do Comitê Diretivo de ESG do Agribank, essa lacuna exige que os bancos vejam o financiamento de carbono em etapas, em vez de considerarem os créditos como uma fonte de pagamento facilmente identificável desde o início. Do ponto de vista de um banco comercial, qual considera ser a intersecção mais importante entre o crédito verde e o mercado de carbono? A intersecção mais crucial reside no intervalo de tempo entre as necessidades de capital e o momento em que o valor do carbono é gerado. As necessidades de capital normalmente surgem durante as fases de preparação e implementação do projeto, enquanto os créditos só aparecem depois que os resultados da redução de emissões são medidos, verificados e as condições de desembolso são atendidas; a receita também depende de transações e pagamentos. Portanto, a questão para os bancos não é se devem ou não comprar e vender créditos, mas sim como financiar o processo de geração de reduções de emissões e quando o valor do carbono é suficiente para influenciar as decisões de crédito. Uma área florestal, um campo ou um sistema de tratamento de resíduos com potencial para redução de emissões não é suficiente para determinar imediatamente o número de créditos que podem ser vendidos. O projeto deve ter uma metodologia adequada, uma linha de base, complementaridade, dados, um sistema de medição, relato e verificação (MRV) e procedimentos completos de desembolso. Para os bancos, é necessário distinguir claramente entre "potencial para redução de emissões" e "registrado", "verificado", "créditos emitidos", "contratos de venda assinados" e "pago". Cada status possui um grau de certeza diferente e não pode ser equiparado mecanicamente à mesma fonte de pagamento. Então, onde exatamente se encontra a maior lacuna financeira na cadeia de valor do carbono, senhora? A lacuna reside principalmente no período anterior à geração do crédito. Durante a fase de preparação, as empresas precisam investir em pesquisas, estudos de viabilidade, documentação, metodologia, dados iniciais e consultoria. Durante a implementação, as necessidades de capital se concentram em equipamentos, infraestrutura, tecnologia e capital de giro. Uma vez que o projeto esteja operacional, as empresas continuam a necessitar de custos de MRV (Monitoramento, Verificação e Relato), verificação independente e financiamento-ponte enquanto aguardam o desembolso ou pagamento. Somente durante a fase de comercialização surgem necessidades como avaliação, negociação de contratos, pagamentos, câmbio, garantias e gestão de fluxo de caixa. Portanto, é improvável que uma única estrutura de crédito seja adequada para toda essa cadeia. O financiamento de carbono precisa ser projetado em etapas e de acordo com os níveis de risco, em vez de atribuir um único "rótulo de carbono" a um único produto de crédito. Como os bancos devem encarar a receita proveniente do carbono em suas estratégias de empréstimo? Os valores do carbono podem influenciar as decisões financeiras por meio de três canais. Em primeiro lugar, investimentos de baixa emissão podem ajudar a reduzir os custos de produção, economizando energia, combustível, água ou materiais. Em segundo lugar, para as empresas que cumprem as regulamentações, a redução das emissões pode diminuir a necessidade de adquirir quotas adicionais. Em terceiro lugar, os projetos que atendam às condições do mecanismo de crédito podem gerar receita a partir da transferência de resultados ou créditos de redução de emissões. Esses três canais precisam ser quantificados separadamente, evitando duplicação. Isso pode levar à formação de um princípio de "fluxo de caixa em dois níveis": o fluxo de caixa da produção/negócio principal constitui a base para o pagamento da dívida; a receita de carbono é um nível suplementar e só é reconhecida na medida da certeza. Essa abordagem permite que os bancos apoiem projetos desde o início, mas não transforma uma expectativa ambiental não confirmada em uma fonte garantida de pagamento da dívida. É possível prever três níveis. No primeiro nível, se um novo projeto tiver uma ideia, área, tecnologia ou reduções de emissões estimadas, a receita de carbono deve ser considerada apenas como um cenário adicional. No segundo nível, quando uma metodologia adequada estiver em vigor, houver dados de qualidade suficientes disponíveis, o projeto estiver registrado e houver um contrato ou resultado confiável, o banco poderá considerar o reconhecimento de uma parcela após a aplicação de um fator de ajuste de risco. No terceiro nível, quando os créditos forem emitidos ou os recebíveis de um contrato de venda constituírem uma base suficiente, o banco terá mais fundamentos para considerar o financiamento, mas ainda deverá avaliar a transferibilidade, as condições de pagamento, a capacidade do comprador e os riscos legais. Dadas as características específicas do Agribank, poderia partilhar quais as vantagens que o banco tem para participar mais ativamente nos fluxos de capital verde ligados ao mercado do carbono? A vantagem do Agribank reside em sua base de clientes, rede de contatos e escala de crédito para a agricultura, agricultores e áreas rurais. Em meados de 2026, o total de ativos do Agribank ultrapassará VND 2,7 trilhões, o capital mobilizado ultrapassará VND 2,5 trilhões e a carteira de empréstimos para a economia ultrapassará VND 2 trilhões. Em agosto de 2026, a carteira de empréstimos para agricultura, agricultores e áreas rurais atingirá mais de VND 1,34 trilhão, representando 64,7% do total de empréstimos. Em 31 de julho de 2026, todo o sistema contará com mais de 58.000 grupos de empréstimo, com mais de 910.000 membros e um total de empréstimos pendentes superior a VND 216 trilhões. artigo.texto: Custom Electronics, Inc. (CEI) is developing bespoke battery modules and electronic systems for drones and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with solutions designed to meet the specific size, weight and power (SWAP) requirements of individual platforms. The company’s battery technology can be adapted to different shapes and aircraft configurations, addressing requirements that standard off-the-shelf products cannot fulfil. Each system is engineered around the available space on the aircraft, with conformal antenna arrays supporting a range of spectral requirements. CEI offers several design configurations, including conformal, form-fit, structural, bare and flexible platform solutions. These options allow UAV designers and manufacturers to integrate power and electronic systems tailored to their aircraft and operational needs. The technologies also support advanced unmanned system architectures, including fully autonomous and semi-autonomous swarms, intelligent sensors, secure communications and integrated power modules intended to extend platform run-time. VTOL Sail Wing supports long-range operations One of CEI’s featured platforms is its VTOL Sail Wing, a long-range unmanned aircraft system (UAS) designed to maximise airtime through an optimised lift-to-drag ratio. The vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) fixed-wing aircraft functions as a modular test platform. Its design combines a lifting-body configuration with a pusher motor, a coaxial quad-rotor arrangement for redundancy and a twin-boom box tail. The tail also provides additional stability and options for antenna attachment. Further features include wind-velocity sensing for anti-stall functionality and stable speed settings. The platform is compatible with Q Ground Control and Mission Planner. CEI focuses on low-SWAP communications, power and electronic solutions to address the evolving demands of unmanned systems. Its customised engineering approach aims to help UAV developers balance aircraft endurance, available space and system performance. Image credit: Custom Electronics.

artigo.texto: U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday urged data center companies to "MAKE DEALS" with local communities to ensure their support for the costly facilities. Trump said that to make them more popular, data center operators should pay the community, "and/or individuals within the community, a 'dividend.'" "I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck. MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A.," the president said in a post on Truth Social. Data centers have become a hot-button issue ahead of the midterm elections in November. Public opposition to the buildout of the facilities and their environmental impact has been growing, with multiple states considering moratoriums. AI infrastructure company Nebius is "100% in principle" having discussions about investing in communities, the company's Chief Revenue Officer Marc Boroditsky told CNBC when asked about Trump's suggestion of a dividend. There could be "some sort of way where the rewards are actually funneled back to the community," Boroditsky told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference. "We see it today in terms of the tax revenue that are arriving. I could see something like a benefit of some sort that's more direct economic opportunity for the community as well," he said. Boroditsky added: "A dividend is being paid in different forms — investing in education, job development, overall economic development. The concept that the president identified... it's not crazy to consider something like that." Data center stocks have also come under pressure this week amid growing concerns about the financial health of the sector. As the AI infrastructure buildout grows more costly, companies are increasingly turning to debt markets to finance deals. When it comes to investing in infrastructure underpinning the technology, HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery advised discernment over an all-in approach. "One has to be selective," Elhedery told CNBC's Dan Murphy on Tuesday. "You have to look at the quality of the tenancy agreements. You have to look at the pricing of these contracts. Not all of them are of that level of virtuosity that you can support strongly. Some of them may be more challenging." Power constraints Much of the concern centers around water usage, power consumption, electricity prices, and the sheer amount of space that some centers require. Access to power is a major constraint on the sector, as power grids in the U.S. and Europe become overwhelmed with applications from large energy users like data centers. Trump, a long-time supporter of data centers, said Wednesday that he has been watching them "very closely" and has now come to a "very strong conclusion." "New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data enters are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid, and therefore there is electric price increase. In fact, there could be a substantial decrease," Trump said.

A Alphabet (GOOGL) propôs um acordo com a Xcel Energy para alimentar um novo data center de IA em Pine Island, Minnesota. O local está planejado para 780 megawatts. Pine Island é uma pequena cidade com cerca de 4.000 habitantes. A Google ajudaria a pagar por nova capacidade de geração na rede da Xcel, que inclui 1.400 megawatts de energia eólica, 200 megawatts de solar e 300 megawatts de armazenamento em baterias. É mais do que o data center precisa. A Google diz que isso se deve ao fato de que a energia eólica e solar não produzem energia o tempo todo. A Xcel afirma que a nova capacidade atenderá todos os clientes locais, não apenas a Google. O acordo tem proteções embutidas. A Google pagaria por pelo menos 75% de sua capacidade contratada, mesmo que use menos. Se rescindir o acordo antecipadamente, poderá dever até oito anos dessas cobranças mínimas. O acordo ainda precisa da aprovação da Comissão de Serviços Públicos de Minnesota. Uma pesquisa da Gallup descobriu que 71% dos americanos se opõem a um data center em sua área local. O uso de energia é uma das principais preocupações, enquanto a Google também deseja operar com energia livre de carbono 24 horas por dia até 2030. Jigar Shah, da Multiplier, diz que as empresas poderiam construir data centers menores onde a rede já tem capacidade ociosa. O observador David Pomerantz observa que as concessionárias geralmente obtêm retornos de cerca de 10% em novas construções, o que pode criar conflitos. O Que o Mercado Está Nos Dizendo Sobre a Ação da Alphabet Para a ação da Alphabet, isso é menos sobre um local específico e mais sobre o problema de energia por trás da IA. A demanda é forte, e a Alphabet diz que ainda está com oferta insuficiente. Sua receita de nuvem no Q2 cresceu 82%, e a margem operacional subiu para 35,6%. O backlog da Cloud cresceu mais de $50 bilhões em relação ao trimestre anterior. Os gastos são o outro lado da história. A Alphabet elevou sua faixa de capex para 2026 de $180 bilhões para $190 bilhões, para até $195 bilhões a $205 bilhões. Ela espera que o capex aumente significativamente em 2027. O fluxo de caixa livre foi negativo em $5,9 bilhões no trimestre e a administração espera que ele permaneça sob pressão. O acordo com a Xcel mostra uma maneira pela qual a Alphabet pode lidar com esses custos. Ele permite que a Google financie melhorias na rede vinculadas ao seu próprio crescimento. Também pode ajudar a amenizar a resistência da comunidade. No geral, a ação da Alphabet reflete um crescimento rápido da IA combinado com gastos pesados. A aprovação em Minnesota é mais um item a ser observado. Os investidores que detêm ações da Alphabet também observarão se o backlog da Cloud se transforma em receita.
