artigo.texto: TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 20, 2026 / Polaris Renewable Energy Inc. (TSX:PIF) ("Polaris" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has awarded and executed a contract with Trina Energy Storage Solutions (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. ("Trina Storage") for the supply of battery energy storage systems ("BESS") for the Company's Punta Lima project in Puerto Rico. Trina Storage is a global utility-scale energy storage provider with 30 GWh of BESS projects commissioned and under execution worldwide, including more than 6 GWh across Latin America and the Caribbean. The Punta Lima BESS project is being advanced under Puerto Rico's Accelerated Storage Addition Program ("ASAP"), a strategic initiative designed to strengthen grid reliability through the deployment of utility-scale battery energy storage systems co-located with existing generation facilities. As background, on June 5, 2026, Polaris Power US, Inc. ("PPUS") fully executed the BESS Standard Offer Agreement (the "SO1 Agreement") with the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority, establishing the framework for its participation in ASAP. The award and execution of the supply contract with Trina Storage represents the next key milestone in advancing the Punta Lima BESS project. The Punta Lima BESS will consist of a single 35.7 MW system with an 8-hour duration. Under the SO1 Agreement, the Storage Capability of 71.4 MW will be served by the BESS through two four-hour energy delivery blocks. Total estimated gross capital expenditures for the ASAP project, including the BESS, medium-voltage transformer, tariffs and balance of plant, are expected to range from US$55 million to US$60 million and will be funded with cash on hand. Once constructed and fully operational, the project is expected to contribute approximately US$12.5 million of EBITDA in the first year of operation. PPUS, as Resource Provider, will be entitled to receive monthly fixed and performance-based payments from the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority in exchange for providing energy storage services, including capacity and grid support. The agreement with Trina calls for deliveries of the BESS containers to take place March/April 2027. Accordingly, commercial operation of the project is currently expected in the third quarter of 2027, and the agreement will run for a 20-year term from the commercial operation date. Marc Murnaghan, CEO of Polaris, commented: "The execution of the supply contract with Trina Storage is a significant milestone in advancing our investment in Punta Lima, moving the project from its contractual framework into equipment procurement and implementation. This investment reflects our confidence in Puerto Rico's long-term energy transition and our commitment to delivering critical storage capacity that will enhance grid reliability and resilience. We look forward to working with Trina Storage and our partners to advance the project toward construction and commercial operation." Polaris remains committed to delivering long-term, sustainable energy solutions across Latin America and the Caribbean and looks forward to working with Trina Storage and other stakeholders through the implementation of the Punta Lima BESS project. About Polaris Renewable Energy Inc. artigo.texto: Shares of Australia's NextDC plunged 39.5% on Wednesday after the data center operator slashed its annual earnings forecast, citing power supply delays at its Melbourne facility amid local community and stakeholder opposition. The company lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to between $475 million Australian dollars and A$500 million, from A$615 million to A$640 million forecast earlier, while cutting its underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, forecast to A$245 million to A$265 million from A$385 million to A$410 million. The delays to power stem from the suspension of infrastructure upgrades at the company's M3 Melbourne data center amid community opposition, with electricity distributor Jemena not expecting to resume work before February 2027, according to NextDC. Jemena cited safety concerns and restricted access to work sites due to community opposition, as well as a lack of consent from the local council pending further community consultation. Citi said in a note that NextDC's power delays could affect earnings beyond fiscal 2027, citing delays to approvals for the M3 expansion and a longer-than-expected timeline for transformer upgrades. As Australia grapples with growing concerns over the impact of data center developments on local communities, Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the government was working to establish national standards for investment. Chalmers told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Wednesday that the government welcomes investment in data centers and AI infrastructure, provided it aligns with the country's national interest, adding that the government was finalizing national investment standards to address concerns surrounding AI deployment. Australia is not alone in facing opposition to data center projects, there has been growing push back against data center developments worldwide, amid concerns over their impact on local communities and the environment. NextDC shares have declined for seven straight weeks, and are on course to end lower for the eighth week.

artigo.texto: Germany Adds 8.2 GWh of Battery Storage in Nine Months, Up 91% According to the BSW-Solar association, more than half a million batteries have been commissioned in Germany since January, driven by large-scale storage. The solar lobby is publishing fifteen reform proposals to accelerate the trend. Germany has markedly accelerated the rollout of stationary batteries. In the first nine months of 2026, more than half a million new systems with a combined capacity of around 8.2 gigawatt-hours (GWh) were commissioned. Newly installed capacity is thus up 91% from the same period in 2025. The large-scale storage segment more than quadrupled, according to an analysis of Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) data by the German Solar Association (Bundesverband Solarwirtschaft, BSW-Solar). Growth driven by large-scale storage For the full year, the association expects additions well above ten gigawatt-hours. According to researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Energy Economics and Energy System Technology (IEE), however, four to five times more additional flexibility would need to be tapped each year by 2030. The aim would be to integrate the planned expansion of renewables at the lowest possible cost. Storage is also advancing outside Germany: Uriel Renovables has completed two 10 MW battery storage plants in the United States, while Ensol counts more than 1,610 residential batteries. According to Fraunhofer IEE calculations, an additional 80 GWh of battery capacity could have relieved consumers and the federal budget of nearly â¬4 billion last year. Batteries can absorb surplus solar and wind power and release it when needed. They thereby help ease the load on power grids. Fifteen reform proposals BSW-Solar has published a position paper containing 15 reform proposals. They aim to remove investment barriers, make better use of existing grids and avoid unnecessary costs in grid expansion and renewable energy support. Three measures are at the centre of the paper. The association first calls for a binding right to fair and flexible grid connection agreements, so that batteries can be operated more easily alongside solar and wind plants or at consumption sites. It then asks that distribution system operators be required to tender specifically for grid-serving batteries at substations. The third measure concerns redispatch, the control of plants to avoid grid congestion. According to BSW-Solar, control should apply at the grid connection point rather than at each individual generation plant. Surplus solar power could then be stored during temporary congestion instead of curtailing solar plants. The association, which represents more than 1,000 solar and storage companies, is appealing to the Bundestag and the federal government. It wants its proposals to be taken into account in the upcoming grid package and reform of the Renewable Energy Sources Act (Erneuerbare-Energien-Gesetz, EEG). Grid reserves to be tapped at substations Another Fraunhofer IEE study assesses the potential of better battery integration. According to its findings, batteries at substations can unlock grid reserves that have so far gone unused. Under the conditions studied, this could allow significantly more solar plants to be connected to existing distribution grids, up to a doubling of installed photovoltaic capacity. BSW-Solar laments the lack, within the federal government, of clearly assigned responsibility, binding expansion targets and an overarching storage strategy. "Battery storage must become a top priority," says Carsten KÃ¶rnig, the association's managing director. He argues that Germany cannot afford to leave a growing share of cheap solar and wind power unused while high electricity costs are under debate. In his view, batteries would allow existing grids to be used more efficiently, and he calls on policymakers to lift the legislative brakes. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: Memphians react to failed data center moratorium MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC) - The Memphis City Council passed a new data center ordinance Tuesday night, but it is not the legislation activists and environmentalists fought for and supported. New security rules instituted after the chaotic Oct. 6 council meeting kept disruptions at a minimum, but not the disappointment. The council passed an ordinance that calls for a 135-day pause on the permitting process for data centers, far less than the 12 to 18 months the activists endorsed. The meeting lasted more than five hours, filled with emotion. Citizens expressed doubt in the council’s decision-making. “History will find us on the right side of this issue,” one man told the council. “Data centers don’t belong in neighborhoods and communities,” said another woman. “And we can’t accept an ordinance, Councilman Warren, drafted by ChatGPT and rubber stamped by SpaceXAI,” another speaker said. Councilman Jeff Warren and Councilwoman Rhonda Logan sponsored the legislation OK’d by council, which was updated at the last minute. And while Councilwoman Jerri Green said council needed more time to understand the changes, Logan disputed that. “My ordinance has not changed. Everything you talked about tonight is not under our purview. The only thing we can address is land use,” said Logan. City Council Chairwoman Jana Swearengen-Washington told Action News 5, “This item is still going to have a pause in it and it’s going to have some guardrails. It’s more of what they need and what they requested.” KeShaun Pearson, founder of Community Against Pollution, said what is needed is more community input and further study of the impact of data centers on Memphis’ air, water and electricity. What council passed, he said, doesn’t come close to addressing that. “It’s not good enough because it’s not what the people wanted,” he told Action News 5, “It’s not good enough because it was presented to the people 45 minutes before it was voted on.” His brother, State Rep. Justin J. Pearson, who successfully challenged the council’s ban on his and five others’ attendance at the meeting in federal court, said the next step in the fight against data centers will be taken at the polls. “It is apparent that the Chamber of Commerce and Elon Musk have significant sway over some of these city council members,” Pearson said, “and it’s the responsibility of the people of this city to see them for who they are and to vote them out next year.” The council has requested a data centers study. Mayor Young issued an executive order earlier this month asking for a review of policy to determine the appropriate guardrails for the facilities. Data center critics said it’s too little, too late and the ordinance passed lacks the teeth to protect the people. “It was a big missed opportunity for the City of Memphis to be a leader in the region,” said Sarah Houston, Executive Director of Protect Our Aquifer, “We could be talking with our neighbors in DeSoto County and in Millington, where they just passed a moratorium and have a collaborative approach to data center regulation so it’s more uniform. It’s a missed opportunity.” The five council members who voted no against the ordinance were: Easter-Thomas, Green, Smiley, Walker and Swearengen-Washington. Councilwoman Cooper-Sutton was not in attendance. Action News 5 was told she’s handling a family emergency in Mississippi. Click here to sign up for our newsletter! artigo.texto: Due to the quick turnaround of press time, The Weekly focused on one key item from last night’s Santa Clara City Council meeting. We offer more in-depth coverage of other items discussed at the city council meeting in the coming days. The Santa Clara City Council kicked the can down the road again on whether to prohibit the construction of new data centers in the city. At its most recent meeting on Oct. 20, the council opted to simply note and file a report detailing the pros and cons of a moratorium on new data centers. Council Member Karen Hardy, who is also running for mayor in the upcoming election, proposed the action at a previous meeting, but the item was deferred because of overly full agendas. The council previously discussed a related matter, proposed by Council Member Suds Jain, regarding the water use of data centers. City Manager Jovan Grogan said the city is unable to provide power to new data centers and has ostensibly halted data center approvals since 2023. The proposal stirred the pot on the council. “What are we afraid of, we’re afraid of having a discussion? That worries me,” Hardy said. Council Member Kelly Cox said she believes data centers are not for every community. She called discourse around data centers “our century’s Cold War,” adding that there is “mass propaganda” surrounding the discourse around them. She opposed halting construction on new data centers, calling it “irresponsible governance.” Council Member Kevin Park said the city uses its low rates as justification for continued expansion of the city’s utility, Silicon Valley Power. “Residential rates keep going up, and it is not the residents that need the power,” he said. Public commenters amounted to union leaders advocating for the jobs that data centers provide. Mayor Lisa Gillmor called data centers the “jewel of the city,” saying Santa Clara is the “gold standard.” Other cities, she said, are “light years” behind Santa Clara. “We do it right. I am really proud of what we do,” she said. “Stop poking at our success, because we have a lot of it … we have done the right thing. We are making sure our residents’ rates are low. We supply good-paying jobs. We are still business-friendly, and that the business centers will also give back to the community.” Hardy also proposed examining how the city deals with non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) regarding data centers. “The public needs to know that we aren’t making back-room deals,” said Park. Gillmor accused her colleagues of hypocrisy, saying several of them agreed to an NDA for the FIFA World Cup and the Super Bowl held at Levi’s Stadium earlier this year. Gillmor and Cox worried that singling out data centers for NDA disclosure sent the wrong message to the public. Gillmor said the city’s “reputation was on the line.” “How can you not put this on for further action right away, otherwise you are hiding stuff,” said Byron Fleck, a public commenter and a volunteer with Hardy’s campaign for mayor. Park amended the motion to broaden the scope of NDAs from data centers to all city dealings. Grogan said he was “increasingly concerned” with the amount of work the council was delegating to the city employees, adding that the council already has 150 items on its list of priority initiatives. A motion to discuss the city’s NDAs passed unanimously. It will return to the council at the same time as when the city discusses data centers and their water usage. Santa Clara City Council Consent Calendar Spending The council approved the following spending in one motion via the consent calendar: - Two $250,000 increases to purchase orders with Reed & Graham and Granite Rock to cover up to four one-year extensions for backfill and asphalt. The total purchase order is now $1.75 million. - A $627,430 increase to a purchase order with Vintage Contractors, Inc. for additional recreational court repair and resurfacing. - $5.83 million agreement with First Shield Security & Patrol, Inc. for city security through the end of October 2029. - A three-year, $2.72 million agreement with ACE Parking for parking control and event parking operations at the Santa Clara Convention Center. - A one-year, $611,903 extension to an agreement with Performance Mechanical, Inc. for boilermaker and pipefitter services. The total is now $2.61 million. The next regularly scheduled meeting is 7 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 10 in the Council Chambers at City Hall, 1500 Warburton Ave. in Santa Clara. artigo.texto: Data center air pollution permit under public review MASON COUNTY, W.Va. (WSAZ) - An air permit application for the Monarch Cloud Campus outlines plans for the site and its’ proposed power system that would operate independently of the traditional electric grid. The plans call for more than 800 primary engines, along with six natural gas heaters, 12 emergency generators and six diesel-powered firewater pump engines. During a public meeting, the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection explained how the state evaluates whether a project like this meets air quality standards. “They want to install a power generation facility that would power their data center campus. And so they’ve applied for an air quality permit for that power-generating equipment. We’ve conducted a technical review of that application,” Terry Fletcher with WVDEP said. The application also calls for testing, emissions monitoring and record-keeping to demonstrate compliance. The permit falls under the state’s major-source permitting program, known as Prevention of Significant Deterioration. The process is intended to allow industrial development while limiting how much air quality can deteriorate. That includes modeling how emissions could affect surrounding areas, including nearby residents, farmland and the river. The review does not require a full environmental impact statement or consider broader issues such as traffic, property values or the project’s economic costs and benefits. Instead, the focus is on whether the facility meets applicable air quality requirements. “The purpose of air permitting is to ensure that a facility is in compliance with the federal and state air quality standards,” Fletcher said. “And so, this puts limits on their operating hours and how much emissions they can emit during their operation. Make sure that there are proper controls in place to make sure that they have all the emission control requirements and things like that in place to ensure that we don’t impact the air quality negatively in the air.” The state received Monarch’s application in April and revised it in May. The public comment period is now underway, with comments due Oct. 30. A virtual public meeting is scheduled for Oct. 29. Copyright 2026 WSAZ. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: - The system pairs a swappable main battery with a 77-kWh range-extension battery to improve battery utilization and lower fleet operating costs. - CATL plans to have 900 heavy-duty truck battery swap stations operating by the end of 2026 and expand to 2,000 by 2027. CATL (HKEX: 3750) has unveiled a dual-electric range extension battery for heavy-duty trucks, pairing a swappable main battery with an independent on-board battery as it expands its push in freight electrification. The world's largest EV battery maker introduced the system in Beijing on Tuesday, alongside upgrades to its Qiji battery-swapping system aimed at reducing fleets' energy replenishment and battery costs. The system consists of 2 independent battery systems: a standardized, chassis-mounted swappable main battery and a 77-kWh range-extension battery behind the cab. The latter supports 3C charging and provides backup power. Drivers of conventional battery-swapping trucks typically return to swap stations with about 30% charge remaining to avoid running out of power en route, leaving part of their leased battery capacity unused, CATL said. With the backup battery, the system can increase the main battery's depth of discharge (DOD) from about 70% to more than 95%, allowing trucks to return to a swap station with less than 5% charge remaining in the main battery. The system can switch power delivery to the range-extension battery within milliseconds, maintaining uninterrupted power and providing redundancy under demanding operating conditions, the company said. It uses what CATL calls a "1+X" architecture. The main battery remains standardized for compatibility with the Qiji swapping network, while the range-extension battery can be tailored to requirements such as low-temperature performance, high energy density or high power. The 2 battery systems can be upgraded independently. The range-extension battery stays with the vehicle as an on-board asset, while the main battery can be leased flexibly according to seasonal freight demand, helping fleets reduce rental expenses during idle periods. Alongside the new system, Qiji introduced the 260# and 300# standardized swappable batteries, with capacities of 432 kWh and 513 kWh, respectively, complementing its existing 75# battery. The new-generation Qiji station can complete a battery swap in 5 minutes and reduces construction costs by 10%, CATL said. It requires no excavation pit and can be deployed in as little as 5 days. The company also changed the billing method for its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) offering, charging customers for net energy charged rather than energy discharged, allowing them to retain the benefits of regenerative braking. The change can reduce per-kWh battery rental costs for users on basic plans by up to 20%, further improving the economics of operating electric heavy-duty trucks, according to CATL. The company plans to have 900 heavy-duty truck battery-swap stations operating by the end of 2026 and expand to 2,000 by 2027. Its long-term goal is to deploy 10,000 stations across China with partners. Agreements covering 13,000 vehicles were signed at the event, with orders for battery-swapping products from major logistics companies including SF Holding and China Postal Express & Logistics. The launch comes amid a rapid increase in new energy vehicle (NEV) penetration in China's heavy-duty truck market. New energy heavy-duty trucks accounted for 50% of the segment in September, up from 29% a year earlier, according to China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) analysis of compulsory traffic insurance data. CATL launched its Qiji Energy heavy-duty truck battery-swapping solution in June 2023 and introduced the 75# standardized swappable truck battery in May 2025, expanding its presence in logistics. On June 30 this year, the company signed a strategic cooperation agreement with J&T Express to provide swappable batteries, swap-station equipment, and operation and maintenance services for more than 5,000 heavy-duty trucks. Beyond the dual-electric range extension system, CATL also unveiled truck batteries for different transport applications, including ultra-light and ultra-thin packs mounted behind the cab, as well as chassis-mounted batteries for short-haul and long-haul operations.

Documenter Melina Jimenez sat in on a presentation at the latest meeting for the Sweetwater Community Planning Group. The battery energy storage systems, or BESS, use rechargeable batteries to store excess electricity, mostly from the electric grid, solar panels or wind turbines. They are a tool used to help with reliable energy, though communities nationwide have raised concerns about fire risks, water and air contamination and impacts on property values. A county proposal aims to set zoning, safety, development and decommissioning standards for storage facilities in unincorporated San Diego. The item will come before the Board of Supervisors for consideration next year. — Written by Brisa Karow, Documenter and freelance reporter

artigo.texto: 3.75 MWh fail-safe system provides energy resilience and grid support at Buffalo's 105-unit affordable housing apartment building while helping lower energy costs for residents BUFFALO, N.Y., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Viridi, the industry leader in fail-safe distributed energy storage systems, and Good Carbon Co., today announced the deployment of a 3.75MWh lithium-ion battery energy storage system (BESS) at Peace Bridge Place, a 105-unit affordable housing apartment building in Buffalo, New York. The project is one of the largest indoor lithium-ion battery systems in an occupied residential building in the United States. At Peace Bridge Place, Viridi's RPSLinkIN indoor BESS is part of a broader clean energy strategy that includes geothermal heating & cooling, domestic hot water, and high efficient building envelope upgrades. The 3.75 MWh system is designed to provide extended backup power for the fully electrified building during outages, while also helping reduce demand on the local grid during peak periods. Good Carbon Co., which focuses on revitalizing multifamily properties in communities throughout Western New York, selected the system to strengthen energy resilience for residents and enable the property to enable flexible, grid-responsive energy management. "Energy is one of the biggest operating costs in multifamily housing, and how you manage it directly affects the long-term performance of a property," said Adam Serbert, CEO of Good Carbon Co. "At Peace Bridge Place, Viridi's battery and energy management technology will help us reduce peak demand, avoid higher-cost periods and participate in demand response programs. That means lower operating costs, new revenue opportunities and a stronger economic foundation for keeping the property affordable and well maintained. For us, this is not just about one building — it is about creating a model we can apply across future multifamily projects." Viridi's intelligent Energy Management System automatically stores and discharges electricity based on the needs of the fully electrified property and the local grid. It allows Peace Bridge Place to reduce electricity demand during peak periods and respond to utility signals when additional grid flexibility is needed, while providing greater energy resilience for residents. By reducing peak demand and participating in demand response programs, the system can help lower the property's energy costs while creating new revenue opportunities. The New York State Energy Research and Development Agency (NYSERDA) is providing support to Good Carbon Co. for the Peace Bridge Place project through its Future Grid Challenge. The Peace Bridge Place project is a National Grid pilot focused on integrating flexible, grid-responsive technologies into its distribution network. Viridi's energy storage and energy management technology will work in coordination with EnergyHub's Edge Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS), enabling the property to respond to National Grid signals during periods of peak electricity demand. "Peace Bridge Place demonstrates how forward-thinking energy storage solutions can ensure New York's multifamily buildings are meeting the energy needs of its residents while creating a more reliable and resilient electric grid," said Doreen M. Harris, President and CEO, NYSERDA. "Projects like this embody NYSERDA's mission to spur innovation that drives New York toward a clean energy future." Distributed across seven battery rooms, the 3.75MWh system is integrated with Viridi's proprietary Energy Management System (EMS), which optimizes the property's electricity use while enabling it to respond to changing conditions on the local grid in two key ways: - Peak Shaving: As the building's grid energy draw approaches a monthly peak, the battery automatically discharges to keep demand below a target threshold, reducing peak demand and associated $/kW demand charges. - Seasonal Demand Response: During peak events, National Grid dispatch signals are delivered through EnergyHub's platform to Viridi's energy management system, which then coordinates the response across the building's battery and other energy systems. For participating residents, smart thermostat setpoints can be adjusted to "pre-cool" or "pre-heat" apartments before the event, enabling reduced HVAC consumption during the event while the battery discharges. Residents can opt out of individual events at any time. Together, these actions allow the property to reduce its net electricity demand while the local grid is under the greatest strain. Deploying lithium-ion battery storage indoors at this scale requires rigorous safety standards. The risk of thermal runaway — and its potential to propagate from cell to cell — has historically constrained where lithium-ion systems can be installed. The RPSLinkIN system is designed to address that challenge through Viridi's proprietary Fail-Safe Anti-Propagation architecture, a passive safety layer designed to prevent thermal runaway from spreading between cells. That safety architecture has undergone industry-standard testing designed to evaluate how battery systems behave during a thermal runaway event. During UL 9540A testing, a cell was intentionally driven into thermal failure to determine whether the event would spread to surrounding cells. Viridi's technology prevented cell-to-cell propagation, with no detectable release of heat, sparks, smoke, gas or flames. RPSLinkIN has also earned UL 9540 Listing from TÜV Rheinland, providing third-party certification of the complete energy storage system. "This project demonstrates what becomes possible when energy storage is designed to serve the building and the grid at the same time," said Jon M. Williams, CEO of Viridi. "Peace Bridge Place will now be able to reduce peak demand, respond when the grid needs support and strengthen resilience for the people who live there. artigo.texto: - On 16 October 2026, China Power International Development signed a BESS Services Framework Agreement with SPIC, covering fully integrated battery energy storage systems, related equipment and technical services through to 31 December 2028. - The paired Battery Cells Procurement Framework Agreement for Xinyuan Smart Storage with Guoning Technology points to a tightly coordinated supply chain approach for future BESS tenders within the SPIC Group. - Attention now shifts to how China Power International Development's expanded BESS framework with SPIC could influence the broader investment narrative around the stock. Spot opportunities around China Power International Development's BESS move by scanning a hand picked group of grid and storage players in our 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks. What Is China Power International Development's Investment Narrative? To own China Power International Development, you need to believe the group can turn a broad power portfolio into steadier earnings while shifting more value toward renewables and energy storage. The new BESS Services Framework Agreement with SPIC and the linked battery cell procurement deal give clearer visibility on project flow, but they also lock the business more tightly into capital heavy storage buildout where pricing, tender discipline and execution quality really matter over the next couple of years. In the short term, the key swing factors remain margin repair, interest coverage and how much cash high yield dividends absorb. Profit margins already compressed to 3% from 6.3% and interest payments are not well covered, even as the stock trades well below one internal fair value estimate and analysts expect strong earnings growth. The SPIC framework could support utilisation and demand for Xinyuan Smart Storage, yet it also raises questions about how much extra leverage or equity the group might eventually need to fund these projects at scale. artigo.texto: Group holds Lexington walkout against AI and data centers LEXINGTON, Ky. (WKYT) - A small but vocal group of Lexington residents is working to shape the rules before more data centers move in. The group, No AI in KY, welcomed speakers and singers Tuesday to show unity against artificial intelligence. Members describe reasons for walkout Reva Russell English, a member of No AI in KY, said singing was included because of a long history of using song as resistance in the United States and around the world. No AI in KY is not just an organization, but words members live by as artificial intelligence use grows daily. The group gathered outside the Lexington government center Tuesday, joining a nationally organized walkout against AI. English said the National Walkout to Freeze AI was organized by Irreplaceable. “We don’t have like a set location to walk out from so a lot of people did leave their jobs early or called out sick today,” English said. Moratorium approved, zoning changes ahead English said Lexington city leaders are listening. In early October, the council approved a one-year moratorium on new data centers. English said the fight is only beginning. During that time, leaders will strengthen the zoning ordinance text amendment, or ZOTA, to decide where and how centers can be built. “We’re going to be around the whole time when they build that new ZOTA and they build that new zone we’re going to make sure that they keep data centers in a way isn’t going to harm this place and its people,” English said. Students raise concerns about AI and creativity “I can only imagine what that will do to the next generation of artists and creatives and how their creative ability will be impacted and the thing is that we don’t know because it’s not been around long enough for us to know,” Mehta said. Mehta said AI does not just impair creativity — it plagiarizes it, using human work to mimic human creativity. He said that is why he is fighting against AI and data centers. English said the group wants more people to join its effort. “It’s a fight for the future, it’s a fight for our lives and we would like more people to be a part of it with us,” English said. The Urban County Council will hear public comments on data centers at its 6 p.m. council meeting Thursday. Copyright 2026 WKYT. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: STL (Sterlite Technologies) has expanded its Neuralis Data Center portfolio with pre-terminated fiber trunk assemblies supporting fiber counts from 48 to 6,912. The new high-density cabling solutions are designed to help hyperscale and enterprise data centers accommodate growing bandwidth demands from AI, cloud computing and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. The launch addresses a key challenge for data center operators: increasing network capacity while reducing installation time and making better use of limited cable routing space. For European data center operators and infrastructure designers, the assemblies offer an approach to scaling optical connectivity without significantly expanding existing pathways, trays and conduits. High-density fiber for space-constrained data centers The portfolio includes two product families covering indoor data hall connectivity and larger-scale indoor/outdoor installations. STL’s indoor pre-terminated fiber trunk assemblies support 48 to 576 fibers, with cable diameters ranging from 5.8 mm to 12.2 mm. Designed for high-density MMC, MPO and LC terminations, the assemblies meet ANSI/ICEA S-83-596 requirements and are available with UL OFNP plenum or OFNR riser-rated cables. For campus, inter-building and inter-row connections, STL offers indoor/outdoor assemblies supporting 144 to 6,912 fibers. The highest-density version accommodates 6,912 fibers in a single cable with an outer diameter of 32 mm. These assemblies feature OFNR/LSZH jacketing and UL 1651-rated sunlight resistance, making them suitable for installations requiring outdoor exposure. Factory termination targets faster deployment Both product families are factory-terminated and 100% tested before delivery, reducing the need for on-site connector installation and helping operators accelerate network deployment. Connector options include MMC, MTP/MPO and LC, with Base-8, Base-12, Base-16 and Base-24 configurations to support different switch and patch-panel architectures. The assemblies are available with bend-insensitive ITU-T G.657.A2 single-mode fiber in 200 µm or 250 µm formats. Indoor versions also support OM4 multimode fiber for shorter-distance connections. STL has integrated its patented IBR rollable ribbon technology into both product families. The color-coded bonded ribbon design is intended to simplify fiber identification and improve splicing efficiency in high-fiber-count installations. Ultra Low Loss connector performance options are also available for applications with demanding optical loss budgets. Supporting AI infrastructure expansion The new assemblies reflect the growing importance of cable density and installation efficiency as data center operators expand optical infrastructure to support AI workloads. “Every data center customer we work with is trying to solve the same equation – more capacity, less time. That’s exactly what this extension of Neuralis portfolio is built around. Our Pre-Terminated Trunk Assemblies are designed for dense networks, they are pre-tested, ready to connect on arrival, and flexible. This is connectivity built for how data centers are actually being constructed today; high density, tight timelines, zero room for error”, said Dr Badri Gomatam, CTO, STL. The expanded portfolio gives operators additional options for increasing fiber capacity within existing physical infrastructure while limiting field termination work.

artigo.texto: Tanzania positions itself to become Africa’s carbon market hub DAR ES SALAAM: TANZANIA is positioning itself to become a leading carbon market hub in Africa by strengthening regulatory frameworks, transparency and investment mechanisms to ensure carbon trading contributes to economic growth, job creation and improved livelihoods. The Minister of State in the Vice-President’s Office (Union Affairs and Environment), Eng Hamad Yussuf Masauni, said this on October 22, 2026, when officially opening the Tanzania Carbon Market and Investment Forum 2026 in Dar es Salaam, held under the theme “One Day. One Market. One Shared Vision.” Masauni said the government aims to establish an integrity-driven carbon market that serves as a key instrument for national development through job creation, increased community income, investment attraction, forest conservation and the promotion of clean energy. He said the initiative aligns with the implementation of Tanzania’s National Development Vision 2050, emphasising that the success of the carbon market would not be measured solely by the number of projects established, but also by the quality of their outcomes, legal compliance, actual investments and tangible benefits reaching communities. “Tanzania has decided to become Africa’s hub for an integrity-driven carbon market, where every verified tonne of carbon translates into jobs for our youth, income for our villages, conserved forests, clean energy in our homes and capital to implement the National Development Vision 2050,” Masauni said. He added that, under the leadership of President Samia Suluhu Hassan, clean cooking energy is among the areas offering significant opportunities in carbon trading because of its potential to reach millions of households while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Masauni said the government recognises the potential of carbon market initiatives to link environmental conservation with economic opportunities, while ensuring that investments generate measurable benefits for local communities. Meanwhile, the Chief Executive Officer of the National Carbon Monitoring Centre (NCMC), Kathryn Kigaraba, said the institution plays a crucial role in supporting the development of Tanzania’s carbon market through scientific expertise, sound methodologies, transparency and robust monitoring and verification systems. Kigaraba said these mechanisms are essential to ensuring that carbon projects are properly recognised and developed, conducted transparently and generate benefits that contribute to Tanzania’s sustainable development. She added that science-based oversight and transparent reporting would help strengthen stakeholder and investor confidence while ensuring that carbon market activities support environmental conservation and improve people’s livelihoods.

artigo.texto: Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF, FRA:X0S) told investors it expects to generate its first commercial revenues from its sulfur battery technology in the current financial year, backed by a strengthened cash position and development agreements with major industrial and automotive partners. The company reported pro forma cash of £9.6 million at 30 June 2026, up from £4.1 million a year earlier, following an oversubscribed £9.9 million net fundraising. Its adjusted EBITDA loss widened to £4.4 million from £4.1 million, although this was 10.4% better than analyst expectations. Total income slipped to £2.5 million from £2.7 million but exceeded consensus forecasts by 17.1%, with government grants and R&D incentives covering 63.2% of research expenditure. Customer revenue fell to £49,000 from £912,000 following the completion of a legacy energy storage project. Gelion has since secured a £2 million funded development agreement with Japan's Mitsui Kinzoku and a co-funded proof-of-concept programme with a top-five global automotive manufacturer. Both are expected to contribute modest commercial revenue in FY27 as the company advances its Nano-Encapsulated Sulfur technology towards customer qualification and manufacturing scale-up. Chief executive Matt Wood said the company was moving "from technology validation towards customer programmes, qualification and scale-up", with a focus on converting technical progress into commercial adoption. "2026 has been an important transition year for Gelion, marked by continued advancements in our sulfur battery technology and growing commercial validation of our NES™ cathode platform through partnerships with leading global industrial and battery sector participants," Wood said. He added: "Supported by a strengthened balance sheet, strong partner engagement and a clear focus on commercial execution, we are confident in our strategy and the opportunity ahead. "As we move from technology validation towards customer programmes, qualification and scale-up, our focus remains on converting our technological leadership into commercial adoption and long-term shareholder value." Gelion also noted on Wednesday that it is winding down its Integration Solutions business and pursuing the sale of its Battery Minerals subsidiary to focus investment on sulfur cathode materials designed for use in existing battery manufacturing infrastructure.

artigo.texto: This article was funded by LebTown donors as part of our Civic Impact Reporting Project. North Lebanon Township supervisors unanimously agreed to advertise an ordinance regulating data centers at their monthly meeting Oct. 19. The ordinance, which places the use in the industrial zoning district, will be up for adoption at the board’s Nov. 16 meeting. Solicitor Amy Leonard explained that the 34-page ordinance was modeled after multiple other municipalities’ data center ordinances and was revised based on comment from the township planning commission. The township’s existing code of ordinances does not address data centers specifically, meaning a developer could make a case to construct a data center in any zoning district. If passed, this ordinance would limit data centers to industrial land and subject them to aesthetic, dimensional, landscaping, screening, and noise/vibration requirements. In addition to the ordinance’s requirements, Leonard said, data centers would also need to follow general requirements for the industrial zoning district. Requirements for data centers laid out by the ordinance include a water feasibility study, a drought response plan, minimum 20-acre lot size, maximum height of 45 feet plus up to 15 feet of roof-mounted equipment, 100 or more feet of landscape buffer, and a sound and vibration study. However, this list is not all-inclusive. This comes alongside increased demand for data centers both locally and nationwide. Residents have voiced concerns about utility impacts, noise and vibration, and pollutants, including in the case of a proposed data center in South Annville Township that was ultimately scrapped. Throughout the county, multiple municipalities have recently implemented ordinances governing data centers. artigo.texto: Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF, FRA:X0S) shares rose over 12% to 18p on Wednesday morning after the sulfur battery technology company reported that its £9.6 million pro forma cash balance and new partnerships with global automotive manufacturers strengthened its position to commercialise its battery technology. Gelion reported total income of £2.5 million for the year to 30 June 2026, down from £2.7 million a year earlier but 17.1% above analyst consensus, mainly reflecting government grants and research and development tax incentives. The adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation loss widened to £4.4 million from £4.1 million in the previous financial year, although it was 10.4% better than analyst consensus as the company continued investing in technology development, partnerships and commercialisation. Pro forma cash and cash equivalents stood at £9.6 million, with no debt, and were 21.1% above analyst consensus, providing funding for the next phase of development. Operational progress included expanded collaborations with TDK Corporation, QinetiQ UK, Nissan Technical Centre Europe and the University of Oxford, alongside development work on its nano-encapsulated sulfur technology, designed as a lower-cost alternative to critical minerals used in lithium-ion battery cathodes. After the financial year ended, Gelion signed a £2 million funded development and scale-up agreement with Mitsui Kinzoku and agreements with two major global automotive manufacturers to test its sulfur cathode technology for electric vehicle batteries. The company also reported that independent testing by the National Laboratory of the Rockies showed cells retained 92% of reference capacity at a 20-fold higher cycling rate, supporting further evaluation for defence, aerospace and drone applications. Chief executive Matt Wood said the company was moving from technology validation towards customer programmes, qualification and scale-up, with a focus on converting its technology into commercial adoption. Gelion said it had strengthened its intellectual property portfolio with six new patent grants across the US, Europe and Asia, and will hold an investor presentation on Thursday, 22 October.

artigo.texto: A U.K. homeowner shopping for battery storage got sticker shock after receiving a quote where the installation cost was about as much as the hardware. The homeowner wanted to add a Fogstar 32-kWh battery paired with a 6-kW inverter package, and they got a quote for £6,999. After finding what appeared to be the same hardware online for £3,995, the shopper turned to Reddit to ask whether the roughly £3,000 installation charge was standard. Here's what to know On Reddit, the homeowner said the plan was for a battery-only setup at a three-bedroom semi. They were aiming for a larger battery because a heat pump was expected to be installed. "I can see on the fogstar website that this combo is available for £3995 so a 3 grand installation cost feels steep?" the original poster wrote. One commenter joked, "Must be nice to make £3k for one days work." Battery storage can be one of the most effective ways to improve energy independence and keep a home better protected during outages. A system sized with a future heat pump in mind can also help cut energy costs by storing power for use when it is needed most. Anyone comparing quotes for battery storage can explore EnergySage to learn about home battery storage options, including competitive installation estimates. EnergySage has teamed up with electrification brand Qmerit to help homeowners get the best price on home battery storage solutions. A reply agreed the price looked elevated and focused on the system layout, saying, "It does seem a little bit high." More background Another Redditor offered a price comparison, writing, "I'm getting 2x16kwh fogstar with 6kw inverter for £4900." While that example does not represent an exact match, it gave the original poster a much lower installed price for roughly the same total storage capacity and inverter size. That led the OP to note that Equivolt also worked in their area, suggesting they should get another quote. Adding battery storage to a house is a major investment, and comparing options can have a meaningful impact on the experience. In this case, the homeowner went to Reddit and got a good lay of the land, but that is likely not enough in itself. What can be done? Getting multiple quotes from competing companies and understanding all the charges is important. Also, separating hardware costs from installation costs can make a quote easier to understand and compare. In this case, the homeowner was able to compare a £3,995 online bundle with a £6,999 installed quote, making the labor and other installation-related charges easier to examine. One clear takeaway is to gather more than one estimate. The original poster had initially been looking for a "sense check," and the shared quotes that commenters provided gave them a concrete baseline to pursue. For shoppers who want backup power but are not ready for a whole-home setup, Pila offers strong battery backup options. Pila's plug-and-play batteries are priced at a fraction of what a whole-home backup system would cost. Much of the discussion centered on sharing quotes and suggesting that the poster get more than one quote. It is hard to judge a deal from just one quote, and this battery shopper has some calling to do. Where can I learn more? artigo.texto: Oct 21 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies building data centers should pay a "dividend" to the communities where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular. "I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post. Data centers fueling the rise of AI have become a political flashpoint in communities across the country given the high quantities of water and power they require, with opposition uniting voters across ideological lines. The Trump administration, which has prioritized rapid AI development to compete with China, has also noted the shifting voter sentiment. "New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data (centers) are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," Trump said in his post. Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centers in order to protect consumers from rising bills. AI giant Anthropic and Elon Musk have laid out blueprints in recent days for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom. The creator of Claude models said over the weekend it is committing 5% of its shares to a new fund for the "public good", while Musk pledged on Monday to give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America", arguing for such direct distributions as the burgeoning sector faces public scrutiny. (Reporting by Akanksha Khushi in Bengaluru; Editing by Tom Hogue and Jan Harvey)

artigo.texto: CATL expands battery-swapping footprint with Huawei Huawei‘s intelligent automotive component subsidiary, Yinwang (or Newcool), has entered into a strategic partnership with CATL and its battery-swapping service arm, Chocolate Swap. The agreement, signed on October 19, 2026, aims to integrate Huawei’s intelligent driving solutions with CATL’s “Chocolate” battery-swapping ecosystem. According to CATL and Yinwang, the collaboration focuses on creating a seamless, automated energy replenishment experience. By connecting vehicle, station, and cloud data, EVs equipped with Huawei’s intelligent driving systems will be able to autonomously locate, enter, and align with battery-swapping stations. The process is designed to be highly efficient, enabling a full battery swap in just 99 seconds before the vehicle autonomously departs. Roadmap for 2027 According to industry reports, the partnership is already accelerating the development of its first wave of vehicles. A total of five battery-swapping models are planned for launch in 2027. The inaugural model will be a product under the Epicland brand, a collaborative brand between Dongfeng and Huawei. Additionally, GAC and Huawei’s collaborative brand, Aistaland, has also incorporated battery-swapping models into its future product planning. While CATL has established a robust network of 2,520 “Chocolate” battery-swapping stations across 200 cities as of September 29, 2026, the adoption of its battery-swapping technology in consumer-facing passenger vehicles has remained limited. By integrating with Huawei’s intelligent driving ecosystem, CATL gains a powerful gateway to reach a broader range of mainstream passenger vehicles. For Huawei, the partnership completes its intelligent service ecosystem by adding a vital energy replenishment scenario, further enhancing the convenience of its intelligent driving solutions. Market Context and Challenges The move comes as CATL faces increasing pressure in the power battery market, with third-quarter net profit growth slowing and gross margins tightening. By shifting from a simple battery supplier to a provider of full-lifecycle energy services, CATL aims to deepen its ties with automakers and secure long-term revenue streams beyond initial battery sales. So far, all of China’s major traditional state-owned car manufacturers (FAW, Dongfeng, Changan, SAIC, GAC, BAIC) have launched battery-swap models based on CATL’s Chocolate technology. GAC and Dongfeng, mentioned above, already had their own battery-swapping models even before this latest CATL-Huawei partnership. GAC’s model has already gone on sale, while Dongfeng’s has appeared in the regulatory filings. CATL has so far built 2,520 battery-swapping stations and aims to have built 3,000 by 2026. This week, it also announced plans to build 900 Qiji battery-swapping stations for heavy goods vehicles by the end of the year. With its ever-expanding battery-swapping network, CATL is gradually becoming an energy supplier.

artigo.texto: O RN não pode perder a corrida dos data centers No próximo dia 23, a FIERN sediará a Data Center Conference 2026, reunindo investidores, empresas de tecnologia, especialistas e autoridades em torno de um dos setores mais disputados da economia global. O momento não poderia ser mais oportuno para o Rio Grande do Norte. Enquanto a inteligência artificial amplia a demanda por processamento e armazenamento de dados em escala sem precedentes, estados brasileiros começam a definir suas estratégias para atrair um mercado que movimentará bilhões de reais nos próximos anos. Levantamento da consultoria Innova Assuntos Públicos identificou 20 projetos de lei relacionados a data centers em 11 assembleias legislativas entre 2025 e outubro de 2026. Dos projetos mapeados, nove possuem caráter restritivo, sete são favoráveis aos empreendimentos, dois combinam incentivos e exigências e dois são neutros. O que antes era visto quase exclusivamente como um tema restrito a uma parcela pequena da sociedade ganha impulso e chega aos legislativos com visões de mundo diferentes e mostra o quanto a temática ganha centralidade nas decisões dos governos daqui para a frente. Ceará e Goiás, os únicos a transformar propostas em legislação, optaram por oferecer previsibilidade regulatória. O Ceará criou um modelo de licenciamento escalonado de acordo com o porte e o potencial poluidor dos empreendimentos. Goiás combinou incentivos, zonas prioritárias e procedimentos simplificados. Em ambos os casos, a mensagem que deixam é que investimentos dessa magnitude procuram regras estáveis e segurança jurídica. O Rio Grande do Norte ainda não possui uma política ampla para atração de data centers, mas deu um passo importante ao aprovar, por meio do Conema, uma regulamentação específica para o licenciamento ambiental do setor. Ao estabelecer critérios conforme a potência instalada e diferenciar exigências de acordo com o sistema de refrigeração utilizado, o Estado sinaliza que compreende o momento, mas ainda precisa que o tema se consolide com uma legislação específica que dê a segurança jurídica para quem pretende investir. Essa discussão ganha importância adicional diante da reforma tributária. Durante décadas, a disputa por investimentos esteve associada aos incentivos de ICMS. Esse instrumento perderá relevância nos próximos anos. A vantagem competitiva passará a depender de fatores mais duradouros, como rapidez no licenciamento, segurança energética, disponibilidade hídrica e qualidade da infraestrutura. Em outras palavras, os estados deixarão de competir por benefícios fiscais e a previsibilidade do licenciamento e regras relacionadas à água e à energia terão mais relevância. Às empresas também cabe entrarem cedo nesses debates, com dados e diálogo com as comunidades locais para a construção de regras mais favoráveis, mostrando a importância desses investimentos para o desenvolvimento do Estado. A liderança na geração eólica, o crescimento da energia solar, os projetos de hidrogênio verde e a posição estratégica na agenda da transição energética colocam o RN em uma situação privilegiada. A Data Center Conference será uma excelente oportunidade para fazer esse debate de forma madura. O RN precisa definir a estratégia. Porque, na economia digital, os investimentos tendem a chegar primeiro aos lugares que sabem exatamente o que querem. Os que se planejam costumam colher os resultados antes dos demais. Quem hesitar correrá o risco de assistir ao futuro passar pela janela.

artigo.texto: The world’s largest battery maker, CATL, has combined swappable battery packs with an onboard range-extender system to solve range anxiety in heavy-duty electric trucks. Drivers on long-haul routes often pull into stations while their packs still hold substantial power. The new dual-battery design runs two independent energy systems inside a single vehicle. This allows haulers to use virtually all stored power without the risk of stopping short of a charger. “The combination of the dual-electric range extension battery and QIJI battery swapping offers the best solution for electrifying heavy-duty trucks,” said Jesse Yang, CEO of QIJI Energy. The core technology uses a setup called a “1+X” architecture. Instead of relying on a conventional fuel-burning combustion generator for range extension, the powertrain splits work between two entirely electric battery packs. The main battery rests in the truck chassis and is built to be swapped out quickly at robotic stations. Behind the driver cabin sits a secondary 77 kWh battery capable of 3C fast-charging, which acts as a permanent onboard reserve. Steady flow of torque Having two separate power systems fundamentally changes how the vehicle manages electricity. In conventional operations, drivers rarely use the bottom 30 percent of their battery capacity. With a secondary pack always on board to act as an energy cushion, the main battery can safely be drained much deeper. More from Transportation See All Drivers can run the primary chassis pack down until less than 5 percent of its charge remains. This lifts the total depth of discharge from roughly 70 percent to more than 95 percent, squeezing far more work out of every charge cycle. When the main chassis battery finally runs dry, onboard switching electronics reroute power to the cabin-mounted backup within milliseconds. Because this transfer occurs almost instantly, the electric drive motors maintain a steady flow of torque without any drop in vehicle momentum. Engineers can also modify each battery system independently because the two circuits operate separately. The swappable chassis unit stays standard to match charging docks, but the backup pack can be tailored to specific driving conditions. To handle diverse logistics duties For instance, operators working in sub-zero regions can install cells with cold-resistant chemistry. Other trucks can carry alternative backup variants focused on ultra-high energy density or extra power delivery for difficult routes. Physical swapping equipment has also been expanded to handle diverse logistics duties. Alongside the existing 75# unit, the system introduces two higher-capacity standardized blocks: a 432 kWh pack known as the 260# and a 513 kWh pack known as the 300#. Automated bays complete the physical swapping process in five minutes, maintaining a mechanical success rate of 99.99 percent on the first attempt. The dual-pack setup extends into asset accounting as well. The backup unit remains with the truck as a permanent vehicle asset. “Aside from the dual-electric solution, CATL also introduced a new lineup of heavy-duty truck batteries tailored to different vehicle configurations and operating requirements at the event,” concluded the Chinese giant in a press release. “The lineup includes rear-mounted ultra-light and ultra-thin batteries for weight- and space-sensitive applications, as well as chassis-mounted solutions for short-haul and long-haul operations.”

artigo.texto: Snyder outlines plans for 7th term, addresses data center ad Incumbent discusses school funding and data center regulations ahead of Nov. 3 election WAUSAU, Wis. (WSAW) -Representative Pat Snyder says he has a plan in mind if he is reelected to a seventh term representing the 85th District, which covers Wausau and Weston. School funding Snyder has previously worked in the Assembly to get more funding for special education departments at public schools. That effort did not pass. Snyder said he is confident it will pass if he can bring it back to the state Assembly if reelected. Snyder and his opponent, John Kroll, agree there should be more funding for public schools. Snyder said there needs to be a plan in place and that the policy should not be generalized. “When they say fully funded, they don’t ever have a number of what fully, because I asked the three when we had our executive session, what is fully funded? Well, just enough to make sure everything’s covered. We got to have a number because the taxpayers would like to know,” Snyder said. Data centers Snyder’s view on data centers differs from Kroll’s. While Kroll does not want data centers, Snyder said they are an inevitability given how much media is consumed. Snyder said that does not mean he is against regulations and protecting Wisconsin’s nature. He said local governments have been doing the right thing by making data centers follow their set rules. “If you do come in, get the local control taken care of, it has to be enclosed water and it has to be your own generation. You bring your power and you can’t put the excess or taxpayers to be anywhere troubled by that,” Snyder said. Response to political ad One political ad running against Snyder says he gave $2 million to a data center near Milwaukee. Snyder said that is not true. He said when utility rates go up, the Public Service Commission sets and approves the rate increases, not legislators. “When they say that I gave $2 million for Microsoft down in Southeast Wisconsin, that was the 2023 budget that Governor Evers signed and passed. He could have vetoed that,” Snyder said. Snyder helped propose a bill that would put restrictions on data centers in 2025. He originally voted no. Amendments included an AI review council, which earned his yes vote. Snyder said technology growth should be possible in Wisconsin, but done in a responsible and controlled way. artigo.texto: October 21, 2026 Introduction Critics often argue that data centers bring large buildings and heavy power demand but few jobs, and on its face the argument is easy to accept.[i] A finished hyperscale campus can run with a relatively small permanent staff.[ii] Yet a count of the people working inside a finished facility captures only a fraction of the sector’s economic footprint. Before a campus opens, electricians, ironworkers, and engineers spend years building it, and specialized manufacturers supply the power and cooling equipment that runs it.[iii] Once it opens, operators buy electricity, maintenance, and security from Iowa businesses and replace servers and other hardware every few years.[iv] That activity matters more in Iowa than in most states. Iowa ranks among the Midwest’s leaders in data center capacity, both in facilities already operating and in projects still in development.[v] National research finds that counties with data centers see “positive effects on total employment, construction employment, establishments, payroll, tax returns, adjusted gross income, and wages.”[vi] This report estimates how much Iowa employment, income, and output these data center lifecycles support. It first documents the size, location, and development of Iowa’s data center sector. It then estimates the direct investment owners and operators have made to date and have announced for the coming years. Common Sense Institute then uses the Regional Economic Models, Inc. (REMI) Tax-PI+ model to simulate the direct, indirect, and induced effects of two phases of spending—construction and initial equipment, and ongoing operations and equipment replacement. Finally, the report opens the door to future CSI research on the sector’s tax impacts, community investments, and resource demands. Key Findings - Data center owners and operators have invested or announced at least $53 billion in Iowa buildings and equipment through 2031 (table 1). - Investments in Iowa data centers to date total an estimated $15.1 billion, or about $4,700 for every Iowan. - Announced investments from 2027 through 2031 would add an additional $38.0 billion. At an average of $7.6 billion per year, these direct investments represent roughly 2.8% of Iowa’s current annual GDP. - Ongoing operating and replacement spending totaled an estimated $4.4 billion in 2026, and announced projects would add about $10.6 billion a year by 2031. - Announced construction and initial equipment purchases would support about 12,775 jobs by 2031, counting direct, indirect, and induced effects. - From 2027 through 2031, they would add about $10.4 billion to GDP and $6.3 billion to personal income (table 3). - The ongoing operations of Iowa’s data centers produce more sustained jobs and more economic activity than their initial construction. - Operations at existing data centers support an estimated 12,647 Iowa jobs in 2026, or nearly three jobs for every direct job (tables 4 and 6). - Once operating, announced projects would support about 29,597 jobs in 2031. From 2027 through 2031, they would add about $18.5 billion to GDP and $9.0 billion to personal income (table 4). - Job gains reach well beyond technology, to electricians, construction workers, retail workers, teachers, and motor vehicle operators (table 5). - Data centers pay more than other employers for the same job titles, from 12% more for security officers to almost 100% more for electrical engineers (figure 4). - Average annual pay in the industry that includes data centers reached $125,759 in 2025, nearly double the $63,469 average for all Iowa workers. - Relative to its population, Iowa is the Midwest’s data center leader, with more operating capacity per resident than any other state in the region (figure 1). - Iowa’s data centers have 71.8 megawatts (MW) of operating capacity per 100,000 residents. Megawatts measure how much electricity a facility can draw at once, which is the most reliable gauge of a data center’s size. - Iowa ranks second in the Midwest in total operating capacity (2,324 MW), behind only Ohio. Including planned projects, it ranks fourth in total capacity and second per capita, behind only Indiana. - Iowa’s data center sector is on track to more than triple in size by 2031 (table 1). - Announced projects would add 5,257 MW to today’s 2,324 MW of operating capacity in about five years. Building what exists today took more than two decades (figure 3). Iowa’s Data Center Landscape This section describes Iowa’s data center sector and what its jobs pay. It begins with the size, location, and development of the state’s data center facilities and compares Iowa with the rest of the Midwest. It then compares pay at data centers with pay at other employers. Operating capacity—facilities already in service—is shown in blue at the base of each bar. Planned capacity, representing projects in development or under construction, is shown in red above it. Cleanview provides the data.[vii] Planned capacity figures for all states are a snapshot. Additional projects will likely be announced or finalized in the coming years, which would raise total planned megawatts across the region. At the same time, these figures assume no currently planned projects are canceled or indefinitely delayed. Figure 1. Only Ohio, Indiana, and Illinois rank higher, at 25,759 MW, 16,837 MW, and 9,962 MW, respectively, and all three have much larger economies. Iowa stands out more on operating capacity alone. artigo.texto: Innovorbs Technologies announced a new AI data center infrastructure practice on October 22, 2026, from Houston, Texas. According to coverage on citybiz and citybuzz, the offering targets enterprises and IT service firms that want to build private AI capacity on-premises or in colocation space, rather than renting every GPU hour from a hyperscaler. Innovorbs describes itself as a global managed service provider (MSP) and IT solutions company. Tayyab Muhammad, its CEO and founder, is the named executive on the release. The practice covers GPU-cluster infrastructure end to end, from back-end fabrics and storage networks to compute, cooling, automation, and observability. The timing fits a wider hardware pattern. Server demand keeps climbing as agentic workloads spread, a trend we covered in TrendForce’s server CPU shipment forecast. Buyers who commit to that hardware now need people who can wire it, cool it, and keep it running. Innovorbs is pitching itself as one of those people. One caution before the detail. The announcement lists technologies and design patterns, but the available coverage names no customers, no cluster sizes, no performance results, no contract values, and no prices. This analysis covers what the practice says it does, what that scope implies, and what buyers should ask before signing anything. Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. What Innovorbs Announced in Houston The announcement dated October 22, 2026 introduces an AI Data Center Infrastructure practice. Its audience is split in two. One group is enterprises that want AI capacity inside their own walls or inside a colocation cage. The other is IT service firms that build and run that capacity for their own clients and need a partner for the hard network and facility work. The headline wording needs a flag. Some summaries of the story use the phrase enterprise GPU deployments. The press-release title itself refers to GPU clusters and private AI deployments, so we treat the first phrase as a paraphrase, not an official product name. The scope reads like a bill of materials for a modern training or inference pod. It spans six areas: back-end fabrics, front-end and storage networks, compute, cooling, automation, and observability. That breadth matters more than any single item. Most failed GPU rollouts stall at the seams between those layers, where a network team, a storage team, and a facilities team each assume another group owns the problem. An MSP that bills across all six areas can, in theory, own those seams. Whether Innovorbs does so in practice depends on delivery details the release does not share. Still, the structure of the offer tells us how the company wants to be judged: as an integrator of a whole cluster, not a reseller of boxes. Why Enterprises Want Private AI Capacity Private AI capacity appeals for reasons that have little to do with fashion. Data residency rules, predictable cost at steady utilization, and tighter control over model weights and training data all push some buyers toward owned or colocated hardware. Others simply want guaranteed access to accelerators when cloud quotas run thin. The trade is operational burden. A rented instance hides the fabric, the cooling loop, and the parallel file system behind an API. Owning the cluster exposes every one of them. A company that has run web servers for twenty years can still struggle with a lossless Ethernet fabric that drops a single class of traffic and stalls an entire training job. That gap creates the market Innovorbs is chasing. Enterprise IT teams rarely employ engineers who tune congestion control for collective communication libraries. They also rarely employ facilities staff who have designed liquid cooling for racks at the density GPUs demand. An MSP can sell that expertise as a service, and the release positions the new practice as exactly that. Large buyers have also watched the supply chain tighten. Our earlier look at cloud capex and the memory shortage outlook showed how much money hyperscalers are committing to AI hardware. Smaller enterprises compete for the same components, which makes experienced integrators more valuable. Back-End Fabrics: RoCEv2 Over 400G and 800G Ethernet The back-end fabric is the network that links GPUs to one another during training. It carries the heaviest and most latency-sensitive traffic in the building. According to the announcement, Innovorbs designs it around RoCEv2 (RDMA over Converged Ethernet, version 2) running on 400G and 800G Ethernet links. The company names a specific toolbox for making Ethernet behave like a lossless medium: PFC, ECN, DCQCN, and adaptive routing. It pairs those with rail-optimized, non-blocking Clos topologies. Each term maps to a real engineering decision, so it helps to unpack them. Lossless Ethernet Tuning in Plain Terms Priority Flow Control (PFC) pauses a single traffic class when a switch buffer fills, which prevents packet drops that RDMA handles poorly. Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) marks packets as queues build, so senders slow down before buffers overflow. DCQCN is the congestion control algorithm that reacts to those marks and throttles RDMA flows. Getting these three to cooperate is delicate. Set PFC thresholds too aggressively and a pause storm can freeze large parts of the fabric. Set ECN thresholds too late and queues overrun anyway. Adaptive routing adds a further layer by steering flows around hot links instead of relying on static hashing, which tends to collide when a few elephant flows dominate. A rail-optimized, non-blocking Clos design wires each GPU position in a server to its own leaf switch group, or rail. Traffic between the same GPU index across servers then stays within one rail where possible.
