artigo.texto: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains New research out of Texas shows how data centers are driving up pollution. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. So far, though, things are looking grim. Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality. “There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did.” In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025. That’s not set in stone, of course. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite. NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible. Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be. “There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

artigo.texto: da Agência iNFRA A EPE (Empresa de Pesquisa Energética) publicou a metodologia que será utilizada para calcular o custo marginal de referência, que servirá de base para a definição do preço-teto do leilão de baterias, marcado para dezembro. A nota técnica disponibilizada na segunda-feira (19) não apresenta os preços, uma vez que o dado é considerado estratégico para o certame, mas detalha como será feito o cálculo para os projetos. A metodologia utiliza um modelo de fluxo de caixa descontado, que avalia os investimentos, os custos e as receitas esperadas ao longo do empreendimento. A EPE calculará uma TEQ (Tarifa de Equilíbrio), isto é, a receita necessária para que o projeto cubra seus custos e remunere o capital, considerando os riscos e as condições financeiras adotadas. A EPE destaca que o preço-teto não será baseado apenas no custo inicial das baterias, mas também considerará os valores necessários para manter os sistemas de armazenamento aptos a operar conforme o contrato. Assim, o cálculo do custo marginal de referência considerará, além do investimento, as despesas com operação e manutenção, degradação das baterias, augmentation (reposição de componentes), tarifas de uso da rede, financiamento, seguros e tributos. Nacional x importado Quanto à divisão do leilão em dois, um para produto nacional e o outro que permite equipamentos importados, a nota técnica da EPE destaca que não se deve presumir que equipamentos nacionais serão mais caros ou mais baratos que os importados, uma vez que vários componentes entrarão na conta. “O efeito final decorrerá da avaliação conjunta dos custos, das condições de financiamento, dos prazos e dos riscos associados à cadeia de fornecimento”, diz o documento, que cita por exemplo que projetos nacionais podem ter condições diferenciadas de financiamento. Com a publicação da metodologia, a EPE agora deve avançar nos cálculos do custo marginal de referência, com as recomendações de preços-tetos. Isso será feito a partir informações dos projetos cadastrados, diligências técnicas, estudos nacionais e internacionais, referências de mercado e informações de fabricantes e bancos. A decisão final sobre o preço-teto caberá ao MME (Ministério de Minas e Energia).

artigo.texto: O Rio Grande do Norte tem nove empreendimentos em processo de licenciamento ambiental para instalação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, conhecidos pela sigla Bess. A tecnologia surge como alternativa para reduzir os cortes de geração de energia eólica e solar, problema que tem provocado perdas financeiras para empresas do setor e limitado o aproveitamento da capacidade instalada no Estado. O avanço dos projetos ocorre em meio à discussão sobre novas formas de armazenamento e comercialização de eletricidade no mercado brasileiro. Os pedidos estão sob análise do Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente do Rio Grande do Norte (Idema). Segundo o órgão, a maioria está vinculada a empreendimentos de geração renovável já existentes. A instalação das baterias permitirá armazenar parte da energia produzida em horários de menor consumo ou de restrição operacional e disponibilizá-la posteriormente, conforme as condições do sistema elétrico. O tema integra a programação da 7ª edição do Energy Storage Brasil, realizada na sede da Federação das Indústrias do Rio Grande do Norte (Fiern), em Natal, com atividades até esta sexta-feira, 23. O encontro reúne empresários, investidores, pesquisadores e representantes do poder público para discutir o desenvolvimento do mercado de armazenamento e sua relação com a expansão das fontes renováveis. Leia mais: FIERN recebe em novembro maior evento sobre produção industrial do RN De acordo com o Idema, o prazo para emissão das licenças varia conforme as características de cada empreendimento. “Depois que o processo é iniciado, o empreendedor recebe um Termo de Referência com um prazo de 120 dias para apresentar documentos e estudos ambientais necessários”, informou o instituto. A análise técnica começa após a entrega da documentação. “Após isso, o Idema vai analisar se os estudos atendem aos requisitos exigidos ou se serão solicitadas providências”, acrescentou o órgão. Caso sejam identificadas informações insuficientes, os responsáveis deverão complementar os estudos. A secretária-adjunta de Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado, Emília Casanova, explica que os sistemas podem apresentar dimensões semelhantes às de caixas eletrônicos ou ocupar estruturas do tamanho de contêineres. A configuração depende da potência, da capacidade de armazenamento e da finalidade de cada instalação. “Tudo vai depender da potência dessa bateria, que varia de acordo com cada projeto. Elas servem para armazenar a geração de energia excedente que pode ser despachada em um momento de pico e até mesmo vendida como energia extra para o mercado livre”, afirmou. O mercado livre permite que consumidores habilitados negociem diretamente a compra de eletricidade com geradores ou comercializadores, diferentemente do ambiente regulado, no qual o fornecimento segue regras tarifárias estabelecidas pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Para Emília Casanova, o aumento do interesse pelos projetos está relacionado à Resolução nº 01/2026 do Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema), aprovada em abril. A norma estabeleceu critérios para o licenciamento ambiental de sistemas BESS no Rio Grande do Norte. Leia mais: Alecrim celebra 115 anos com ações para fortalecer o comércio “Além do RN, apenas Rio Grande do Sul, Bahia, Ceará e Piauí possuem legislação que permite aos empreendedores solicitarem licença para esse tipo de armazenamento”, afirmou a secretária-adjunta. Segundo estimativas do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) apresentadas durante as discussões, o uso de baterias poderá reduzir entre 40% e 50% os cortes de geração, dependendo da localização e das condições operacionais. A tecnologia, entretanto, não elimina a necessidade de investimentos na rede de transmissão. Cortes de geração pressionam por investimentos O avanço do armazenamento ocorre em meio às perdas provocadas pelas restrições de geração. Em outubro, a Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE) registrou 568 manifestações de usinas potiguares interessadas em aderir ao mecanismo federal de ressarcimento por cortes de energia. São 347 empreendimentos eólicos e 221 solares, com compensações estimadas em R$ 780 milhões. O problema também compromete novos investimentos. Dados da Aneel mostram que 112 projetos solares tiveram autorizações revogadas no RN entre 2025 e setembro de 2026, envolvendo 5,63 gigawatts de potência prevista. Entre os fatores associados estão as restrições de escoamento e o excesso de oferta. No início de outubro, a Aneel aprovou novas regras para organizar os cortes obrigatórios de geração. A regulamentação estabelece critérios para a distribuição das restrições entre usinas e busca ampliar a previsibilidade das decisões operacionais. Leia mais: Procura pela primeira CNH cresce 86% no RN Para o diretor executivo da Associação Brasileira de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae), Fábio Monteiro, o desenvolvimento desse mercado poderá melhorar o aproveitamento da infraestrutura elétrica. “O armazenamento viabiliza a retomada do crescimento das renováveis, equilibra nosso sistema elétrico, reduz custos para o consumidor e otimiza o uso da rede de transmissões”, afirmou. A perspectiva de contratação de baterias também depende dos leilões federais previstos para dezembro. Segundo o ONS, o resultado desses certames será determinante para a contribuição efetiva da tecnologia na redução dos cortes de geração. Data centers ampliam demanda por energia limpa Além das baterias, o Rio Grande do Norte busca atrair investimentos em centros de processamento de dados. Segundo o Idema, três data centers de pequeno porte, com capacidade de até 40 megawatts, já receberam licenciamento ambiental. Um deles está em operação em Currais Novos, associado a um empreendimento de energia renovável. Não há pedidos registrados para instalações acima dessa capacidade. artigo.texto: In China, new-energy heavy truck sales have overtaken diesel truck sales. Just three years ago, new-energy heavy trucks accounted for only around 5% of sales, but electrification is spreading on the back of Chinese government support and lower transport costs. That contrasts with the United States and Europe, where heavy truck electrification remains in the single digits. Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL; 宁德时代), the world's largest battery maker, unveiled a new battery system aimed at long-haul heavy electric trucks as it moves to tap the long-distance transport market. On the 21st, according to China First Commercial Vehicle Network, about 65,800 heavy trucks were newly registered for insurance in China's domestic market in September, of which about 33,100 were new-energy vehicles. That was 50.3% of the total, a majority. While total heavy truck registrations fell 21% from a year earlier, registrations of new-energy vehicles rose 37%. Electrification of China's heavy truck market has accelerated rapidly in recent years. According to China First Commercial Vehicle Network, the sales share of new-energy heavy trucks surged from the 5% range in 2022–2023 to 13.6% in 2024 and 28.9% in 2025, then reached 38.1% in January–September this year. New energy includes not only pure electric vehicles but also Hydrogen Fuel Cell vehicles. CATL said, "In the heavy truck electrification market, the competition between internal combustion and electric vehicles is already over; from now on, the competition will be between EV technologies and business models." Compared with major global markets, China's pace of electrification stands out even more. According to the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT), in the first half of this year, zero-emission vehicles accounted for only 2.3% of new registrations of heavy trucks over 12 tons in the European Union (EU). In the United States, the figure was 0.34% last year. However, collection standards and periods differ by country. ◇ Chinese government to provide support in the 4 trillion won range for replacing old cargo trucks China's rapid electrification appears to reflect a combination of government support and improved economics. According to CATL, the Chinese government is building more than 3,000 heavy truck-dedicated charging and battery exchange facilities, centered on major metropolitan areas and expressways, to reach a 40% electrification rate for heavy trucks. It is also pushing plans to create a "carbon zero (0)" road transport network spanning a total of 30,000 kilometers. In particular, it allocated 22 billion yuan (about 4.3688 trillion won) from ultra-long-term special government bonds to support scrapping and replacing old commercial cargo trucks, and in some regions, the combined central and local government subsidies reportedly reach up to 220,000 yuan (about 43.68 million won). Electric trucks cost more upfront than diesel trucks, but their maintenance expense is relatively lower, so the longer the driving distance and the higher the utilization rate, the greater the potential cost savings. Adoption is said to be especially fast on short-haul, fixed routes such as mines, ports, steel mills, and construction sites. That is because fixed routes make it easier to secure charging infrastructure, and repeated vehicle operation can yield fuel cost savings. ◇ CATL unveils new "battery swap + auxiliary battery" system Against this backdrop, CATL has introduced a battery solution to improve long-haul efficiency for heavy electric trucks. On the 20th (local time), CATL held a product launch at the Shoudu International Exhibition and Convention Center in Shunyi District, Beijing, unveiling four new rechargeable batteries for heavy electric trucks and a new battery swap system. The new system combines a fixed auxiliary battery with the existing battery swap system. First, a main battery with up to 513 kWh capacity is mounted under the truck, and it can be replaced at a swap station in about five minutes without lengthy charging. CATL is operating battery swap systems on five major transport corridors: Guangdong–Shanghai, Chengdu–Wuhan, Changzhou–Yulin, Ningde–Xiamen, and the Hainan Island ring road. The fixed auxiliary battery is mounted behind the driver's seat. With a capacity of 77 kWh, it assists vehicle operation when the main battery's power is low. Because electric truck drivers, concerned about running out of charge, typically left about 30% remaining and then exchanged the battery, an auxiliary battery was added separately to improve this. CATL said this would allow the main battery to be used down to under 5% remaining, improving efficiency. CATL began mass production the same day as the product launch and signed cooperation agreements totaling 13,000 vehicles with logistics and transport companies including China Post, SF Express, STO Express, and YTO Express. It plans to expand battery exchange stations to 900 by the end of this year and 2,000 next year. In the long run, it aims to build 10,000 nationwide. ◇ The key is the economics of charging infrastructure Still, it is uncertain whether CATL's battery swap method will become mainstream for heavy electric trucks. Building battery exchange stations requires significant upfront investment expense, and if sufficient vehicle utilization is not secured, operating profitability risks falling. For vehicles from multiple manufacturers to use the same exchange facilities, battery specifications and vehicle designs must be standardized in cooperation with automakers. It will also face unavoidable competition from ultra-fast charging technology. In Europe and the United States, megawatt-class ultra-fast charging technology and infrastructure for heavy electric trucks are being developed. artigo.texto: Gentari and BYD Malaysia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore the deployment of BYD’s Flash Charging technology in Malaysia. The collaboration aims to expand ultra-fast EV charging infrastructure beyond showrooms, including along major intercity routes connecting key population centres. BYD’s Flash Charging technology is capable of delivering up to 1.5MW which would provide approximately 400km of driving range in just five minutes for compatible EVs under optimal conditions. The MoU was signed in Shenzhen, China, on 21 October 2026, between Gentari Group CEO Sushil Purohit and BYD Malaysia Managing Director Jacob Ma. The ceremony was witnessed by BYD Chairman Wang Chuanfu and BYD Vice President Liu Xueliang. Gentari and BYD to explore Flash Charging along major highways Under the agreement, Gentari and BYD Malaysia will jointly identify suitable locations for BYD Flash Charging stations, especially along key intercity corridors. Both companies will also assess power infrastructure requirements, battery energy storage systems (BESS), technical and commercial feasibility and potential operating models to support future deployment. The collaboration combines Gentari’s experience in developing and operating EV charging networks with BYD’s battery and high-power charging technology. Gentari Group CEO Sushil Purohit said, “Malaysia’s EV market is growing, but the next phase of adoption will depend on the quality, convenience and reliability of the charging experience.” He added, “Speed is one part of that equation. Drivers also need chargers in the right places, backed by reliable power and dependable operations. BYD’s leadership in EV, battery and high-power charging technology, combined with Gentari’s experience in developing and operating EV charging networks, gives us a strong foundation to strengthen Malaysia’s EV charging ecosystem and support wider adoption.” Gentari currently operates more than 600 EV charging points in Malaysia. Through its Gentari Go Roaming Hub, it also provides access to approximately 18,000 charging points across Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and India. BYD Vice President and General Manager of BYD Asia Pacific Auto Sales Division Liu Xueliang said, “Malaysia is an important market for BYD, and we are pleased to bring BYD Flash Charging here as part of our continued efforts to support the country’s growing EV adoption. Through our collaboration with Gentari, we look forward to exploring how this technology can contribute to a faster, more convenient and more connected charging experience for Malaysian EV users.” Meanwhile, BYD Malaysia Managing Director Jacob Ma said, “We are very excited to see this collaboration come together. As an EV leader, we believe our responsibility goes beyond delivering great vehicles. We want to give our customers the confidence to make the switch to electric and enjoy a truly seamless EV ownership experience. This is an important step for BYD in Malaysia, and we are proud to be part of the journey to build a stronger and more complete EV ecosystem for Malaysians.” Besides EV charging infrastructure, Gentari and BYD will also explore collaboration in renewable energy generation and energy storage. BYD Flash Charging stations already spotted in Malaysia As reported previously, BYD Malaysia had confirmed plans to introduce its Flash Charging technology in Malaysia, starting with Denza showrooms before expanding to other locations. The Flash Charging stations can deliver up to 1,500kW (1.5MW) of DC charging output. When paired with compatible EVs equipped with BYD’s second-generation Blade Battery technology, it can charge the battery from 10% to 70% in five minutes, or from 10% to 97% in just nine minutes. The chargers are also supported by BESS to manage the massive power demands without requiring the same level of power directly from the grid. Earlier this week, we spotted what appears to be BYD Flash Charging BESS equipment at Denza Glenmarie in Shah Alam. This was followed by another sighting at Denza Balakong, where the distinctive T-shaped overhead Flash charging structure and battery storage cabinets have already been installed. While the Flash Charging technology supports a maximum DC output of 1,500kW, compatible vehicles are required to achieve the highest charging speeds. The Denza Z9 GT is currently the only model available in Malaysia that supports BYD’s full Flash Charging capability. As shared by BYD Malaysia earlier, the Flash Charger will also be open to other BYD models and non-BYD EVs, up to their respective supported DC charging rates. BYD Malaysia has yet to reveal the official opening dates for the Flash Charging stations in Malaysia.

artigo.texto: Soluna Holdings, Inc., a green artificial intelligence (AI) data center developer, has entered into a definitive agreement with Applied Digital Corporation, a developer and operator of digital infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC), and AI cloud services, to establish a jointly owned company to develop a planned 50 MW critical IT data center for AI and HPC workloads at Project Dorothy 3 in Texas. Project Dorothy 3 is a planned data center co-located with Briscoe Wind, a 150 MW wind farm in Briscoe County. According to a press release, Dorothy 3 will draw power from both the wind farm and the grid. “We have said for a long time that the constraint in AI is energy access, not chips,” said John Belizaire, Soluna Chief Executive Officer. “We built Soluna to bring load to the generation, so the power would be ready when the demand arrived. Partnering with Applied at Dorothy 3 puts that strategy to work: our site and wind power, combined with a proven builder and operator of AI data centers. We look forward to completing the remaining steps, including the tax abatement process in Briscoe County, and to bringing this project forward with the local community.” Under the transaction agreement, Soluna will contribute a portion of the Dorothy 3 site, including land and power-related project assets, to the joint venture, with Applied Digital expected to provide capital to support development. Once the transactions outlined in the agreement are closed, Applied Digital will have a 51 percent interest in the joint venture, with Soluna holding the remaining 49 percent. It was also announced that Applied Digital’s ChronoScale Holdings Corporation, an accelerated compute platform supporting AI workloads, has signed a non-binding letter of intent to lease the facility. However, the companies stated that there can be no assurance that a definitive lease will be entered into on the terms set out in the letter of intent. The lease is also subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive documentation. In August, w.media reported that Texas Governor, Greg Abbott, directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to conduct a verification audit of all data center projects moving through ERCOT’s interconnection process. While Soluna and Applied Digital intend to power Dorothy 3 with a mix of wind and grid power, the companies didn’t share what that mix looks like or how much power will need to be sourced from the grid. ERCOT’s Batch Zero approval process applies only to projects requesting 75 MW or more from the grid, so it’s possible this project could bypass that process.

artigo.texto: Nigeria’s carbon market is gaining traction following the Federal Government’s first approvals for international carbon credit sales, a Nigerian carbon project developer, 9JA Carbon Trade, has said. The company said the approvals demonstrated that Nigeria’s carbon market framework was operational, as African governments, investors and project developers were urged to move beyond developing regulations to delivering projects and securing investment. The position was made known after 9JA Carbon Trade participated in the Carbon Markets Africa Summit (CMAS) 2026, held in Kigali, Rwanda, from October 14 to 15. The summit attracted about 600 delegates from 52 countries, representing more than 150 organisations, including over 50 investors and buyers. At a session on country readiness on October 14, Ibrahim Shelleng, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Climate Finance and Stakeholder Engagement, disclosed that Nigeria issued six letters of authorisation in March 2026 and two additional letters by September. A letter of authorisation is a formal government approval allowing carbon credits to be used internationally. Okpara, however, sought clarification on whether the Federal Government planned to enter into a bilateral carbon agreement with another country. The discussions formed part of broader efforts to strengthen Africa’s capacity to attract private capital into carbon markets and translate climate commitments into viable projects. At the close of the summit, the Acting Permanent Secretary of Rwanda’s Ministry of Environment, speaking on behalf of the Minister of Environment, outlined six areas of agreement among participants. The priorities included strengthening market integrity, building trust, ensuring that host communities benefited from carbon projects, increasing Africa’s share of the value generated by the market, improving regulatory implementation and securing long-term investment. Arakwiye noted that improved cookstoves accounted for approximately 87 per cent of Rwanda’s issued carbon credits, while agriculture had generated barely one per cent of voluntary carbon market credits over two decades. The International Air Transport Association told delegates that the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), a United Nations-backed scheme for international aviation, would become mandatory for airlines in 2027. Credits used under the scheme must carry a government letter of authorisation. Lukas Visek of the European Commission said a Commission proposal envisaged European Union purchases of carbon credits covering up to 260 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent between 2036 and 2040. Participants were also told that higher-quality credits were attracting better prices. artigo.texto: Global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Projected to Reach US$111 Million by 2032, at 18.0% CAGR 1.1 Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Summary Silicon-carbon anode materials for solid state batteries are high-capacity anode materials developed for solid-state and semi-solid lithium battery systems. They are typically based on nano-silicon, silicon oxide, graphite, and porous carbon, and are improved through composite structure design, surface coating, and interface stabilization. The materials are mainly used in automotive power batteries, high-end consumer electronics batteries, and next-generation high-safety energy storage batteries. The market is still in an early commercialization stage as solid state batteries move from sample validation and pilot projects toward small-scale production. Demand for silicon-carbon anode materials is increasing as automakers, battery manufacturers, and material companies accelerate joint development programs. Compared with conventional graphite anodes, silicon-carbon systems offer much higher theoretical capacity, but they also face challenges such as volume expansion, interfacial side reactions, initial efficiency loss, and batch-to-batch consistency. According to the new market research report "Global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery Market Growth 2026-2032", published by LP Information, the global Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery market size is projected to reach US$111 million by 2032, at a CAGR of 18.0% during the forecast period. According to LP Information, the global key manufacturers of Silicon-carbon Anode Materials for Solid State Battery include Group14 Technologies, Sila Nanotechnologies, Amprius, etc. In 2025, the global top three players had a share of approximately 31.65% in terms of revenue. To read the full report or request a free sample report, please use the link: https://www.lpinformationdata.com/reports/1866822/silicon---carbon-anode-materials-for-solid-state-battery 1.2 Industrial Chain The upstream segment mainly includes metallurgical-grade silicon, silane, graphite, and porous carbon, with representative suppliers such as Elkem, Hemlock, and East Hope Group. Raw material purity, particle size distribution, carbon structure, and supply stability directly affect capacity performance, swelling control, cycle life, and batch consistency, while also forming the basis for cost control and mass production. The midstream segment focuses on silicon-carbon composite structure engineering, interface stabilization, swelling suppression, surface coating modification, and particle morphology optimization. The main challenge is to balance high capacity with long cycle life while controlling initial efficiency, tap density, and processing compatibility. Stable mixing, heat treatment, coating, and classification processes directly affect yield, customer qualification time, and unit manufacturing cost. Downstream demand mainly comes from automotive power batteries and consumer electronics lithium batteries. Power battery customers focus on longer driving range, fast charging capability, safety, and long-term cycling performance, while consumer electronics customers emphasize volumetric energy density and thinner product design. Silicon-carbon anodes help battery makers improve energy density and create differentiated performance for solid state batteries, premium vehicles, and high-end devices. 1.3 Influencing Factors Drivers: The core growth driver is rising demand for high-energy-density batteries. Longer-range electric vehicles, fast-charging platforms, and thinner high-end consumer electronics are pushing anode materials from conventional graphite toward silicon-carbon systems. As solid state battery development and demonstration projects accelerate, battery makers are increasing validation demand for high-capacity, low-swelling, and long-life anode materials, supporting order growth and market expansion. Challenges: The main barrier is process stability and cost pressure. Silicon materials tend to expand and trigger interfacial side reactions during charge and discharge, which raises requirements for coating, structure design, and battery system matching. If batch consistency, initial efficiency, and cycle life cannot meet customer requirements steadily, qualification cycles will be extended and production expansion and profitability will be constrained. Trend: Future development will focus on higher capacity, lower swelling, and better adaptation to solid state battery systems. Material suppliers will use nano-structure design, porous carbon frameworks, elastic coating layers, and interface modification to improve cycling stability, while developing customized products for different solid electrolytes and cell processes. (WTOC) - Effingham County commissioners voted to hire an outside firm to represent the county’s interests and oversee Project Camellia, the plan allowing OpenAI to build a 1,400-acre data center campus in the county. Residents say they want their voices heard as county leaders move forward with the project. County hires Charles Abbott Associates Effingham County voted to hire Charles Abbott Associates. The firm previously helped with the Hyundai site in Bryan County and the children’s hospital in Atlanta. County leaders said the firm will be their point of contact to address issues at the site, such as truck traffic or construction noise. The firm said it plans to have 12 people providing oversight, inspections and reviews of phase one of the project. “We currently provide building inspection and plan review services across the nation to over 100 communities. We’ve dealt with roughly two dozen data centers across the country as well, large distribution centers,” said Will Hart. Firm’s experience and meeting format The firm said it only works with local governments and has 40 years of experience with large industrial projects. Firm representatives only took questions from county leaders. There was no public comment for this portion of the meeting. Copyright 2026 WTOC. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Partners with Muehlbauer Group for Production Equipment SAN JOSE, Calif., Oct. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- QuantumScape Corporation (NASDAQ: QS), a global leader in solid-state lithium-metal battery technology, today announced a planned 100 megawatt-hour (MWh) capacity cell production line to meet demand for solid-state batteries from markets including AI data centers, aerospace and defense. To develop this line, QS has partnered with Muehlbauer Group, a leading German automation and manufacturing technology company, as an ecosystem provider of cell assembly equipment. QS is currently demonstrating scalable production of solid-state batteries using its highly automated Eagle Line pilot facility in San Jose. Muehlbauer evaluated the Eagle Line processes and developed design enhancements to bring the technology to mass production; engineering work on higher-throughput processes and equipment for the new line is underway. Start of cell production is targeted for 2028. "We are excited to welcome Muehlbauer to the QS ecosystem," said Dr. Siva Sivaram, president and CEO of QS. "Muehlbauer is an experienced and respected global player in manufacturing automation and battery equipment, and they've shown top-tier system integration capability, impressive engineering depth, and the scalability mindset necessary to bring our groundbreaking technology to the gigawatt-hour scale. They join a world-class ecosystem of technology partners as we bring solid-state batteries into mass production." "The Eagle Line proved to us that QuantumScape's solid-state technology is ready to scale to the next level," said Josef Markus Mühlbauer, CEO of Muehlbauer Group. "We have been working on-site with QS in San Jose to develop a scale-up plan built on the foundation of the Eagle Line. With decades of experience in turning innovative technologies into scalable production processes, we are proud to be a preferred partner within QuantumScape's ecosystem and to contribute our expertise to the mission of revolutionizing energy storage and enabling a more sustainable future." About QuantumScape Corporation QuantumScape is on a mission to revolutionize energy storage to enable a sustainable future. The company's next-generation solid-state lithium-metal battery technology is designed to enable greater energy density, faster charging and enhanced safety to support the transition away from legacy energy sources toward a lower carbon future. For more information, visit www.quantumscape.com. About Muehlbauer Group With around 4,500 employees at 40 locations worldwide and 45 years of experience, the Muehlbauer Group has developed into one of the most advanced suppliers of complete production solutions. The company has achieved a leading position in the semiconductor industry with its unique die sorting technology and serves 90% of worldwide demand for RFID. More than 90,000 machines and systems have already been installed worldwide, and the Group specialises in high-precision, high-speed assembly systems, even in cleanroom environments. For more information, visit www.muehlbauer.de.

artigo.texto: Spokane County Commission extends halt on data centers through June, passes regulation baton to state A monthslong public pressure campaign led Spokane County officials this week to extend the existing pause on permitting for load data centers. The Spokane County Commission voted unanimously Tuesday on a resolution that halts the acceptance and processing of data center permits until June 1, 2027, or until the county establishes rules for the tech behemoths, whichever comes first. The measure replaces a pause put in place by the county commissioners in August that would’ve expired in December. The Spokane County Planning Commission was expected to have code updates and zoning amendments to present to the board for approval by the commission’s last meeting of the year if the board did not vote to extend the pause. Tuesday’s action included a work plan for how those updates will continue to move forward. The new timeline introduced by the commissioners could mean state lawmakers will now weigh in on the data center discussion. The matter is anticipated to come before the Legislature in the next session, which means Gov. Bob Ferguson could be weighing laws pertaining to data centers that will supersede any action by the county before the pause is up. Commissioner Al French, who faced heavy criticism, accusations and threats following the revelation through public records requests he participated in several meetings with industry members, called the ordeal a “political nightmare,” instead of what could have been a step forward for the county. He does not know if any company would be interested in moving forward locally in the current climate, he said. He took the offensive with members of the crowd who’ve been vocal in their distaste of French, often in less than socially acceptable ways. “This has certainly been an interesting 120 days,” French said. “Many of you have revealed the lengths you’re willing to go to to ensure that you get your way. You have lied to the public, you have engaged in character assassinations, you created and spread conspiracy theories, and quite frankly, just embarrassed yourself.” Spencer Lambdin, an outspoken member of the crowd as of late, screamed an expletive at French and stormed out of the meeting. “I think to myself as I listen to your accusations, ‘How proud your parents must be,’” French said, raising his hand in the direction of Lambdin. “He makes my case for me.” French took the time ahead of the vote to “clarify” the record and dispel rumors, accusations and “slanderous” comments lobbed by local residents lately, he said. He had Chief Civil Prosecutor Matthew Folsom corroborate the legal definition of public record regarding those aforementioned meetings to address the accusation they were held in secret. He did not discuss the ordinance with anyone at Avista, with a proposed data center developer or related industry members ahead of the vote, he said. He also has not entered into any nondisclosure agreements with anyone, or receive any compensation for “recruiting” companies or business leaders to Spokane – something he’s done throughout the Pacific Northwest for years, he said. “My reward in attracting a company or helping an existing company expand is helping someone get a job that might not have one, or get a better paying job than they already have,” French said. “… When I worked with Amazon to bring them to Spokane, my reward was seeing over a thousand people, residents in Hillyard, getting a good paying job with benefits working at the Amazon fulfillment center.” Planning Director Scott Chesney said the work plan directs the commission to consider the updates as part of the comprehensive plan update required by state law. The commission will continue their work, but state law may be updated prior to that point under the new pause timeline. Commissioners across party lines conveyed willingness to implement an extension early on, but it did little to quell concerns in what’s become a contentious issue locally and nationally. Over the past few months, constituents packed the county governing board’s weekly meetings, repeatedly calling for an extension on the pause, or moratorium, as soon as it took effect. A similar saga played out in public testimony Tuesday. Spokane resident Brittany Anderson, a stay-at-home mom who’s gained a local following in advocating against data centers, was one of many who told the commission she was not in support of the extension because it still left “significant loopholes,” like the possibility of breaking up a center between smaller parcels, she said. Anderson, and several who testified, referenced existing drafts of updates considered by the planning commission and included in part in the work plan moving forward. “I do not endorse this weak approach to safety and sustainability,” Anderson said. “Our residents deserve meaningful protection and transparency.” Anderson announced on social media this week that she’s running as a write-in candidate for Washington’s 5th Congressional district, in opposition to Democrat Carmela Conroy and Republican Rep. Michael Baumgartner. Her entrance to the race comes as some voters are already casting ballots. She said voters deserve more choice in the race. She did not share much on campaign points, only that she cares “about clean water, protecting our environment and farmland, affordable living, human rights, peace, and a government that answers to the people rather than wealthy donors and powerful interests.” “These aren’t issues I suddenly discovered during an election year,” the statement reads. “They’re issues I’ve already been speaking about, researching, and fighting for.” Folsom assured there were no workarounds for a developer to receive permits under the approved resolution. artigo.texto: O recuo na infraestrutura da Nscale em Loughton deve-se a atrasos na ligação à rede elétrica britânica. A Microsoft confirmou o cancelamento do acordo celebrado com a startup britânica Nscale para o aluguer de capacidade de computação num novo centro de dados dedicado à inteligência artificial (IA) em Loughton, a nordeste de Londres. A decisão assenta em constrangimentos infraestruturais na rede elétrica do Reino Unido. Segundo a imprensa britânica, a distribuidora UK Power Networks informou a Nscale de que o complexo de Loughton não teria acesso à energia elétrica necessária antes da década de 2030. Em declarações oficiais, um porta-voz da multinacional norte-americana esclareceu que a “decisão dizia respeito a um único local” e sublinhou que a empresa “continua empenhada na sua parceria com a Nscale”. Por seu turno, a Nscale confirmou que está a procurar fontes alternativas de energia elétrica para o local e que o percalço não afeta os restantes contratos da empresa. Impacto nas Ambições Britânicas e no Mercado de IA O projeto de Loughton tinha sido classificado pelo ex-primeiro-ministro britânico Keir Starmer como “o maior centro de dados de IA soberano do Reino Unido”. O anúncio do cancelamento surge numa altura em que a Nscale prepara a sua Oferta Pública Inicial (IPO) em Nova Iorque, com uma valorização estimada em 35 mil milhões de dólares. A desistência da Microsoft junta-se a outro recuo recente no mercado britânico de supercomputação: no início do ano, a OpenAI retirou-se de uma parceria com a Nscale e a Nvidia que visava implementar uma versão britânica do projeto de infraestruturas Stargate.

artigo.texto: Proposal to pause new data centers in Michigan City sparks protests over Google exemption MICHIGAN CITY, Ind. (WSBT) — Michigan City's Common Council took the first step toward pressing pause on future data center developments. But one major project would be exempt. Protesters outside Tuesday's meeting said the proposed moratorium does not go far enough because Google's data center project is already under construction and would not be affected. A proposal to pause new data center developments is back before the Michigan City Common Council, but opponents say the ordinance leaves out a major piece — Google's data center project that is already underway. They want the council to remove that exemption before moving forward. Protesters gathered outside City Hall before Tuesday's council meeting, chanting and holding signs. They say they are concerned about future data center projects and the rules governing the Google project that is already underway. "It totally exempts Google and all of its future phases and build out for a moratorium and effectively pause on data center development here," said protester Ashley Williams. The ordinance would pause future data center development, but it would not apply to current projects like Google's, which has already broken ground. Councilman Bryant Dabney (D), one of the ordinance's sponsors, says the city has no plans to stop the project. "Some people want us to stop what's going on now, but we have millions of dollars that have already been given to Michigan City with permitting fees, building fees that are happening over there," said Dabney. Tuesday was only a first reading of the ordinance. The council will be able to make amendments during its second reading at their next meeting on November 4.

artigo.texto: Amazon hosts open house to discus data center development in Posey Co. POSEY COUNTY, Ind. (WFIE) - Posey County residents got the chance to speak directly with Amazon representatives Tuesday, asking questions about a possible data center the company could build in the area. The meeting drew people from Posey County and beyond, about a month after Amazon first revealed its interest in the area at a public hearing on a proposed data center ordinance. [PREVIOUS: Amazon looking to develop in Posey Co.] Community activist Christopher Newman said he isn’t taking a side on the project — but wants to make sure the process is done right. “I’m neither for nor against data centers. I just want us to do whatever it takes to get it right the first time. Whatever we decide as a community as far as ordinance and protections, I think we need to make sure that the community as a whole is protected,” Newman said. Why Amazon Is Looking at Posey County Amazon officials say they’re eyeing Posey County in part because CenterPoint Energy has excess capacity on its power grid. The company also says any data center it builds would be water conscious, using about as much water per year as nine restaurants. Amazon says the project would bring in new jobs — but not everyone is convinced that’s a win for local residents. Posey County resident Shannon Straw said she wants assurances the jobs will go to people who actually live in the county. “They say that this data center is going to help our county and not make it die, but obviously we need people employed from our county. We don’t need remote workers or a hybrid mix. We need actual people to come and work in our county,” Straw said. A Look Inside Officials also brought a mobile unit to the meeting, giving residents a hands-on look at equipment that simulates what a data center computer looks like. Amazon says any facility it builds would comply with local ordinances regarding sound, energy consumption and environmental impact. Keith Klein, AWS Director of Data Center Solutions, said the company wants to keep hearing from residents — including those who have concerns. “We’re here to talk to the community and to understand exactly what the community is looking for in a deployment of this size, and continue that particular dialogue with us, we’re open to hearing that particular conversation, and don’t look at us as someone you can’t speak to, we want to hear from the community and we want to build something together,” Klein said. What’s Next Officials say they were glad to see so many people turn out, even those who remain skeptical of the project. As plans continue to develop, Amazon says it’s likely to hold more public events like this one to keep the conversation going between the company and the community. Copyright 2026 WFIE. artigo.texto: Envision commissions a 125 MWh battery storage system for OCP in Morocco Envision Energy announces the commissioning of a 25 MW / 125 MWh LFP battery system at OCP Green Energy's Benguerir site, backed by $20 million in financing. Envision Energy has announced the commissioning of Morocco's first large-scale lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery energy storage system. Installed at OCP Green Energy's mining site in Benguerir, the system offers 25 MW of power and 125 MWh of capacity. According to the company, it is currently undergoing testing ahead of commercial operation. Battery storage is expanding across several markets, as shown by the installation of a 3.75 MWh storage system in Buffalo by Viridi and Good Carbon, the energization of three 24.6 MWh storage sites in Japan by GRITZ and the start of construction of 840 MWh of storage at Bertikow by Enlight and ENERTRAG. In Morocco, the contract with Envision Energy was signed in late 2025. A tool for managing peak hours Envision Energy says it supplied the entire system and led the commissioning work. The group integrated the batteries with the site's solar generation, grid conditions and industrial load profile. The system is designed to shift excess solar electricity produced during the day to peak consumption hours. According to the company, this shift would cut the site's electricity bill by about 25% during those peak hours. With five hours of storage, the system functions more as an industrial energy management tool than as a short-term grid asset. It is designed for a 25-year lifespan with daily charge and discharge cycles. Financing and national targets The project benefits from $20 million in financing from the Clean Technology Fund, managed by the African Development Bank Group. For OCP, the focus is on reducing peak-hour costs over the system's lifetime rather than on the battery's capacity itself, according to the project's description. John Lee, Envision Energy's managing director for the Middle East and Africa, called the project a historic step for Morocco's energy transition. Omar Kadir, CEO of OCP Green Energy, said storage extends the group's energy strategy and could help integrate renewables into the national grid. The project supports the country's target of drawing 52% of its installed electricity capacity from renewable sources by 2030, according to the release. artigo.texto: Nvidia Unveils DSX POD Amid Greenpeace Protest Nvidia says its DSX POD can slash AI data center deployment times, but its Berlin launch also underscored growing backlash over the industry’s rapid expansion. BERLIN – A simple imperative has defined the AI data center boom: faster, bigger, and more powerful. But that acceleration is also drawing pushback, particularly in the US, where communities are raising concerns about the speed, scale, and sustainability of new data center development. Nvidia sits at the center of that expansion. The GPU leader is not only supplying much of the technology behind the AI buildout but also helping shape the economics of the next generation of AI-optimized facilities, which it calls AI factories. A Modular Push for Faster AI Buildouts At its GTC event in Berlin, Nvidia unveiled its latest effort to accelerate that growth: a prefabricated modular reference design called DSX POD. The design is intended to give Nvidia partners, including Dell Technologies, HPE, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv, a standardized blueprint for containerized data centers built around the company’s Vera Rubin AI infrastructure. Nvidia said the factory-built, pre-integrated modules can reduce deployment times from roughly six months to as little as 14 days. Chief executive Jensen Huang introduced the DSX POD during his keynote, positioning it as a way for operators to bring expensive AI infrastructure online more quickly and begin generating returns sooner. Huang said that each gigawatt-scale data center costs $50 billion. “The revenue generation you expect is tens of billion dollars per year,” he said. “If delayed by just three months, that's $10 billion worth of revenues.” By shifting more of the work into the supply chain, he said, the time from installation to production can fall from months to about a month. Huang described the DSX POD approach as a fundamental change in how data centers are delivered, arguing that shorter deployment cycles would reduce idle computing capacity and unused capital expenditure while improving profitability. Greenpeace Protest Interrupts Keynote Shortly before Huang detailed the new design, however, a small group of Greenpeace protesters interrupted the keynote from the audience. The protesters unfurled a banner and projected a message onto the stage reading “Clean up Your Dirty Business.” They also shouted questions about Nvidia technology reportedly found in Russian drones, as well as the environmental effects of data center expansion. “Jensen, what about the technology that was found in Russian drones?” one protester shouted. “What are you doing about the environmental destruction? What about sustainable energy?” Protesters held up a banner that read, “Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!” (Image: Andrew Donoghue) Greenpeace later said it was behind the protest. “While Nvidia is building an unchecked AI empire no one consented to, people are paying the price,” Benjamin Stephan, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in a statement. “Around the world, communities face damage to water supplies and soil, alongside rising electricity bills because of unchecked expansion of data centers.” Huang remained calm during the interruption and asked security not to overreact as protesters were escorted from the hall. “Everybody has a chance to say something,” he said. “I'll talk to you later. But let me get through my keynote.” The protesters’ comments about Russian drone technology referred to reports earlier this year that Nvidia Jetson Orin modules had been found in the wreckage of drones used by Russia’s military. Nvidia has said the products are consumer-grade systems sold to students, developers, and startups. The protests underscored a broader tension for the industry. While anti-data center demonstrations have become more common, they are typically staged outside venues rather than inside keynote halls. Brownfield Potential and Deployment Questions That tension is also relevant to the DSX POD itself. Nvidia says the system uses dry coolers in place of traditional evaporative cooling, which could help address concerns about water use. At the same time, a platform designed to accelerate deployment could intensify opposition in communities already uneasy about how quickly data center projects are moving. The containerized form factor may prove equally divisive. Critics may see it as a symbol of industrial infrastructure arriving faster and more visibly. Nvidia did share an image of a large data center campus built entirely from DSX PODs, but the company’s vice president of DGX systems, Charlie Boyle, told Data Center Knowledge that the units could be deployed inside existing industrial buildings and brownfield sites, effectively turning disused sites into new data center capacity. “I have got people putting these effectively in old, abandoned warehouses,” Boyle said. “An old, abandoned building you see every day – suddenly there are lights in there, and it’s now a data center.” That aligns with the industry’s recent push to reuse brownfield sites and former industrial property. However, recent data from JLL suggests that in parts of Europe, operators are increasingly looking beyond urban centers for larger campus-style developments. Boyle also argued that the modular design offers flexibility from a sustainability perspective, saying operators could place the units where waste heat might be reused and where the systems can be integrated into a wider site strategy. “You can put these things anywhere. You can grow trees around them,” Boyle said. “That is part of the flexibility of it. You can put it somewhere you can reuse the heat, like next to a swimming pool. You have a lot of options.” Boyle also pushed back on concerns about upgradability and lifespan of containerized designs, given how closely integrated the power, cooling, and other support systems are to the IT. artigo.texto: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, durante evento político nos Estados Unidos. (Kent NISHIMURA / AFP) Estagiária de jornalismo Publicado em 21 de outubro de 2026 às 11h44. O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira, 21, que data centers no país devem produzir sua própria energia elétrica e firmar acordos financeiros com as populações dos locais onde eles se instalam. As declarações ocorrem em meio a tensões entre moradores do interior do país e o setor tecnológico, que avança pelo território com data centers para atender à alta demanda da inteligência artificial. "Determino que novos data centers de grande porte — em alguns casos, gigantescos — produzam sua própria energia elétrica e forneçam ou vendam qualquer excedente para a comunidade local ou para a rede elétrica; assim, não haverá aumento nos preços da eletricidade. Na verdade, pode até ocorrer uma redução substancial.", afirmou o republicano em publicação na rede social Truth. "O mesmo vale para outros aspectos! Se as empresas quiserem que seus data centers sejam bem aceitos, que paguem à comunidade — e/ou aos indivíduos que a compõem — uma espécie de 'dividendo'." Ele afirmou também que tem "observado esse processo atentamente", em que data centers "que eram muito malvistos em determinadas regiões tornaram-se extremamente bem aceitos após a formalização de um acordo financeiro". A expansão acelerada de datacenters de IA pelo interior da América do Norte está gerando conflitos entre moradores e grandes empresas de tecnologia. De acordo com dados da plataforma Data Center Map, existem 4287 estruturas nos Estados Unidos, sendo 1500 deles em construção. Essa nova onda de investimentos tem uma diferença essencial daquilo que já existe no país. Ao passo que 87% dos datacenters em operação estão em áreas urbanas, 67% dos novos estão sendo construídos em áreas rurais. Nessa frente de expansão, porém, as empresas de tecnologia têm encontrado resistência da população. Centenas de organizações em 42 estados dos EUA já se mobilizaram contra projetos em suas comunidades, segundo levantamento da Data Center Watch divulgado pela Wired. Os casos se multiplicam. Nos estados de Montana e Utah, comunidades com poucos recursos políticos e jurídicos tentam frear obras bilionárias. Um estudo de 2023 estimou que gerar entre dez e cinquenta respostas de tamanho médio em chatbots de IA consome meio litro de água. A Agência Internacional de Energia calculou que datacenters usaram 140 bilhões de litros de água globalmente só para resfriamento em 2023, segundo a CBC. Do lado das empresas e governos, o argumento é de segurança nacional e competitividade econômica. "O potencial do que estamos criando é muito importante para a defesa e para a economia", disse o investidor Kevin O'Leary, que apoia a construção de um datacenter de 4 mil acres em Utah, à CNN. O governador do estado, Spencer Cox, foi na mesma direção: "Cada estado tem uma obrigação de permitir que esses datacenters sejam construídos." Do lado dos moradores, a demanda é mais transparência, estudos independentes e tempo para avaliar o impacto antes que as obras comecem. Caroline Gleich, ativista ambiental de Utah, disse à emissora: "Vamos fazer um estudo de impacto ambiental e publicá-lo. Vamos colocar algumas coisas por escrito e dar à comunidade tempo para revisá-las."

artigo.texto: Data centers and the electricity grid that feeds them have been consuming sizable amounts of copper, steel and other base metals in the United States and other parts of the world this decade. A recent analysis by global research firm Wood Mackenzie finds such demand could eventually outpace supply if data center construction and grid investment momentum continues. “Geopolitical disruptions, resource nationalism and an escalating power crunch are reshaping global base metals markets,” states the United Kingdom-based research firm. “As the global data center pipeline surpasses 250 gigawatts (GW), demand for power infrastructure is accelerating competition for copper, aluminum and other strategic materials,” adds the company. Investment analysts and financial media outlets have been increasing their scrutiny of artificial intelligence (AI) and data center spending and financing arrangements, casting some doubt on whether data center spending momentum may have peaked. In the meantime, says Wood Mackenzie, the metals impact of AI extends beyond data centers themselves and into the transmission networks, substations and dedicated power generation network that “can require three to four times more metal than the facilities they support.” Should this new structural demand continue, the analysis finds that “upstream investment is struggling to keep pace,” referring to mining and metals production capital spending. “Despite elevated commodity prices, project sanctioning remains below expectations as permitting delays, geopolitical uncertainty and increasing project complexity weigh on investment decisions,” writes Wood Mackenzie. "Data centers represent an economy-wide power infrastructure challenge [and high metal] prices should trigger investment, yet project sanctioning remains below expectations,” says Lindsay Grant, vice president of metals and mining research at Wood Mackenzie. “Without faster approvals and investment commitments, the industry cannot deliver the mine supply needed to support future growth,” adds Grant. In the copper sector, Wood Mackenzie says record prices of more than $14,750 per ton reflect material dislocation, with U.S. stockpiling creating nearly six months of inventoried domestic supply “while leaving the rest of the world in a 460,000-ton deficit.” A supply shock from Middle East smelter damage has contributed to a global primary aluminum deficit thus far in 2026, says Wood Mackenzie, despite “Chinese operating rates reaching 99 percent and Indonesia producing 1.3 million tons.” Wood Mackenzie reports it is tracking more than 250 GW of data center projects globally, a figure it says is three times the size of the pipeline one year ago. “AI data center electricity demand is forecast to increase fivefold between 2025 and 2030 and exceed 1,000 terawatt hours (TWh) by 2035,” adds the research firm. Concludes Grant, “Across copper, aluminum, nickel and lithium, the common thread is that future supply depends on investment decisions being made today. Markets are adapting to a world where security of supply, energy availability and geopolitical considerations increasingly sit alongside cost competitiveness in shaping investment outcomes.”

artigo.texto: Facing pushback on data centers, tech giants are promising hosts more money and fewer secrets With host communities across the U.S. turning against their gargantuan data centers, America’s technology giants are promising to take fewer taxpayer handouts, keep fewer secrets or shower more money onto the communities willing to allow the server warehouses With host communities across the U.S. turning against their gargantuan data centers, America’s technology giants are promising to take fewer taxpayer handouts, keep fewer secrets or shower more money onto the communities willing to allow the server warehouses. The promises come as anti-data center sentiment has become a potent issue in the midterm election with control of Congress and 36 governors’ offices on the line. In addition to ramping up financial incentives, officials with Google and Meta said in interviews with The Associated Press they are trying to address mistrust by being more transparent with communities where they would like to build. With host communities across the U.S. turning against their gargantuan data centers, America's technology giants are promising to take fewer taxpayer handouts, keep fewer secrets or shower more money onto the communities willing to allow the server warehouses. The new raft of promises from the world's richest companies comes as anti-data center sentiment has become a potent issue in the midterm elections, with control of Congress and 36 governors' offices on the line. Despite backing from President Donald Trump, the data centers powering the artificial intelligence boom have become politically toxic. Community opposition that blocks municipal permits has become a bottleneck, and tech giants could face even more challenges if voters next month elect more public officials who are skeptical of data centers. The tech industry says it has gotten the message. In addition to ramping up financial incentives, officials with Google and Meta said in interviews with The Associated Press they are trying to address mistrust by being more transparent with communities where they would like to build. Companies are also making pledges to reduce their impact on the environment and offering assurances that data centers will boost local property values — all while maintaining AI is a positive force for the American economy, despite its skeptics. Tech giants pledge more transparency Devi Thomas, Google’s global head of community development and engagement, told AP that she wouldn’t call resistance to data centers a “backlash,” but that “there are often community questions to be addressed.” “Early public consultation is increasingly a very important part of the process. We have done as much as we can to make sure communities are involved early on,” Thomas said. Earlier this month, Amazon rolled out its “Amazon Data Center Commitment," including pledges to improve the environmental rating of its backup diesel generators and disclose more about its data centers' energy and water use. It also said — as have Microsoft and Google — that it had stopped requiring government officials to sign non-disclosure agreements. The use of non-disclosure agreements has meant people in host communities may know little or nothing about a project until it shows up on a municipal board’s voting agenda. Besides that, tech companies often have hidden their involvement in a project behind a code name and developers who do the legwork with local governments, critics and other developers say. That practice “raises people’s suspicion as to what’s truly happening,” said Anita Verma-Lallian, a developer with data center projects in Arizona. Meta is always evaluating how well it shares information with communities, said Lindsay Elin, Meta’s vice president of public policy and external affairs. “As part of that work, we are reviewing our use of non-disclosure agreements,” she said in a statement to the AP. In a report this month that sharply criticized data center giants including Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft, several Senate Democrats said companies have used non-disclosure agreements to freeze out the public. The report also said the companies aggressively seek state and local tax breaks and do not cover the entire cost of the electric-grid buildout needed for energy-hungry data centers. Spending ramps up in host communities, along with skepticism The dominant players in the industry — Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft — project they’ll spend more than $600 billion this year combined on capital projects, primarily data center construction in the U.S. Even as the companies prepare to spend more to entice communities — payments that some critics call “bribes” — Trump urged them in a social media post Wednesday to pay people and communities a “dividend” if they “want to make their Data Centers popular.” “MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A.,” Trump wrote. Meta and Amazon said recently they will each spend $1 billion on financial incentives to host communities in the coming years, on top of millions they already spend to support schools, charities and job training. Google says its investments in local programs in data center communities will reach $1 billion by the end of 2027. Microsoft has pointed to a couple local tax breaks that it will forego. And Google recently said for all of its new data center campuses, the company will pay full real property taxes on the buildings and land. The companies have known since last fall that community opposition was becoming a serious problem. Data center demand began driving up electric bills last year across a 13-state electricity grid stretching from Illinois to New Jersey and Maryland, angering ratepayers. The outcry led to promises from the tech giants to pay the cost of the power infrastructure to feed their data centers, while Microsoft rolled out its five-point “Community-First AI Infrastructure” plan. Data centers’ critics aren’t persuaded. Sam Burleigh, who helped start Concerne

artigo.texto: A parceria reúne a empresa americana Crusoe e a desenvolvedora paraguaia Araico, anunciou o governo norte-americano. Por Misto Brasil Os Estados Unidos anunciaram um acordo para instalar no Paraguai um centro de computação de alto desempenho voltado a serviços de I.A. O projeto pretende usar energia hidrelétrica de Itaipu e atender empresas de computação em nuvem dos Estados Unidos e da América Latina, conforme informou o Times Brasil. A parceria reúne a empresa americana Crusoe e a desenvolvedora paraguaia Araico. Segundo o governo americano, a primeira etapa do centro deve começar a funcionar em 2027. A iniciativa busca aproveitar a eletricidade gerada pela usina de Itaipu para abastecer uma estrutura de computação voltada a grandes volumes de processamento de dados. Esse tipo de instalação exige energia constante para operar equipamentos usados em serviços de nuvem e aplicações de inteligência artificial. O Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos divulgou o acordo durante a visita de Christopher Landau, vice-secretário de Estado americano, ao Paraguai. Nesta semana, ele se reuniu com o presidente paraguaio, Santiago Peña, para tratar sobre o assunto. De forma geral, o projeto americano busca capitalizar um maior volume de energia usando a usina de Itaipu. O local movimenta grandes quantidades de água e deve beneficiar os dois continentes. artigo.texto: Parceiro institucional: O projeto de armazenamento de energia ocorre em um momento de ampliação da capacidade produtiva da empresa Repórter de ESG Publicado em 20 de outubro de 2026 às 17h45. Última atualização em 21 de outubro de 2026 às 17h16. A Rivelli Alimentos, empresa mineira que atua na cadeia de produção avícola, instalou um sistema de armazenamento de energia por baterias de 1,29 megawatt-hora (MWh) em Carmo do Cajuru, Minas Gerais, com expectativa de reduzir a conta de eletricidade em aproximadamente 50%. O projeto combina baterias da chinesa Huawei, geração solar e conexão à rede elétrica para diminuir os custos nos horários de maior demanda e garantir o abastecimento em caso de apagões. Desenvolvida pela Powersafe e pela Zipp Energia, a instalação é a primeira para um consumidor privado em Minas Gerais a receber homologação integral da Cemig Distribuição. O sistema utiliza seis gabinetes de baterias e uma usina solar de 378 quilowatts-pico (kWp), além de manter um gerador a diesel como fonte de emergência. As baterias foram instaladas na Granja de Matrizes da Rivelli, unidade dedicada à criação de aves reprodutoras. A tecnologia permite armazenar eletricidade para utilização nos horários de tarifas mais elevadas e manter equipamentos essenciais em funcionamento durante interrupções da rede. Dependendo das condições de consumo, a autonomia estimada pode chegar a 27 horas. O sistema instalado na granja é composto por seis gabinetes de baterias Huawei LUNA2000, cada um com capacidade de 215 quilowatt-hora (kWh), totalizando 1.290 kWh de armazenamento. Os equipamentos utilizam baterias de lítio-ferro-fosfato (LFP), tecnologia de armazenamento baseada em compostos de lítio, ferro e fosfato. A estrutura também inclui 540 painéis solares de 700 watts-pico (Wp), distribuídos sobre três galpões, com capacidade instalada de geração fotovoltaica de 378 quilowatts-pico (kWp). Uma das principais funções do projeto é deslocar o consumo de eletricidade para períodos de menor custo. A estratégia, conhecida como load shifting, ou deslocamento de carga, permite carregar as baterias em horários mais favoráveis e utilizar a energia armazenada durante o horário de ponta, quando o consumo da rede costuma ter tarifas mais elevadas. Segundo as empresas responsáveis, a solução foi dimensionada para permitir que o consumo de energia da concessionária seja reduzido a zero nesses períodos. Outra aplicação é o peak shaving, técnica de redução dos picos de demanda elétrica. Nesse caso, as baterias ajudam a controlar a potência solicitada à rede, com o objetivo de manter a demanda máxima da granja em até 360 quilowatts (kW). O sistema também atua na correção do fator de potência, indicador da eficiência com que a instalação utiliza a energia elétrica, para evitar cobranças adicionais relacionadas à energia reativa. A combinação dessas funções sustenta a estimativa de redução de aproximadamente 50% na fatura de eletricidade. O percentual, porém, é uma projeção apresentada pelas empresas, e não um resultado medido após um período de operação. Além do impacto econômico, a instalação busca resolver um problema operacional da cadeia avícola: a dependência de eletricidade para manter as condições ambientais necessárias à criação dos animais. Na Granja de Matrizes, sistemas de ventilação, ambiência, refrigeração e bombeamento precisam funcionar continuamente. Uma falha prolongada pode comprometer as condições de criação das aves. Antes da implantação do projeto, a transferência do fornecimento para o gerador a diesel dependia de acionamento manual. Com o novo sistema, as baterias assumem automaticamente o abastecimento em caso de interrupção da rede elétrica. O gerador continua disponível como uma segunda camada de segurança, podendo ser acionado conforme a necessidade da operação. Segundo os estudos de dimensionamento, em um cenário considerado crítico, com chuvas intensas e interrupção da rede logo após o horário de ponta, a autonomia estimada é de aproximadamente dez horas. Esse período pode chegar a 27 horas caso equipamentos não essenciais sejam desligados, reduzindo o consumo de eletricidade. Em condições favoráveis de geração solar, a autonomia também pode ser prolongada enquanto a produção dos painéis for suficiente para sustentar o consumo. As estimativas dependem, portanto, das condições de geração e da quantidade de equipamentos mantidos em funcionamento durante uma interrupção. O projeto preserva o gerador movido a diesel como recurso emergencial. Assim, embora amplie a participação da energia solar na operação, a estrutura não elimina o uso potencial de combustível fóssil em situações de contingência. A infraestrutura da Rivelli inclui uma subestação dedicada de 13,8 quilovolts para 380 volts e foi projetada para operar no modelo zero grid, configuração na qual a instalação não injeta excedentes de eletricidade na rede da distribuidora. Com isso, a energia solar produzida na granja é direcionada ao consumo da própria unidade e à estratégia de armazenamento, sem exportação para a rede da Cemig. A integração entre as diferentes fontes permite que a eletricidade seja administrada de acordo com as necessidades da operação. Para Renato Mondino, diretor de BESS C&I da Huawei, o projeto indica uma mudança na forma como empresas com atividades críticas podem utilizar sistemas de baterias. “A combinação entre BESS, geração solar e gestão da demanda permite ampliar a resiliência da operação e, ao mesmo tempo, otimizar o uso da energia”, afirma. A implantação envolveu diferentes fornecedores. A Huawei forneceu a tecnologia de armazenamento e os inversores fotovoltaicos, enquanto a Powersafe ficou responsável pelo fornecimento dos sistemas de baterias, testes e comissionamento, etapa de verificação dos equipamentos antes da operação. A HDT Energy participou da cadeia de fornecimento, e a Zipp Energia e a KBTZ Engenharia atuaram no desenvolvimento do projeto, nas obras, na subestação e na integração da infraestru
