artigo.texto: In summary Despite seven new statewide laws regulating data centers, at least 26 resolutions, moratoriums, or bans on data centers have been passed or proposed in California since June. Although California lawmakers recently passed a suite of laws intended to bring transparency to the development of new data centers, local communities across the state are signaling that disclosure isn’t enough. California currently ranks third among U.S. states in overall data center density, according to independent trackers like the US Data Center Map, with the state home to 366 of such facilities that are either fully operational, under construction, or moving through the planning process. Local elected officials are proposing data center moratoriums to slow that momentum — if not stop it in its tracks. In the first half of October alone, Oakland’s city council unanimously approved a 45-day moratorium on new approvals, making it the first city in Alameda County and the fourth in the Bay Area to adopt such a measure. San Francisco approved a similar moratorium this month, while the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors postponed a vote to permanently ban large-scale data centers, often called hyperscale facilities, on unincorporated land after receiving an overwhelming volume of public feedback. In Santa Clara, city officials considered a moratorium vote, and are moving forward with new rules to govern data center development, including more stringent water and air pollution regulations. Alhambra residents will vote on a moratorium measure in the November election. Across California, at least 26 resolutions, moratoriums, or bans on data center development have been passed or proposed since June, according to the D.C.-based non-governmental organization Food & Water Watch, which tracks similar proposals nationwide. The escalating pushback underscores a widening gap between state-level regulation and municipal action. While Gov. Gavin Newsom last month signed into law seven new measures that focus primarily on disclosure requirements, environmental impact studies, and grid protection, grassroots groups and city councils are moving fast to halt construction entirely. “I have a hard time remembering something that caught fire the way the opposition to data centers has,” said Nicole Ghio, California Director at Food & Water Watch. “Local municipalities have been able to respond quicker to the grassroots wave of opposition of people saying, ‘Hold on, let’s press pause. Let’s actually figure out what we’re doing before we commit to this huge change.'” Opponents say these energy-hungry facilities strain power grids, potentially deplete water supplies and pollute the air, and contribute to broader economic anxieties around AI-driven job elimination. The anti-data-center movement cuts across party lines; conservative group Humans First, for example, finished its nationwide Data Center Revolt tour this month with three stops in California, joining a chorus of figures on the left who call for local control as well as additional environmental and consumer protections. “This is very much a unifying issue,” Ghio noted, adding that residents are alarmed by potential rate hikes and environmental degradation. “This is not a future that I think a lot of people want. I mean, it’s a great future if you’re a tech billionaire. It’s not a great future if you’re a regular American.” Industry proponents, however, argue that halting infrastructure development risks eroding critical national interests. Doug Kelly, CEO of the policy advocacy coalition American Edge Project, framed the current buildout as an essential infrastructure race. “Artificial intelligence and the data centers that power it, this is the next foundational block of infrastructure that America is building out,” Kelly said, comparing it to historical investments in railroads and highways. Kelly acknowledged that past developments lacked sufficient community input, leading to local friction. To address these fears without stopping construction, his organization promotes an “AI Community Compact” — an agreement offering local guarantees to protect ratepayers from cost spikes, safeguard resources, and promise early transparency. “So, communities can decide whether they want data centers there or not, but they shouldn’t just blanket ban them because then you lose all your negotiating power,” Kelly said. “You’re literally saying ‘we want this billion dollar investment to go somewhere else, anywhere but here.’” Yet for local advocates, piecemeal guarantees and disclosure laws fall short of addressing the underlying risk. Advocates point to a one-year pause on hyperscale data centers that New York’s governor ordered in July as a roadmap, hoping state legislators will eventually follow local leaders’ lead. As cities continue to draft temporary freezes and outright bans, the tension between local community control and global technological dominance remains unresolved. State transparency laws may have opened the books on data center growth, but local opponents are making it clear that seeing the plans isn’t the same as approving them.

artigo.texto: Uriel Renovables completes two 10 MW battery storage plants in the United States Uriel Renovables and Silo Energy have finished building two battery storage plants in Framingham and Chicopee, Massachusetts. The installations, backed by a $20 million investment, fall under the Clean Peak Standard program. Uriel Renovables has completed construction of two battery energy storage system (BESS) plants in Framingham and Chicopee, in the state of Massachusetts. The company operates through its U.S. subsidiary Uriel Renewables, alongside its local partner Silo Energy. Battery storage is also advancing elsewhere in the United States, including the two battery storage contracts won by Flatiron Energy in the Bronx and the 3.75 MWh system installed by Viridi and Good Carbon in Buffalo. Both units are in the commissioning phase, according to Uriel Renovables. 10 MW of power and 40 MWh of capacity Each plant has a power rating of 5 MW with a duration of 4 hours, equal to 20 MWh of capacity per installation. Together, they represent 10 MW of power and 40 MWh of capacity. The two units required an investment of $20 million, the company said. The plants will store energy during hours of lowest demand and release it to the grid during periods of high consumption. Uriel Renovables says they will contribute to the stability of the New England power system. They would also make it easier to integrate a larger share of renewable energy into the grid. The projects fall under the Clean Peak Standard Both projects fall under the Clean Peak Standard, a program through which Massachusetts encourages clean energy to cover the hours of highest demand. The installations will earn certificates for the energy they feed into the grid during those consumption periods. Electricity suppliers will purchase a growing percentage of these certificates. The inauguration ceremony for the Framingham plant, located in Middlesex County, took place on September 30. State representatives, members of the Framingham municipality, and executives from the financing banks, engineering firms, contractors and other companies involved in the project attended. Ignacio Huarte, president of Uriel Renovables, and Juan FÃ©lix Huarte, president of Uriel Inversiones, the group's parent company, were present along with members of the management team. Ignacio Huarte said the two plants were the company's "first step" in the U.S. storage market and "a firm commitment" to Massachusetts. He added that storage allows renewables to meet demand when it is highest. Jorge Romero, country manager of Uriel Renovables, thanked the Framingham authorities and the company's partners, who made both projects possible. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: Ørstedhave announced their innovative large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) has officially completed construction. The system is designed to support the Hornsea 3 Offshore Wind Farm, located off the Norfolk coast. As part of the construction programme, 170 Megapacks have been installed alongside the project’s onshore converter station. Once fully operational, the facility, known as Iceni, will have a capacity of 600 MWh, enough to power an estimated 80,000 UK homes. Beatrice d’Eufemia, Project Manager for the Iceni BESS at Ørsted, said: “The system will make the best use of renewable energy produced in the UK. When electricity generation exceeds demand, the excess can be stored and then used when demand is greater.” According to Ørsted, the BESS is located separately from the Hornsea 3 onshore converter station and is connected by 18 x 33 kV cables, each approximately 600 metres long. Richard Swann, Construction Manager for the Iceni BESS at Ørsted, said: “It’s a real testament to the hard work, dedication and co-operation of teams from many different organisations that construction has been completed successfully.” The project will now move into the final stages of mechanical and electrical installation ahead of commissioning. artigo.texto: Latest Headlines Kigali Summit: Nigeria’s Carbon Market Working, Says 9JA Carbon Trade – As Africa told to move from drafting rules to closing deals Kuni Tyessi in Abuja A Nigerian carbon project developer, 9JA Carbon Trade has declared that Nigeria’s carbon market system is working following the federal government’s first approvals for international carbon credit sales. The company, a subsidiary of Qietur Limited specialising in land-use projects, made the assessment after participating in the Carbon Markets Africa Summit (CMAS) 2026 in Kigali, Rwanda. The summit, which drew 600 delegates from 52 countries and over 150 organisations, closed on October 15 with a call on African governments, buyers and financiers to move from writing rules to delivering projects. At a session on country readiness on October 14, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Climate Finance and Stakeholder Engagement, Ibrahim Shelleng, said Nigeria issued six Letters of Authorisation in March 2026 and two more by September. A Letter of Authorisation is the federal government’s formal approval for carbon credits generated in Nigeria to be traded and used outside the country. Speaking at the summit, Co-Technical Manager of 9JA Carbon Trade Ltd, Timothy Solomon, said the Kigali meeting changed the question Africa is asked. “Kigali changed the question Africa is asked. It is no longer whether the continent can supply carbon credits, but whether it can deliver them with integrity, at fair prices and with benefits host communities can see. Nigeria now has the framework and its first approvals. Our part is to bring forward projects worth approving,” Solomon said. Also speaking from the floor, Co-Technical Manager, Ekene Okpara, said the authorisations give developers confidence that the process works. He asked whether Nigeria plans a bilateral carbon agreement with another country and sought advice for developers still awaiting approval from the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC). The company also joined a roundtable on October 15 at the summit’s solution lab on reducing risk for private investors. Closing the summit on behalf of Rwanda’s Minister of Environment, the Acting Permanent Secretary listed six points of agreement, including that integrity creates value, trust is the currency of the market, and communities are partners whose benefits must be shared. Africa, the statement said, must capture more value rather than simply supply credits. Governments were asked to finish their rules, apply them and publish every authorisation and transfer, while buyers and investors were urged to move “from signals to signatures” with long-term purchase agreements at fair prices. Development partners were asked to fund project preparation, described as the stage “where good projects die today.” Declaring the summit open, Rwanda’s Minister of Environment, Dr Bernadette Arakwiye, said: “Writing rules is one thing, and running them is another.” She noted that 87 per cent of Rwanda’s issued credits come from improved cookstoves while agriculture accounts for barely one per cent of voluntary market credits in two decades. The International Air Transport Association (IATA) told delegates that CORSIA, the United Nations scheme for international aviation, becomes mandatory in 2027 and will require government-authorised credits. The European Commission disclosed plans to buy credits covering up to 260 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent between 2036 and 2040. Lorna Ritchie of the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market said credits carrying its Core Carbon Principles label sell for about 25 per cent more on average, while ratings agency BeZero Carbon said reforestation credits range from $5 to over $40 depending on rating. The African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) said Africa still relies on foreign verifiers for over 90 per cent of verification work, causing up to half of project delays. It said its accelerator programme will help build African validation and verification bodies. The Africa Carbon Investment and Finance Alliance (ACIFA) was launched at the summit to connect projects with finance, while the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) offered five support windows. The summit urged Africa to arrive at COP31 in November “with one voice and with evidence of delivery.”

artigo.texto: Discussion surrounding a small-scale data center continues in Estherville, Iowa ESTHERVILLE, Iowa (KTIV)— Discussion of a possible data center in Estherville continued as the city’s Planning and Zoning Commission heard from a representative of PathOne Data Centers. The representative said the company believes Estherville would be a good fit for a small-scale, 25-megawatt facility measuring about 100,000 square feet. Community questions and county moratorium Community members asked questions about noise, water usage and deconstruction at the end of the facility’s lifespan. In August, the Emmet County Board of Supervisors passed a one-year moratorium on new data center projects to allow time for studying impacts and creating permanent zoning rules. It only applies to unincorporated areas of the county. Gyles Uhlenhopp, chief investment officer at PathOne Data Centers, said the company designs projects for rural communities. “PathOne Data Centers has specifically designed a solution for rural America and we specifically build edge data centers that are designed to look into overlooked communities and design something that can be net positive,” Uhlenhopp said. “Estherville is a prime example of communities that have a pretty scarce resource when it comes to heavy industrial zones, areas with expanded capacity that we would call stranded power.” No tenant lined up PathOne does not have a tenant lined up for a potential project in Estherville, but company officials said demand is high. “Once an ordinance is approved, if those ordinances are parameters we could exist within, if a project could exist within those parameters then we would pursue a project, and that is where it is my job to help raise money for the project once those things exist,” Uhlenhopp said. “It is about 12 to 18 months to actually build a facility and turn on the lights.” The Planning and Zoning Commission will continue its conversation next Thursday at 5 p.m. That’s when members hope to finalize a memorandum with recommendations to be sent to the Estherville City Council. artigo.texto: Dan Cox demands statewide ban on new Maryland mega data centers ADAMSTOWN, Md. (WBFF) — Community members and Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox met Wednesday to address the expansion of mega data centers and concerns that power transmission lines could take farmland and other private property through eminent domain. WBFF has been following mounting concerns from Adamstown residents about how these large-scale developments affect families, farmers, and property owners. Local voices highlighted the loss of farmland, air and water quality issues, noise, traffic, and worries about children’s health, particularly with hundreds of diesel generators near Carroll Manor Elementary School, where 500 students attend classes close to ongoing construction. ALSO READ | Gov. Candidate Dan Cox Criticizes Key Bridge Rebuild Delays "With the taking of our farmland, the taking of our property, the taking of our air quality, the taking and the sucking of our water supplies and the endangering of our children," Cox said at the press conference. He attributed fast-tracked permits for these facilities to decisions by Gov. Wes Moore and Frederick County Executive Jessica Fitzwater and called for immediate statewide action, including halting current and future mega data center approvals. He described the fast-track process as “many times done with NDAs or non-disclosure agreements,” and argued this was “unconscionable and it's harmful to the community.” Cox pointed to reports of air pollution, dust, water contamination and increased traffic, saying state and county officials had ignored the community’s pleas for help. The candidate proposed a statewide ban, a temporary moratorium on new data center development and a mandatory review of existing permits and environmental impacts. He said a governor could issue an executive order to enact a moratorium while pursuing legislation for a permanent ban. He argued current policies do not adequately protect communities, saying, “We need a statewide ban on new mega data centers. We need to enforce the law in Adamstown and across Maryland, and we need to have remedies for established harm and protect the families and children who live here.” Watch his Oct. 21 press conference in the video above. Local resident Hope Green, whose property borders a data center, described persistent dust, air pollution, and chemicals in her water: "As the county has identified, by the way, forever chemicals have been found in at least six wells in this area.” Green said the conditions have damaged her home's value, making it hard to sell, and she has received no compensation or buyout offer. Gene Butler, a third-generation landowner and farmer, described work noise and spotlights from the facility shining into his home at night. “We've had accidents, we've had people trespassing, the lights. It's just mind-blowing what they're getting away with," Butler said. He also shared concerns about possible effects on livestock and his inability to move his family business because of costs and declining property values. ALSO READ | Moore, Cox clash on bridge rebuild, crime and taxes in first Maryland governor debate Elyse Wilson, an Adamstown resident and advocate, noted the large impact of the diesel generators, saying that, on average, they are "about the size of a 26-foot moving truck." Wilson called for air quality monitoring around homes, not just the school, and said, “We just want not just Adamstown to be safe, but Maryland to be safe and the environment to be safe.” She cited other states, like Virginia, which have implemented stricter monitoring requirements and noted that local requests for similar measures have gone unanswered. "It's here. It's not going away. But we're trying to tell the rest of Frederick County and the state of Maryland what could happen to them. We don't want to see it," Green told FOX45's Maxine Rose following the press conference. Additional speakers said eminent domain for new transmission lines would take private property and farmland, affecting families across Frederick County and beyond. “It's not just going to be an Adamstown issue; it's going to be a Brunswick issue. It's going to be a Jefferson issue," said Frank Hollewa, a candidate for Frederick County council. "You got power lines that are going through district two, where it's going to destroy land through eminent domain. And people are just saying, 'Help me.'” Several called for meaningful compensation, independent assessments, and fair buyouts for affected property owners. Others warned about water and air pollution, potential health risks from diesel exhaust and damage to the region’s rural character. Cox criticized state and local leaders for what he called a lack of transparency and poor communication about these kinds of projects, citing reports of non-disclosure agreements and a community benefits agreement that local residents and candidates described as insufficient. He pledged to review permits issued for such developments and said he would seek to rescind state water and environmental permits. He also proposed independent, repeated testing of affected wells; monitoring for dust, noise and light; and practical assistance for families when testing and health guidance establish a need. ALSO READ | Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox talks delays in rebuilding of Key Bridge When asked about his past co-sponsorship of a House bill, which proposed tax incentives for data center equipment, Cox responded, “Do I regret it? Well, certainly under this condition I don't support that.” He said today’s mega data centers are on a different scale and have a different impact than when the legislation passed. Residents called on elected officials to listen, prioritize safety, and “do the right thing to help us.”

artigo.texto: Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant Expõe uma Lacuna de Relatórios de Nove Dígitos O Condado de Grant descobriu mudanças não reportadas em propriedades de data centers de IA, incluindo uma ampliação estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. A avaliação de data center de IA do Condado de Grant agora levanta uma questão básica: os registros tributários locais conseguem acompanhar campi computacionais cada vez mais complexos? A descoberta não estabelece automaticamente fraude tributária, ocultação deliberada ou um valor final de impostos não pagos. As informações publicamente disponíveis ainda não resolveram esses pontos. Elas mostram, porém, que mudanças físicas importantes estavam ausentes das informações usadas pelos avaliadores locais. Essa distinção importa em Quincy, Washington, onde Microsoft e diversos operadores de colocation construíram grandes campi em torno de energia hidrelétrica barata e acesso à fibra óptica. Os data centers se tornaram centrais para a base tributária local, tornando registros imobiliários precisos mais do que uma questão administrativa. O Condado de Grant agora precisa determinar quando cada melhoria passou a ser tributável, como ela deve ser avaliada e se avaliações anteriores exigem correção. Os operadores podem contestar essas decisões, como vários proprietários de data centers de Quincy já fizeram antes. Portanto, o conflito é maior do que uma estrutura negligenciada. A infraestrutura de IA está se expandindo mais rapidamente, tornando-se mais densa e incorporando equipamentos mais especializados. Os sistemas locais de avaliação ainda dependem de licenças, declarações dos proprietários, inspeções físicas e comunicação precisa entre departamentos. O Que Encontrou a Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant A principal constatação é uma lacuna de relatórios, e não ainda uma decisão tributária final. Segundo a investigação local inicial, autoridades do condado identificaram mudanças em data centers que não haviam sido reportadas para avaliação. Uma única ampliação foi estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. Esse valor parece descrever o valor de uma melhoria, e não uma cobrança tributária confirmada. Valor avaliado e imposto sobre propriedade são medidas diferentes. Os distritos tributários aplicam alíquotas aos valores avaliados depois de considerar isenções, classificações e outras regras. O registro público também não estabelece por quanto tempo a ampliação permaneceu fora do cadastro de avaliação. Esse cronograma influenciará se o condado pode ajustar avaliações anteriores e quanto de receita adicional poderá resultar disso. Os avaliadores de Washington avaliam imóveis, incluindo edifícios qualificados e melhorias permanentes. As empresas também declaram bens pessoais tributáveis mantidos em 1º de janeiro. Em um data center, essa distinção pode separar um edifício de servidores, sistemas elétricos e outros ativos móveis. O calendário publicado pelo Condado de Grant informa que os proprietários devem apresentar seus relatórios de bens pessoais ao avaliador. Enquanto isso, licenças de construção e inspeções físicas ajudam o condado a identificar mudanças em imóveis. Um campus hyperscale complica ambos os processos. Sua estrutura visível representa apenas uma parte do investimento. Distribuição de energia, sistemas de resfriamento, geradores, subestações, equipamentos de rede e instalações de servidores podem chegar por meio de projetos separados. A propriedade também pode ser dividida entre um proprietário de terreno, operador da instalação, empresa de nuvem e inquilino. Uma licença pode identificar uma parte, enquanto o equipamento tributável pertence a outra. Isso cria vários possíveis pontos de falha. Uma estrutura concluída pode não chegar prontamente ao avaliador. Uma declaração do proprietário pode omitir uma instalação. Os registros também podem classificar uma melhoria de forma diferente do tratamento final dado pelo avaliador. As evidências atuais não identificam qual explicação se aplica a cada discrepância no Condado de Grant. Seria prematuro descrever o caso como evasão intencional sem registros que o sustentem ou uma constatação oficial. No entanto, a escala elimina qualquer possibilidade de que se tratasse de uma questão trivial de documentação. Uma melhoria avaliada em mais de US$ 100 milhões pode alterar materialmente a avaliação de uma parcela e a distribuição das obrigações tributárias locais. A próxima etapa é a conciliação. A equipe do condado precisará comparar licenças, registros de inspeção, declarações de propriedade, datas de conclusão e fichas de avaliação anteriores. Os operadores devem ter a oportunidade de fornecer documentação e contestar qualquer valor proposto. Esse processo pode produzir uma avaliação mais alta sem gerar um aumento idêntico na receita do governo local. O sistema de alíquotas de Washington inclui limites de taxa e cálculos específicos por distrito que podem redistribuir as cargas tributárias entre proprietários. Ainda assim, incluir o valor omitido no cadastro é importante. Isso garante que grandes propriedades industriais recebam o mesmo escrutínio esperado de residências, fazendas, lojas e outras empresas. Por Que Uma Ampliação de Nove Dígitos Pode Ficar Fora do Cadastro Tributário Os data centers de IA expõem os limites de sistemas de avaliação projetados para ciclos de construção mais lentos e visíveis. Um projeto industrial convencional geralmente segue uma sequência reconhecível. O proprietário apresenta planos, obtém licenças, conclui inspeções e inaugura um edifício finalizado. Essa sequência cria várias oportunidades para que o avaliador identifique novo valor tributável. Os campi modernos de data centers nem sempre se desenvolvem de maneira tão organizada. Os operadores adicionam salas, sistemas de resfriamento, pátios elétricos, geradores e capacidade de servidores em fases sobrepostas. artigo.texto: Abrint e Abranet questionam obrigação ligada a data centers no leilão de 6 GHz Entidades cobram avaliação da sustentabilidade das instalações, dos efeitos concorrenciais e das obrigações previstas no edital. Abrint e Abranet questionaram a sustentabilidade econômica e os efeitos concorrenciais das obrigações de infraestrutura digital previstas na proposta de leilão de 6 GHz. Em audiência pública da Anatel hoje, 21, em São Paulo, as entidades pediram revisão dos critérios para implantação de data centers edge, esclarecimentos sobre sua operação e avaliação dos impactos sobre as empresas do setor. Pela Abrint, Cristiane Sanches defendeu que o desenho considere o retorno financeiro e a continuidade das instalações. Já o representante da Abranet, Eduardo Parajo, cobrou aprofundamento dos estudos jurídicos, econômicos e concorrenciais que fundamentam a vinculação desses investimentos à licitação de espectro. “Não basta construir essas instalações. É necessário demonstrar que haverá demanda, que a localização disponível é tecnicamente adequada, que os custos operacionais serão sustentáveis, e que existirá um modelo de exploração capaz de manter esses ativos funcionando ao longo do tempo”, afirmou Parajo. A pedido do setor, a consulta pública foi prorrogada pelo Conselho Diretor da Anatel até 7 de dezembro. Em novembro, acontecerá outra audiência pública presencial, em Fortaleza. Localização e continuidade Cristiane questionou a relação entre os critérios de localização dos data centers e as condições necessárias para manter sua operação. Segundo a representante da Abrint, a ausência desse tipo de infraestrutura em uma localidade não significa, necessariamente, que os operadores da região enfrentem um problema de conectividade. “A partir do momento em que eu tenho localidades desprovidas desse tipo de infraestrutura, e eu tenho a necessidade de continuidade futura daquela operação, eu posso ter um problema no edital de alocação desses próprios recursos”, afirmou. A representante da Abrint também questionou a aplicação do conceito de adicionalidade ao modelo proposto. Na avaliação apresentada, os critérios precisam ser examinados em conjunto com a viabilidade econômica das instalações e os compromissos financeiros dos vencedores. A Abranet, por sua vez, pediu que o edital esclareça as responsabilidades ao longo da operação. “É fundamental esclarecer quem será o responsável pela propriedade, operação, manutenção e atualização dos centros de dados”, afirmou Parajo. A entidade questionou ainda quem assumirá o risco de demanda insuficiente. Fundamento jurídico e concorrência A Abranet argumentou que redes móveis e centros de processamento de dados envolvem atividades e mercados distintos. Por isso, solicitou demonstração da necessidade, da proporcionalidade e dos benefícios públicos da obrigação. “Nós entendemos que é indispensável esclarecer o fundamento jurídico da conversão do valor econômico da outorga em investimentos dessa natureza”, disse Parajo. A associação também pediu avaliação dos efeitos sobre empresas independentes de hospedagem, colocation, processamento e interconexão. Segundo a manifestação, diferenças de custos, financiamento e obrigações regulatórias podem afetar as condições de competição entre os agentes.

artigo.texto: CATL has unveiled a dual-battery system for heavy-duty electric trucks, combining a swappable main pack with a separate backup battery to help operators use more energy between stops. Presented in Beijing on October 20, the technology arrives alongside an expansion of CATL’s Qiji battery-swapping network and new Tectrans II truck batteries. The setup pairs a chassis-mounted main battery, available in 432 kWh or 513 kWh configurations, with a fixed 77 kWh battery behind the cab. Both power sources are batteries, so the range-extender function remains fully electric. CATL says conventional swapping trucks often return with around 30 percent charge remaining. Its backup pack allows drivers to use more than 95 percent of the main battery’s capacity, with power switching between packs within milliseconds. The intended benefit is greater use of the battery capacity fleets already lease, while retaining an energy reserve for reaching a swap station. CATL says its upgraded Qiji station completes swaps in five minutes. The company targets 900 truck swapping stations by the end of 2026 and 2,000 in 2027, with a longer-term ambition of 10,000 across China. A revised battery rental billing method also lets operators retain the benefit of regenerative braking. CATL claims this can reduce per-kWh rental costs by up to 20 percent for customers on basic plans. Alongside the dual-battery launch, CATL introduced Tectrans II variants for different freight applications. These include lighter packs for short-haul operations, thinner batteries for construction trucks and a configuration suited to shorter-wheelbase vehicles. A separate long-range version offers 760 kWh capacity, an 800-volt architecture and a claimed driving range exceeding 600 kilometers. Agreements announced at the event covered an initial 13,000 units, underlining commercial interest in CATL’s expanding truck battery and swapping ecosystem. [source: CarNewsChina]

artigo.texto: President Donald Trump said that data center companies should pay local communities a "dividend" to make their projects "popular." In a Truth Social post early Wednesday, Trump urged companies to "MAKE DEALS," but did not provide details on how much money they should return to communities or individuals where data centers are being built. "I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," he wrote in the post. There's been a growing backlash against data center construction across the US, with some saying the projects are noisy, raise electricity bills, and compromise the general quality of living. Data centers are becoming an increasingly important issue in next month's midterm elections, and some politicians have shifted how they talk about the projects in recent months. Data Center Watch, a research project run by 10a Labs, found that in the first quarter of this year, at least 75 data center projects were delayed or canceled due to local opposition. Some companies have already started trying to placate unhappy locals with money or discounts. This summer, Elon Musk's SpaceX offered eligible Memphis residents a 50% discount on its Starlink internet service, tied to its growing AI build-out in the city. NorthPoint Development opted for a pure cash incentive and said it would pay every household in a Pennsylvania township $10,000 if it got permission to build a data center, the Wall Street Journal reported last month. In his Wednesday post, Trump also referenced one of his previous efforts: having tech companies cover their power costs when they build data centers to help keep local electricity prices flat. Several tech leaders agreed to do so in March, when they signed the "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," which mandates that companies provide or pay for the power generation and electricity needed for their AI projects, among other commitments. Trump closed his Wednesday post by saying that building data centers under his newest stipulations would be "GREAT FOR THE U.S.A."

artigo.texto: Data centers podem abrir novo mercado para vanádio brasileiro, diz Largo Em entrevista ao Mapa da Mina, co-CEO da mineradora destaca crescimento da demanda por baterias de fluxo e avanço do fornecimento de vanádio aos Estados Unidos A expansão dos data centers, impulsionada pelo avanço da inteligência artificial, pode abrir um novo mercado para o vanádio produzido no Brasil. A avaliação é do co-CEO da mineradora canadense Largo, Alberto Arias, que afirmou, em entrevista ao Mapa da Mina, programa de mineração da CNN, que a demanda pelo mineral para fabricação de baterias de armazenamento de energia tem crescido nos Estados Unidos. A companhia opera a mina Maracás Menchen, na Bahia, considerada uma das principais operações de vanádio do mundo. O mineral é utilizado principalmente na fabricação de aços de alta resistência e ligas metálicas para as indústrias de defesa e aeroespacial, mas vem ganhando espaço em tecnologias de armazenamento de eletricidade. “Fizemos muitos investimentos em baterias nos EUA. Criamos uma joint venture com uma produtora de baterias e, nos últimos dois anos, essa empresa está vendo um aumento exponencial de demanda de baterias de vanádio na indústria de data centers”, afirmou Arias. O executivo se refere à Storion Energy, empresa criada em 2025 a partir de uma parceria entre a Largo e a americana Stryten Energy. A companhia desenvolve componentes e eletrólitos utilizados em baterias de fluxo de vanádio, tecnologia voltada ao armazenamento de energia por períodos prolongados. Diferentemente das baterias convencionais de íons de lítio, as baterias de fluxo armazenam energia em soluções líquidas que contêm vanádio e circulam entre tanques e células eletroquímicas. A tecnologia permite armazenar grandes quantidades de eletricidade por várias horas, com longa vida útil e menor risco de incêndio. Por isso, é considerada uma alternativa para instalações industriais, redes elétricas e data centers, que precisam de fornecimento contínuo de energia para manter servidores e sistemas de processamento funcionando. O crescimento dessas instalações, especialmente das estruturas dedicadas à inteligência artificial, exige investimentos cada vez maiores em geração, transmissão e armazenamento de eletricidade. Para a Largo, esse movimento pode ampliar o consumo de vanádio, tradicionalmente concentrado na indústria siderúrgica. Arias afirmou que convidou representantes da parceira americana para conhecer a operação da Largo na Bahia e que os executivos ficaram impressionados com o potencial de ampliação da capacidade produtiva brasileira. “Para o Brasil, é uma capacidade enorme de poder expandir a produção de vanádio para uso em data centers aqui no Brasil”, disse. A aposta da mineradora é que a expansão dos data centers no país também possa estimular uma cadeia doméstica de armazenamento de energia, criando demanda para o mineral extraído em território brasileiro. Mina na Bahia e fornecimento aos EUA A Largo é uma companhia canadense com ações negociadas nas bolsas de Toronto e de Nova York. Seu principal ativo é a mina Maracás Menchen, localizada a cerca de 250 quilômetros de Salvador, que começou a produzir em 2014 e possui um dos depósitos de vanádio de maior teor do mundo. A operação é realizada a céu aberto e produz principalmente pentóxido de vanádio, composto utilizado na fabricação de ligas metálicas de alta resistência e como matéria-prima para outras aplicações industriais e energéticas. A importância estratégica do mineral também levou a Largo a ampliar sua atuação no mercado de defesa dos Estados Unidos. Em junho, a companhia foi selecionada para fornecer pentóxido de vanádio de alta pureza à DLA (Agência de Logística de Defesa dos Estados Unidos), responsável, entre outras atribuições, pela aquisição e formação de estoques de materiais estratégicos para o país. O contrato integra um programa de compras compartilhado com valor máximo de US$ 125 milhões e duração de cinco anos. Em julho, a Largo recebeu uma primeira encomenda de US$ 60,1 milhões, com entregas previstas até janeiro de 2030. O material produzido na Bahia será destinado aos estoques estratégicos americanos e poderá atender às necessidades da indústria de defesa, incluindo a fabricação de ligas metálicas utilizadas em equipamentos militares e aeronáuticos. Para Arias, o movimento reflete o interesse de países ocidentais em reduzir a dependência de fornecedores como China e Rússia em cadeias de minerais considerados críticos e estratégicos. O executivo defendeu que o vanádio receba maior atenção das políticas de minerais críticos, diante de suas aplicações na indústria de defesa, no setor aeroespacial e nas tecnologias de armazenamento de energia. Produção de cobre e expansão na Bahia Além do vanádio, a Largo começou a diversificar sua produção mineral na Bahia. Em agosto, a companhia iniciou a recuperação de concentrado de cobre associado a metais preciosos, após receber autorização da ANM (Agência Nacional de Mineração). O novo produto é obtido a partir do processamento de materiais da própria operação de Maracás Menchen e contém, além de cobre, elementos como ouro, platina, paládio e prata. Na prática, a mineradora passou a aproveitar outros minerais presentes no material extraído para produzir um concentrado comercializável, utilizando parte das instalações que já existiam na mina. Com a expansão das aplicações do vanádio e a diversificação para o cobre e metais preciosos, a Largo busca aumentar a rentabilidade de sua operação brasileira e aproveitar a demanda internacional por matérias-primas estratégicas.

artigo.texto: Ten Reputable Solar Energy Storage Battery Manufacturers in China 2026: Advancing Clean Energy Storage Press Release Date 10-20-2026 A 2026 guide to ten reputable Chinese manufacturers of solar energy storage batteries. CALIFORNIA, CA, UNITED STATES, October 20, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- SHENZHEN, China, October 21, 2026 — Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd., a lithium battery pack manufacturer based in Bao'an District, Shenzhen and trading as HCC, heads a ten-company editorial list of Chinese solar energy storage battery manufacturers published today. The list places the company alongside nine further Chinese battery producers whose storage products are sold in domestic and export markets. The review assesses companies on four criteria that are observable from public information: breadth of in-house research and engineering, certification coverage relevant to export markets, manufacturing footprint, and the range of storage applications served. It is an editorial assessment compiled from company information and third-party market data. It is not a third-party ranking, and no company paid for inclusion. The list is published as demand for battery energy storage systems expands. Grand View Research estimated the global Battery Energy Storage System market at approximately USD 13.2 billion in 2025, with a projected value of USD 99.7 billion by 2033, and reported that lithium-ion batteries accounted for 53.5% of the segment in 2025. Industry context: demand growth and tightening standards Storage demand is being shaped by two forces at once. The first is volume: utility, commercial and residential installations all require cell and pack supply, and the same cell chemistries now compete across all three. The second is standardisation, which changes what qualifies as a credible supplier. Three documents anchor the compliance side of the market. IEC 62619:2022 is the current international safety standard for lithium-ion batteries in industrial and stationary applications, and covers thermal runaway behaviour and battery management system verification. UL 1973 is the primary North American safety standard for batteries in stationary applications such as solar energy storage and uninterruptible power supplies. UN 38.3 governs the transport of lithium batteries globally and requires eight specific tests, including altitude simulation and thermal testing. Segment demand is uneven. Mordor Intelligence and Strategic Market Research estimated the global golf cart battery market at USD 1.49 billion in 2024, with lithium-ion types capturing a 47.18% share — a reminder that storage chemistries are displacing lead-acid in motive applications at the same time as they scale in stationary ones. How the ten companies were assessed The four criteria were applied consistently across all ten companies, and each company is described only on the basis of publicly stated business scope. The criteria are: Technical research and engineering. Whether a company operates its own development capability for cells, modules or packs, and whether that capability extends to custom configurations rather than catalogue-only products. Certification coverage. Whether products are documented against RoHS, CE, UL or equivalent schemes, since these determine access to European and North American channels. Manufacturing footprint. Plant area, headcount and production arrangements, used as an indicator of how much of the value chain a supplier controls directly. Application and solution breadth. The range of use cases served, from residential wall-mounted systems to golf cart traction packs, industrial backup and commercial peak-shaving configurations. No single criterion decides placement. Companies with large cell output but limited pack-level customisation are not treated as equivalent to companies that design and assemble complete packs for specific applications. The ten manufacturers 1. Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd. (HCC) Founded in 2022, Shenzhen Topway New Energy operates from a 10,000 m² facility in Bao'an District, Shenzhen, with 200 employees and a 15-person R&D team, and states an export ratio of 40% across markets including the United States, Germany, Italy, Poland, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam and Australia. Its storage range covers the Wall-TW01 5 kW wall-mounted battery, built on LiFePO4 cells rated for at least 6,000 cycles at 80% capacity with a maximum continuous discharge current of 50 A; a 48 V 280 Ah solar battery pack rated at 200 A continuous discharge; a 51.2 V 200 Ah unit; 51.2 V 100 Ah and 48 V 100 Ah models; and 25.6 V 100 Ah and 12.8 V 100 Ah units. A 51.2 V 105 Ah pack serves golf cart traction. Products carry RoHS, UL and CE certification. Its position on the list reflects the depth of its cell engineering and its role as a cell supplier to system integrators, which places its products inside a large share of finished storage installations rather than only in direct-sale configurations. 3. artigo.texto: Meta gives tour of Huntsville data center amid questions over energy, water use HUNTSVILLE, Ala. (WAFF) - Meta opened its Huntsville data center for a tour, highlighting the facility’s role in powering some of the company’s most widely used platforms as questions about data centers’ energy and water usage continue to draw attention nationwide. Meta’s Huntsville data center stores information used by platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, and supports the company’s AI applications. Henry Thornton, with Meta, said the center matches its electricity use with clean and renewable energy. When asked how much electricity the Huntsville facility uses, Thornton did not provide a specific figure. “Our electricity usage is something we don’t disclose at the exact megawatt level for our sub gigawatt facilities, but we match every megawatt we use with clean and renewable energy,” Thornton said. Thornton said the facility receives its power through the Tennessee Valley Authority. “What I’d say is that a Meta data center is not going to raise your electricity bill. We are responsible users of water,” Thornton said. He said the facility’s water comes from Huntsville Utilities. The company has pledged to become water-positive by 2030, but it did not provide specific water-use figures for the Huntsville facility. “People often have a very misconstrued idea about data centers and water usage. We, you know, really don’t use that much more than other industrial facilities or, you know, perhaps a golf course or something like that,” Thornton said. Meta leaders said they consider themselves active members of the Huntsville community and said the company has donated millions of dollars to Madison County initiatives. Meta is scheduled to give a presentation on the Huntsville facility at the Dec. 3 Huntsville City Council meeting. artigo.texto: A Greenvolt celebrou um acordo para a venda de dois projetos de armazenamento de energia em baterias na Polónia, à sociedade A&R Investments, por 391,5 milhões de euros, segundo um comunicado ao mercado. Na nota, divulgada pela Comissão do Mercado de Valores Mobiliários (CMVM), a empresa informou que a sua subsidiária Greenvolt Power "celebrou um acordo para a venda de dois projetos de armazenamento de energia em baterias na Polónia, com uma potência total de 400 MW [megawatts] e uma capacidade de armazenamento total de 1,6 GWh [gigawatts/hora], à A&R Investments, um veículo de investimento sediado em Malta". De acordo com o comunicado, o valor da operação ascende a 391,5 milhões de euros, dos quais 311,5 milhões de euros correspondem a um valor fixo e até 80 milhões de euros a um pagamento adicional, "cujo montante dependerá do momento em que os projetos obtenham a autorização para prestar serviços de equilíbrio à rede elétrica". Segundo a empresa, "os projetos Ełk e Turośń Kościelna, situados no nordeste da Polónia, já se encontram construídos e têm, cada um, 200 MW de potência e 800 MWh de capacidade de armazenamento". A Greenvolt indicou ainda que estes projetos "têm receitas contratadas a longo prazo, através de contratos de 17 anos no mercado de capacidade polaco, a partir de 2028, e de um contrato com a Statkraft" para gestão das baterias e "venda da sua flexibilidade nos mercados de eletricidade". A empresa referiu que a conclusão da operação está prevista até ao final de 2026, sujeita à verificação das condições habituais. "Esta venda enquadra-se na estratégia de rotação de ativos da Greenvolt, que consiste em vender integralmente a maioria dos projetos que desenvolve, realizando o valor criado e reinvestindo o capital em novos projetos, e em manter os restantes projetos detidos a 100%", rematou. artigo.texto: Os Estados Unidos fecharam nesta terça-feira (21) uma parceria entre a americana Crusoe e a paraguaia Araico para construir um data center abastecido por energia da usina de Itaipu, na fronteira entre Brasil e Paraguai. O Brasil não foi citado no anúncio. O acordo foi firmado entre a Crusoe, que desenvolve infraestrutura de computação de alto desempenho, e a Araico, desenvolvedora paraguaia de projetos de energia. Segundo o Departamento de Estado dos EUA, a 1ª fase da instalação deve entrar em operação em meados de 2027. O anúncio aconteceu durante visita do vice-secretário de Estado americano, Christopher Landau, ao Paraguai. A viagem foi entre segunda (19) e quarta (21). Landau se reuniu com o presidente Santiago Peña e com o chanceler Rubén Ramírez Lezcano. O interesse americano não é novo. Em maio de 2025, o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, já defendia esse tipo de parceria no Senado dos EUA. "Temos que discutir como investiremos em países que têm um suprimento de energia capaz de atender a essa demanda. Como, por exemplo, o Paraguai", disse Rubio à Comissão de Relações Exteriores do Senado americano. Por que o Brasil não participa do acordo? O Brasil ficou de fora porque, desde 1973, o Tratado de Itaipu reservava ao país a exclusividade sobre o excedente de energia não consumido pelo Paraguai. Um acordo de 2025 revisou essa regra e autorizou os paraguaios a vender energia diretamente a terceiros. A energia de Itaipu é dividida meio a meio entre os dois países, mas o Paraguai usa só parte da própria cota. O consumo interno paraguaio passou de 10% em 2012 para mais de 30% em 2024. Publicidade Na prática, a decisão sobre o excedente deixou de depender de negociação bilateral com o Brasil. O restante do excedente agora pode ir a clientes como a Crusoe. Enquanto isso, o Brasil vive expansão própria de data centers, com projetos que também miram energia barata e abundante. O tema virou consenso entre os presidenciáveis na eleição deste ano, que defendem atrair mais investimento do setor para o país. A relação entre Brasil e Paraguai já vinha de atrito. Em julho, o país vizinho entregou nota de repúdio ao embaixador brasileiro por causa de uma fala do presidente Lula sobre a Guerra do Paraguai. Reportagens do setor elétrico apontam que autoridades brasileiras já tratam o fim dessa exclusividade como risco. O temor é perder previsibilidade no fornecimento e poder de barganha regional diante do Paraguai. O que acontece agora A primeira fase da instalação movida a Itaipu deve entrar em operação em meados de 2027, segundo o Departamento de Estado dos EUA. O comunicado americano não revelou o valor do investimento nem o volume de energia contratado. O acordo é parte de uma ofensiva maior dos EUA no Paraguai. A americana Uranium Energy Corp. também anunciou investimento de US$ 12 milhões numa concessão de urânio, e os dois países assinaram acordo de assistência para interceptação aérea.

artigo.texto: Lexington council unanimously restricts data center zoning Council votes to remove data centers from six zones, asks for new stand-alone zone LEXINGTON, Ky. — Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council members voted unanimously Thursday to remove data centers as a primary use in six zones, blocking the possibility of new centers there. Council also voted to ask the Planning Commission for a stand-alone data center zone. Council member calls vote a win Council member Emma Curtis, who backed both items, called the outcome a win. “Tonight’s victory is not just something that belongs to myself of council member Morton, but something that belongs to the entire community who have consistently come out and made their voices heard on this issue,” Curtis said. No land currently zoned for data centers Curtis said no existing land will be zoned for data center use under the proposed new zone. “There is no land in Lexington that is designated for any data center usage, and anybody who wants to develop a data center would have to go through the process of a zone change which would go before the planning commission and then ultimately before the council to have final say,” Curtis said. Definition of data center has changed In documents, council members point to the meaning of the term “data center” changing from when the zoning rules were first written. Curtis said she looks forward to working with the Planning Commission to update the regulations to match the current definition. “I’m really looking forward to creating a more collaborative and transparent process going forward that centers on the voices of Lexingtonians and not the voices of these predatory out of state corporations seeking to exploit us,” Curtis said. With the moratorium extension in effect, the county now has another year to further refine what the future of data centers looks like. artigo.texto: Venture Global lays plans for data centers next to LNG sites in Cameron, Plaquemines Cameron Parish officials say company did not discuss plans with them CAMERON, La. (KPLC) - Venture Global is expanding power at its South Louisiana LNG sites, which would pave the way for adjacent data centers, the company announced in a news release. Venture Global has LNG export terminals in Cameron and Plaquemines parishes and already runs on-site private power grids. The Virginia-based company is working with two energy technology companies to add power to these sites — enough to potentially run AI data centers. Cameron Parish officials told 7News they were not aware of this development until the public announcement was made. Mark Daigle, who represents District 5 on the Cameron Parish Police Jury, said he first learned of the plans through a social media post. “I actually saw it last night right before I went to bed,” Daigle said. As an elected official, Daigle said he expected to hear about a potential development of this scale before the public did. He reached out to other parish leaders to see if they had been told. “I actually reached out to the president and vice president. They did not hear about it,” Daigle said. Daigle said that lack of communication creates a larger problem for public trust in local government. “And when we start getting calls as elected officials from our constituents, and we tell them we found out like them, I think they lose a lot of hope in us as elected officials to do what’s right for them,” he said. Daigle said he is not opposed to the investment; he just wants the parish included in the conversation going forward. “I would have liked to see them talk with us and discuss to where we’re not finding out with the people, to where we could have told them our possible, if any, issues or maybe shortfalls that they might have,” Daigle said. Venture Global’s Calcasieu Pass LNG facility is directly south of the community of Cameron, and Calcasieu Pass 2 is under construction adjacent to it. RELATED COVERAGE: - Police jurors deny tax reduction requests from Phillips 66, Venture Global - Lawsuits on hold after federal court handles claims related to 2025 dredging spill - Federal court rejects petition against Cameron LNG facility - Cameron residents raise concerns over Venture Global construction dust The company has not confirmed a deal for an actual data center. In effect, the announcement serves as a pitch to future developers, touting Venture Global’s existing power grid and water supply as a built-in advantage for siting a data center at its Louisiana sites. The company said power would be generated on-site with closed-loop water, placing no demand on the public grid and water. Therefore, it would create no additional cost for consumers. Venture Global signed an agreement with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes to potentially develop up to 16 new 720-megawatt power island units by the end of 2034. The company’s sites already produce 4.5 gigawatts of gas-fired generation to power its LNG facilities, and it plans to develop up to 10 gigawatts of compute capacity to power potential data centers. The company expects to build the additional capacity in stages based on customer demand and will begin purchasing equipment for the expansion by the end of 2026. The new power island units would include combined cycle gas turbines. In a statement to 7News, a Venture Global representative said the agreement with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes “simply reserves the right” to purchase future power equipment for the company’s LNG business and potential future data center development. The representative said any future expansion “would of course be coordinated with state and local officials” and, like the company’s current operations, would have no reliance on the public grid or water utilities — and therefore no added cost for consumers in Cameron Parish or surrounding areas. Venture Global said it planned to file its first permit applications for the project last week. The company said expansion is separate from and will not impact its LNG operations, which remain its key objective. Venture Global’s full statement: You can also read the press release here. artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. BYD Brings Flash Charging to Indonesia with New DENZA Models BYD introduced its second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology in Indonesia, marking the technology's overseas debut. The announcement coincided with the launch of two new DENZA models, the D9 and the Z9GT, as BYD expands its electric vehicle lineup and charging services in the Southeast Asian market. According to BYD, its Flash Charging technology can charge a battery from 10% to 70% in as little as five minutes, and from 10% to 97% in nine minutes under normal conditions. The system integrates energy storage with charging equipment and features a lightweight charging connector designed to make plugging in easier, as well as a plug-and-charge function. To support the rollout, BYD plans to install Flash Charging equipment at 10 DENZA dealerships in Indonesia in the initial phase. The stations will be open to the public, providing an initial charging network before the company expands coverage further. The new DENZA D9 comes equipped with the second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology, alongside upgrades to powertrain performance, driving range and comfort. The Z9GT, meanwhile, is built on BYD's e³ platform, extending the brand's premium electric vehicle offering in Indonesia. Huawei-Backed Yinwang Teams Up with CATL on Automated Battery Swapping Yinwang Intelligent Technology, a Huawei-affiliated smart vehicle company, has signed a strategic cooperation agreement with CATL and its battery-swapping subsidiary, Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology, to develop an intelligent battery-swapping ecosystem for autonomous vehicles. The agreement was signed on October 19 and covers vehicle integration, swappable batteries and network development. The three companies plan to connect vehicles, battery-swapping stations and cloud systems, using real-time battery data and drivers' travel patterns to predict energy needs and coordinate services. The proposed system would allow vehicles to determine when a battery swap is needed, locate a station, enter and align automatically, complete the swap in just 99 seconds, and drive away without human intervention. The partnership brings Yinwang into CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem. The companies will adapt participating vehicle models to work with the network, with the aim of expanding access to battery-swapping services for vehicles equipped with Huawei's Qiankun intelligent automotive solutions. CATL's Choco-Swap network had 2,520 stations across 200 Chinese cities as of September 29. The company plans to expand the network to 30,000 stations and connect urban and highway coverage, although the announcement did not specify a timeline for reaching that target. The deal highlights how Chinese companies are working to integrate automated driving with energy replenishment. By linking vehicle intelligence, cloud-based service coordination and battery-swapping infrastructure, the partners aim to make battery replacement faster and more convenient while extending the service network available to intelligent vehicles. Schaeffler Opens Humanoid Robot Factory in China Schaeffler opened a humanoid robotics factory in Taicang, Jiangsu province, on October 20, bringing robot-component manufacturing, robot training and industrial applications together under one roof. Spanning approximately 7,500 square meters, the facility is designed to help move humanoid robots from experimental projects into real-world manufacturing. Six humanoid robots are already working on an assembly line producing joint modules for other humanoid robots. Across five workstations, they handle tasks including material handling, parts sorting, press-fitting, inspection and packaging. The setup marks a step toward a closed manufacturing loop in which humanoid robots help produce components for the next generation of robots. The factory also includes dedicated training environments for industrial tasks such as visual inspection, material picking and component assembly. A digital-twin system connects robot training with production validation and process optimization, allowing Schaeffler to test and refine processes virtually before implementing changes on the actual production line. The opening comes as Schaeffler expands its humanoid robotics business in China. The company said it secured orders from two new Chinese customers in the third quarter of 2026, bringing its cumulative global order intake in humanoid robotics to approximately €400 million. The Taicang facility will also serve as a platform for collaboration with Chinese robotics companies.

artigo.texto: The 13-member Lancaster County Data Center Task Force met for the first time Tuesday to set expectations and goals for its six scheduled meetings, during which members will study data center regulations and develop recommendations for the Lancaster County Board. The group will govern the development of data centers in rural Lancaster County. “I cannot express my gratitude for you taking on this assignment,” Lancaster County Commissioner Christa Yoakum said. “This is going to take up a chunk of your lives from now until the end of the year, when we hope that you’re able to have a recommendation, or some recommendations to bring forward to us.” The County Board nixed a potential 12-month data center moratorium in favor of the task force. Currently, at least four cities — Lincoln, Omaha, Kearney and Papillion — and eight counties — including Cass, Gage and Seward — have moratoriums on data centers. As part of the inaugural meeting — which was led by David Cary, director of Lincoln-Lancaster County Planning and Development Services, who is not a member of the task force — each of the 12 members present was asked to share their goals, which included making policy, supporting the community and setting baselines. “I want to protect public health safety and welfare,” said John Hansen, president of the Nebraska Farmers Union. “But I also want to come up with a balanced set of rules and regulations.” The task force also laid groundwork for the months ahead, including going over county and zoning regulations. Currently, there are no data centers in rural Lancaster County. However, two companies have bought land for potential centers — though Cary said the county has not had any discussions yet about either. West of Hallam, Sagebrush Infrastructure Partners, which builds hyperscale data centers and natural gas-fired power plants, entered into the agreements for about 1,700 acres of land valued at about $10.35 million, according to documents from the Lancaster County Assessor’s Office. The purchase agreements — involving at least 11 landowners and 21 parcels of land — were signed between December and March, according to the assessor's office. These agreements give Sagebrush an exclusivity period ranging between 2½ and four years into the future to purchase the land at an agreed-upon price. A representative for Stark Power, the Israeli-owned company that acquired Sagebrush in June, said the company is exploring the possibility of developing a data center in the area, though no final decision has been made. The project could be a 1.7-gigawatt hyperscale campus, enough to power 1.3 million homes. And just outside of Lincoln, Coffee Grounds Data LLC, registered in Delaware, agreed to a purchase agreement for about 560 acres worth $3.46 million with landowner Larry Coffey in September, according to property records. The land sits off U.S. 34 and Nebraska 79 less than five miles east of Malcolm. Signing the deal for the data company was Ricardo Graf, chief development officer and managing partner at Arevia Power, a San Francisco-based company known for its solar power projects. More recently, the company, through subsidiary Rhea Data, has delved into data centers, proposing a 600-megawatt facility on public land in Idaho, which could be the state’s largest. Graf and Arevia were also connected to a project in Adair, Okla., a town about 45 minutes northeast of Tulsa. Two community members who live by the potential Arevia data center spoke during the task force’s public hearing. Nate Tederman, who lives in Malcolm, said he was unhappy with his community’s lack of representation. “Our voices aren’t getting heard. We’re the community out there,” he said. “I couldn’t be more against it.” On the other hand, Adam Hohbein, whose land neighbors where the potential data center could be, said he was not fully opposed to the project, but hoped the task force weighed it carefully. “I really want to make sure that we’re taking into consideration the people that are existing residents,” he said. “I just want to make sure that we’re being diligent about how we’re going about this process and what kind of regulations we set on them.” The task force will meet again Nov. 3. Its final meeting is expected to be on Jan. 5, though its timeline could be extended if necessary. Another data center task force, put together by Gov. Jim Pillen and overseen by the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy and Environment, held its second meeting in Columbus on Tuesday. Made up of 19 members including the CEOs of Lincoln Electric System, the Nebraska Public Power District and the Omaha Public Power District, Pillen’s task force is expected to meet again in Lincoln on Nov. 19. © 2026 Lincoln Journal Star, Neb. artigo.texto: Yasin Gungor 21 October 2026•Update: 21 October 2026 US President Donald Trump on Wednesday urged operators of large artificial intelligence data centers to strike financial agreements with local communities and pay them dividends to ease public backlash over rising energy costs. "If companies want to make their data centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a 'dividend,'" Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social, arguing that projects facing fierce local opposition quickly gain acceptance once direct economic pacts are reached. Trump said facilities must produce their own power rather than draining public utilities. He maintained that new and large data centers are required to "make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," asserting that such measures would prevent utility inflation and potentially yield "a substantial decrease" in electricity rates. The US has more than 5,000 data centers, with facilities projected to expand roughly 9% annually through 2030, according to the US Department of Commerce. The directive comes amid escalating friction over power consumption driven by the artificial intelligence boom ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Public surveys show strong bipartisan opposition, with a Gallup poll finding 71% of Americans resisting local developments over concerns that facilities will inflate residential utility bills. The policy builds upon Trump's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge established in March, which called on technology firms to cover all power generation and transmission costs.

artigo.texto: GREEN CHARTER TOWNSHIP, Mich. (Michigan News Source) – After years of controversy, lawsuits and political battles, the proposed Gotion electric vehicle battery plant in Mecosta County is heading toward a legal conclusion. And the current price tag for settling one federal claim? One dollar. Township Approves Settlement The Green Charter Township Board of Trustees approved a proposed settlement agreement on Thursday, October 15 during a special meeting, potentially ending litigation involving Gotion Inc. and its controversial battery plant project. MORE NEWS: Trump Calls Slotkin a ‘Lowlife’ Over Remarks About Young Trump Administration Recruits According to the Big Rapids Pioneer, the agreement requires Gotion to transfer the proposed project property to the Michigan State Land Bank. The Michigan Strategic Fund would also drop its demand against Gotion involving grant funds. The township would refund certain project-related funds and remove some public statements concerning Gotion, the litigation, and economic development organization The Right Place. One Dollar and Done? Under the agreement, Gotion would receive a consent judgment on one federal claim with just $1 in damages. All remaining claims would be dismissed with prejudice, preventing them from being refiled. The parties would also terminate project agreements and release claims against one another related to the dispute. Township attorney Kyle O’Meara said the agreement follows negotiations culminating in an October 2 settlement conference before a federal magistrate judge. Although the township has approved the terms, final paperwork may still require additional board approval. MORE NEWS: Political Signs Spark Owosso Farmers Market Showdown; GOP Alleges Double Standard For residents who fought the controversial project, the proposed settlement signals that the long-running battle over the battery plant is finally moving toward a conclusion. Cella: Gotion Deal Was a Threat to National Security Joseph Cella, director and co-founder of the Michigan China Economic Security and Review Group, who has been a vocal opponent of the Gotion battery plant project, called the agreement between government officials and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)-linked company corrupt from the beginning. He said in a statement to Michigan News Source, “It moved fast and in secret and it ruptured the consent of the governed,” He accused officials of failing to conduct proper due diligence and ignoring national security concerns, describing the project as having “all of the textbook markings of a subnational incursion and influence operation by a CCP-tied entity.” Cella credited local residents for defeating the project, saying it would not have happened without the patriots of Mecosta County who “courageously stood up, exposed it, tenaciously fought it, and ultimately restored the consent of the governed.”

artigo.texto: Micro-resfriamento xMEMS Entra em Produção em Massa para Dispositivos de IA e Componentes de Data Centers A xMEMS anunciou em 20 de outubro a produção em massa de dois chips de micro-resfriamento, levando fluxo de ar ativo a dispositivos nos quais ventiladores convencionais têm dificuldade para caber. O anúncio de micro-resfriamento da xMEMS abrange óculos de IA, smartphones e determinados componentes de data centers. Sua importância está no posicionamento do resfriamento: mais próximo de pequenas fontes de calor, dentro de produtos com pouco espaço para hardware rotativo. O marco de produção precisa de algum contexto. A xMEMS já havia informado que seu menor XMC-2400 estava sendo enviado em julho. O anúncio de outubro abrange esse dispositivo junto ao maior XMC-4800 e amplia a mensagem comercial da empresa. Ele não estabelece que algum dos chips tenha aparecido em um produto de varejo publicamente identificado. A disputa subjacente é entre o resfriamento ativo direcionado e projetos que dependem principalmente da dissipação de calor por meio de um gabinete fino. A Frore Systems, cuja tecnologia AirJet já aparece em um mini PC ZOTAC, oferece uma referência comercial. Para fabricantes de dispositivos, a decisão envolve desempenho sustentado, consumo de bateria, espaço físico e conforto. Um componente de resfriamento precisa melhorar todo esse equilíbrio. O que muda com o anúncio de produção do micro-resfriamento xMEMS O anúncio disponibiliza dois componentes de resfriamento para integração comercial, enquanto a adoção em produtos finalizados permanece em grande parte não divulgada. Segundo o anúncio de produção em massa da empresa, o XMC-2400 é voltado a dispositivos compactos, incluindo óculos e armazenamento pessoal. O XMC-4800 é destinado a smartphones e subsistemas de data centers de menor consumo. Os primeiros produtos comerciais com o XMC-2400 são esperados para o início de 2027. Essas categorias descrevem diferentes problemas de integração. Os óculos precisam de resfriamento dentro de uma armação vestível. Os celulares precisam de controle térmico sem ceder espaço interno excessivo. O hardware de armazenamento precisa operar de forma consistente dentro de um gabinete ou sistema que restringe o fluxo de ar. Uma arquitetura de componente comum não torna esses requisitos de engenharia intercambiáveis. Para os fabricantes, o status de produção importa porque muda a conversa de planejamento. Um protótipo pode demonstrar que uma ideia merece investigação. Um componente em produção oferece a uma equipe de projeto algo mais concreto para avaliar em fornecimento, montagem, qualificação e suporte. Essas etapas ainda exigem evidências além do anúncio de um fornecedor. A cronologia também limita como o evento deve ser enquadrado. Em seu anúncio de produto de julho, a xMEMS disse que o XMC-2400 já estava sendo enviado e apoiava suas primeiras vitórias de projeto em óculos. Uma vitória de projeto significa a seleção para um projeto de cliente; ela não estabelece necessariamente disponibilidade no varejo. Portanto, outubro não deve ser descrito como a primeira divulgação de que o XMC-2400 havia chegado à produção. O desenvolvimento mais claro é o anúncio que abrange ambos os modelos em produção e seus mercados pretendidos. Essa distinção preserva o marco sem transformar uma declaração comercial atualizada em uma estreia técnica inteiramente nova. A mesma cautela se aplica à palavra “comercial”. Envios de componentes, qualificação de clientes, anúncios de dispositivos e disponibilidade para consumidores são eventos separados. Um fornecedor pode alcançar a produção enquanto seus clientes continuam refinando os produtos. Os leitores devem evitar tratar essas etapas como evidência da mesma coisa. Para potenciais compradores, a consequência imediata é uma relevância maior durante a avaliação de produtos, e não uma recomendação de compra imediata. Não há no anúncio um par de óculos ou smartphone identificado pelo nome para avaliar. A alegação de produção se torna mais útil quando vinculada a um dispositivo finalizado, uma carga de trabalho identificada e um resultado mensurável. É por isso que a próxima etapa importa para mais do que engenheiros térmicos. Gerentes de produto que decidem quais recursos permanecem locais precisam entender os limites operacionais do hardware. As equipes de software precisam saber se um dispositivo mantém seu comportamento depois de aquecer. Um componente de resfriamento em produção introduz outra opção de projeto nessas decisões. Dispositivos finos de IA colocam o desempenho sustentado à frente de breves demonstrações A aplicação mais forte é um dispositivo cujo tempo útil de operação é limitado pelo calor, e não pela capacidade de processamento anunciada. IA de borda significa executar inteligência artificial em um dispositivo local em vez de depender inteiramente de servidores remotos. Seus requisitos térmicos dependem da carga de trabalho real. Uma interação curta e uma tarefa prolongada baseada em câmera criam condições operacionais diferentes, mesmo quando usam o mesmo processador. Considere óculos que capturam vídeo continuamente enquanto realizam análise local. A experiência relevante inclui duração da gravação, temperatura da superfície, capacidade de resposta e uso da bateria. Um dispositivo que lida confortavelmente com uma demonstração breve pode se comportar de forma diferente durante uma sessão prolongada. O resfriamento merece atenção quando essas diferenças limitam o recurso pretendido. Isso pressiona os fabricantes de dispositivos, em vez de atingir diretamente uma empresa específica de processadores. As equipes de hardware precisam escolher quanto trabalho manter dentro do gabinete disponível. Suas respostas podem incluir reduzir a atividade de processamento, alterar o projeto físico, mover o trabalho para outro lugar ou adicionar capacidade térmica. A limitação térmica, a redução do desempenho operacional para controlar a temperatura, é uma distinção esp
